Title: Public Preview: Per-disk resiliency for Azure VMs

Body.Content:
Azure automatically recovers a VM when it loses access to an attached managed disk for an extended period. The VM is shut down and powered back on after disk connectivity is restored, with no customer action required. This remains the default behavior.

Now in public preview in select regions, per-disk resiliency provides another option for applications that can tolerate the temporary loss of an individual data disk. When enabled, Azure detaches and takes only the affected disk offline while the VM and its remaining disks continue running. Once disk connectivity is restored, Azure automatically attaches and brings the disk back online.

Use per-disk resiliency where a single data disk is not a single point of failure:
  1. Production VMs with backup or auxiliary disks, so a secondary disk issue does not interrupt the primary workload.
  2. Clustered and shared-disk applications with their own high-availability or failover logic.
  3. Containerized workloads with per-pod disks, so one persistent volume can recover without disrupting other pods on the node.
Per-disk resiliency is opt-in for each Azure Managed Disk. While a data disk is offline, I/Os to it returns errors, so the application must continue without that disk until access is restored. OS disks continue to use the default VM shut down recovery behavior.

Available now in public preview in select regions. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Multicloud Interconnect

Body.Content:
Announcing the public preview of Azure Multicloud Interconnect, a managed service that provides private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providers, with Amazon Web Services (AWS) available as the first supported provider in preview. 

As organizations increasingly distribute applications, data, AI services, and business-critical workloads across multiple clouds, establishing and operating cloud-to-cloud connectivity can become complex and operationally intensive. Azure Multicloud Interconnect helps simplify this experience by providing a managed connectivity solution that reduces deployment complexity while delivering resilient private, high-performance connectivity between Azure and supported cloud environments.

With Azure Multicloud Interconnect, you can deploy a multicloud connection directly from the Azure portal, select your cloud provider, region, and bandwidth, and onboard your environment through a guided experience. Once provisioned, you can connect Azure virtual networks and supported cloud-provider virtual networks through a private cloud-to-cloud connection, helping streamline operations and accelerate multicloud deployments.

Key highlights:

  • Managed private connectivity between Azure and supported cloud providers
  • Simplified deployment and onboarding
  • Built-in resiliency designed for mission-critical workloads

Learn more: 

  • Read the documentation 
  • Read the announcement blog

Title: Generally Available: Azure VM Image Builder in sovereign and air-gapped clouds

Title: Generally Available: eBPF host routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for AKS

Body.Content:
eBPF Host Routing in Advanced Container Networking Services for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is now generally available. 

eBPF Host Routing improves Kubernetes networking performance by moving packet forwarding and routing decisions directly into the Linux kernel using eBPF. This removes the overhead of iptables-based processing and reduces dependence on the host networking stack, resulting in lower latency, fewer network hops, and higher throughput for application traffic. For large-scale AKS deployments, eBPF Host Routing helps deliver more efficient network performance, improved scalability, and a better experience for latency-sensitive and high-traffic workloads. 

This release also introduces an enhanced enablement experience that respects existing network connections during rollout. When eBPF Host Routing is enabled on an existing cluster, AKS performs a controlled node rotation to transition nodes to the new networking mode, helping maintain connection continuity and minimize disruption to running applications.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Custom block response code and body for Application Gateway WAF

Body.Content:
Announcing the General Availability of custom block response code and body for WAF integrated with Application Gateway 

Azure WAF integrated with Application Gateway now supports customizable response status codes and bodies for blocked requests, enabling greater flexibility and control. 

By default, when the WAF blocks a request due to a matched rule, it returns a 403 status code with a "The request is blocked" message. As with WAF with Azure Front Door, now customers can also define a custom response status code and message with Application Gateway when WAF blocks a request. This customization is a policy-level setting, ensuring that all blocked requests receive the same custom response status and message. 

For further details, please reach out to the Azure WAF product team.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Summarized advertised gateway prefixes for route advertisement

Body.Content:
Summarized advertised gateway prefixes for route advertisement is now generally available. You can specify aggregated (summarized) prefixes for an Azure gateway to advertise to your on-premises networks, rather than having every individual virtual network address space advertised. The capability is supported on both ExpressRoute Gateway and VPN Gateway, and covers IPv4 and IPv6 address spaces.  

Large hub-and-spoke deployments often approach the advertised-prefix limits of ExpressRoute and VPN Gateway as spokes are added. Advertising a covering prefix such as 10.0.0.0/16 in place of hundreds of individual spoke prefixes keeps route counts well within those limits and lets you keep growing an environment without re-architecting the address plan or splitting virtual networks. Any spoke address space that falls outside the summarized prefix continues to be advertised on its own, so existing connectivity is preserved when you turn the feature on. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: vCore Customization: Disable Multithreading and Configurable Constrained Cores

Body.Content:
Today, we are announcing the General Availability of VM vCore Customization for Azure Virtual Machines, introducing two new capabilities: Disable Simultaneous Multi-Threading/Hyper-Threading (SMT/HT) and Configurable Constrained Cores. These features provide greater control over virtual CPU configurations, helping customers optimize performance while reducing software licensing costs.

With VM vCore Customization, customers can now disable SMT/HT on supported VMs to provide workloads exclusive access to physical cores for improved latency consistency and performance. Customers can also select from supported vCPU counts to align with software licensing requirements or workload demands without changing the VM's memory, storage, or network bandwidth.

By decoupling active core count from VM size, organizations can deploy larger-memory or higher-bandwidth VMs while activating only the vCores they need. This is especially valuable for licensed software workloads such as SQL Server, Oracle, and SAP, where licensing costs are tied to core count.

VM vCore Customization is now available in all Azure public regions and includes support for Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) Uniform orchestration mode. Customers can configure these capabilities through the Azure portal, ARM templates, Azure CLI, and PowerShell. Support is currently available for first-party Azure operating system images. Marketplace images that include third-party licensing are not supported.

Title: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution License-included service will be retired August 30, 2027

Body.Content:
In November last year, Broadcom changed its VMware licensing policies across all hyperscaler platforms to require customers to “bring your own” portable license for VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF).

What’s changing?

On August 30, 2027, as a result of the latest Broadcom VCF licensing change, the AVS license-included service will be retired.  Customers currently using license-included Reserved Instance (RI) SKUs will be required to purchase portable Broadcom VCF Licenses and transition to an AVS VCF BYOL SKU prior to August 30, 2027, to avoid service disruption on August 31, 2027.

Take Action Today:

Allow plenty of time to purchase VCF licenses from Broadcom and complete the transition to AVS VCF BYOL. For customers evaluating modernization opportunities, start assessing current AVS environments immediately, and develop a transition roadmap to ensure you have time to evaluate all options and avoid service disruption on August 31, 2027.

Contact your account team to plan your transition.

Key Dates and Transition Details:
  • August 30, 2027 Last Day of all AVS license-included services
  • AVS License-included RIs Microsoft allows for the exchange of Reservations with expiration dates beyond August 30, 2027
  • AVS License-included PayGo SKUs will retire on October 31, 2026
  • UPDATE AV36 SKU Retirement is now August 30, 2027
Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Managed Instance on Azure App Service

Body.Content:
Managed Instance on Azure App Service is now generally available. 

Managed Instance helps organizations migrate web applications to Azure App Service with minimal configuration and no code changes. Applications running on-premises or in virtual machines can move to a fully managed PaaS environment while maintaining compatibility with Windows-specific dependencies.

Many business-critical .NET applications rely on Windows services, third-party libraries, custom runtimes, and other components that can make modernization challenging. Managed Instance enables these applications to run on Azure App Service while preserving compatibility and reducing operational overhead.

Key benefits include:

  • Built-in App Service capabilities such as autoscale, resiliency, zone redundancy, and Azure service integration.
  • Administrative control through Azure Bastion-enabled RDP access, custom scripts, registry adapters, storage mounts, and identity management.
  • Support for complex workloads, including classic .NET Framework applications, without code changes.
  • Enterprise-ready capabilities, including a 99.95% SLA, Premium v4 performance, Azure Policy integration, Microsoft Defender for Cloud support, and deployment through Bicep, Terraform, and ARM templates.

Get started by assessing eligible workloads with Azure Migrate and deploying through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, or infrastructure-as-code tools.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Pre-upgrade validation checks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

Body.Content:
Pre-upgrade validation checks are now generally available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server, helping you proactively validate major version upgrade (MVU) readiness before initiating the actual upgrade process. With the general availability of this update, you can now run these checks from both the Azure portal and Azure CLI using the new --validate-only option. 

With pre-upgrade validation checks, you can independently run upgrade compatibility validations and identify potential blockers ahead of time, helping reduce failed upgrade attempts and improve operational predictability. The validation process checks your server against Azure PostgreSQL upgrade policies and PostgreSQL pg_upgrade --check compatibility requirements, surfacing actionable guidance for issues such as unsupported extensions, replication slots, prepared transactions, configuration mismatches, and other upgrade constraints. 

By shifting validation from inline execution during upgrade to a proactive pre-flight step, this capability helps improve first-time upgrade success rates, reduce troubleshooting effort, and simplify upgrade planning for production workloads. You can resolve identified issues, rerun validations as needed, and proceed with the upgrade only when your environment is ready. 

Learn more.

Title: Retirement: Containerized data connector agent for the Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications

Body.Content:
On September 14, 2026 we will retire the containerized data connector agent for the Microsoft Sentinel solution for SAP applications. After this date the agent will be permanently disabled and will stop sending SAP logs to Microsoft Sentinel.

The SAP agentless data connector is generally available and is the replacement. Creation of new containerized agents is already disabled.

How this affects you:
If you use the containerized agent, SAP log collection through it stops on 14 September 2026. Analytics rules, workbooks, hunting queries and playbooks that rely on this data will stop returning results for the affected SAP systems. Customers already using the agentless connector are not affected. There is no change to pricing or billing meters.

What you need to do:
Migrate to the SAP agentless data connector before September 14, 2026. Migration runs side-by-side with no gap in coverage: deploy the agentless connector alongside your existing agent, validate log ingestion, then decommission the agent. Your existing analytics rules, workbooks and playbooks keep working throughout.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Batch rule updates for Azure Front Door

Body.Content:
Batch rule updates are now generally available for Azure Front Door Standard and Premium. This capability enables customers to add, update, delete, or reorder multiple rules in a rule set as a coordinated operation, ensuring that all changes are applied together or not applied at all. 

Batch rule updates improve deployment safety and predictability for customers managing large or complex rule sets through Terraform and other Infrastructure-as-Code workflows. They help prevent partial rule states, rule-order conflicts, deployment retries, and rollback complexity that can occur when related rules are updated individually. 

Customers explicitly enable batch mode when creating a new rule set and submit the complete desired rule configuration. Azure Front Door then applies the changes together at the rule-set level. Existing rule sets continue to use classic rule management by default, preserving full backward compatibility. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Front Door mutual TLS

Body.Content:
Mutual TLS, also known as client certificate authentication, enables Azure Front Door to authenticate clients using X.509 certificates before requests reach an application. It helps protect sensitive applications and APIs across business-to-business, Internet of Things, financial services, VPN, and enterprise network scenarios.  

Customers can choose from four client certificate validation modes: 

  • Require and validate: A client certificate is mandatory. Azure Front Door validates the certificate at the edge and forwards it to the origin in the X-Azure-ClientCertificate request header. 
  • Require without validation: A client certificate is mandatory, but Azure Front Door does not validate it. The certificate is forwarded in the X-Azure-ClientCertificate header for validation by the origin. 
  • Validate when presented: A client certificate is optional. When a certificate is presented, Azure Front Door validates it and forwards it to the origin. Requests without a certificate are allowed to continue. 
  • Pass through to the origin: A client certificate is optional. Azure Front Door does not validate it but forwards it to the origin when presented, allowing the origin to perform validation.  

Azure Front Door supports client certificates issued by public and private certificate authorities. Customers upload the trusted certificate authority chain to Azure Key Vault and associate it with a Front Door custom domain. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard

Body.Content:
Azure ExpressRoute resiliency guard is now available in public preview for ExpressRoute virtual network gateways. The new resiliency model property lets you specify whether a gateway is intended for a single-homed or multi-homed configuration, helping align your deployment with the resiliency requirements of your workloads.

For multi-homed gateways, resiliency guard guides you to connect either two ExpressRoute circuits in different peering locations or an ExpressRoute Metro circuit. Portal guidance and configuration safeguards help identify incomplete setups and reduce the risk of changes that could weaken gateway resiliency. Single-homed configurations remain available for workloads that do not require multi-site resiliency. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Explicit proxy in Azure Firewall

Body.Content:
Azure Firewall explicit proxy is now generally available. Explicit proxy enables customers to configure applications and browsers to send HTTP and HTTPS traffic directly to Azure Firewall using proxy settings, providing an alternative to route-based traffic steering and enabling more granular control over outbound web traffic. 

The GA release builds on extensive customer validation during public preview, where explicit proxy was enabled across 300+ Azure subscriptions and adopted by approximately 40 S500 customers. Customer feedback gathered during preview directly influenced several key enhancements delivered as part of GA, including support for serving both HTTP and HTTPS destinations through a single proxy endpoint, Managed Identity-based PAC file retrieval, and an improved portal configuration experience. 

A key customer use case for explicit proxy is Azure Arc onboarding in hybrid environments. Organizations can use Azure Firewall as a forward proxy for Arc-enabled servers, enabling secure connectivity to required Microsoft services while maintaining centralized outbound access controls. Combined with support for forward proxy migration scenarios and application-level traffic steering, Explicit Proxy helps customers simplify network operations while leveraging Azure Firewall's existing security capabilities. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Route-Maps for Azure Route Server

Body.Content:

Route-maps provide the following capabilities: 

  • Route summarization: Summarize routes when on-premises networks connect to the virtual network through ExpressRoute or VPN. 
  • Route control: Control routes entering and leaving Azure Route Server between on-premises networks, NVAs, and virtual networks. 
  • Path selection: Modify BGP attributes such as AS-PATH to make routes more or less preferred. 
  • Route tagging: Tag routes by using the BGP Community attribute. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: Reservation exchanges for Azure services supported by savings plans will no longer be available starting February 1, 2027

Body.Content:
Starting February 1, 2027, Azure reservations exchanges will no longer be available for services covered by savings plans.  At the time of this announcement, this includes reservations for the following services:    

  • Compute services: Azure Virtual Machines, including exchanges between non-premium and premium storage, Azure Dedicated Host, and Azure App Service. 

  • Database services: Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Database for MySQL, Azure DocumentDB, Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Database, and Azure SQL Managed Instance.  

Each active reservation for impacted services purchased before February 1, 2027, will retain the right to one final exchange after that date.  

This reservation exchange policy update excludes products or services that are deprecated and approaching end of life, as well as cloud environments that don’t currently support savings plans. 

As savings plans coverage expands, reservations for those services will follow this policy and will not support exchanges. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium

Body.Content:
We’re announcing post-quantum resilient symmetric keys on Azure Key Vault Premium are now available in public preview. 

This preview enables customers and partners to evaluate symmetric encryption capabilities using the oct-HSM key type and the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) algorithm directly within Azure Key Vault. Customers can use AES algorithms to encrypt, decrypt, wrap, and unwrap data while continuing to benefit from Azure-managed security, compliance, and operational controls. 

AES algorithms with 256-bit keys are aligned with CNSA 2.0 requirements and can help organizations prepare for post-quantum cryptography readiness scenarios. 

Key benefits include: 

  • Centralized key management through Azure Key Vault Premium 
  • Support for oct-HSM symmetric keys 
  • AES-based encryption and decryption operations 
  • Simplified integration with existing Azure security workflows 
  • Consistent security and operational controls across Azure services 

Note: Azure portal support for symmetric key management is currently rolling out. During the rollout period, customers can use Azure CLI, ARM templates to create and manage oct-HSM symmetric keys and access the full preview functionality. 

Learn more:

  • About keys  
  • Key types, algorithms, and operations

Title: Public Preview: Support for SMB Opportunistic Locking (Oplocks) configuration

Body.Content:
Azure NetApp Files now supports configuration of SMB opportunistic locking (oplocks) for SMB and dual-protocol volumes. Opportunistic locks (Oplocks) improve SMB client caching and are enabled by default. You can configure oplocks on new volumes or update the setting on existing volumes. System default is the default selection and enables opportunistic locks on the volume. A cross-region replication destination volume can use an oplock setting independent of its source volume.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available for evaluation

Body.Content:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 RC1 is now available for evaluation in the Retail Eval feed. Whilst this release encompasses no customer-facing changes, it represents a major bump in Azure Sphere's underlying Linux kernel version as part of our long-term support and security commitment, as such, this release will operate for an extended evaluation period, until September 2026, enabling additional time for customer evaluation testing.

Whilst we've taken every measure to ensure that this update does not impact any of our contractual surfaces, with over six months of extensive integration and regression testing, we strongly encourage customers to evaluate this release with their in-market applications and to raise any issues with the Azure Sphere product group as early on as possible.

Following this evaluation period, 26.09 will be promoted and deployed broadly to devices in the Retail feed.

The 26.09 RC1 OS Retail Eval release includes a major Linux kernel version bump.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Enclave

Body.Content:
Announcing the public preview of Azure Enclave for Microsoft Azure, Azure Government, Azure Government Secret, and Azure Government Top Secret. Azure Enclave helps streamline the deployment and management of isolated cloud environments for sensitive workloads across government and other regulated industries. Azure Enclave helps customers quickly deliver their critical workloads while maintaining essential security and isolation. Azure Enclave is designed to isolate virtual networking infrastructure by default and includes controls intended to help ensure connections are explicitly configured and managed. 

With Azure Enclave, customers can: 

  • Quickly deploy secured environments using managed infrastructure and predefined architectural patterns. 
  • Provide access to authorized users in shared environments with controlled data access policies and defined permissions. 
  • Configure secured connections to sensitive data using endpoints you define and control for connectivity between resources. 
  • Apply multiple security controls, including network segmentation, role-based access, and monitoring, to help protect workloads and simplify management. 
Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: NAT64 on StandardV2 NAT Gateway

Body.Content:
StandardV2 NAT Gateway now supports NAT64, enabling IPv6 workloads to communicate with IPv4-only internet destinations by translating synthesized outbound IPv6 traffic into IPv4 traffic. NAT64 relies on a DNS64-capable resolver to synthesize IPv6 addresses by embedding the IPv4 address within the NAT64 Well-Known Prefix 64:ff9b::/96 – so client traffic is naturally addressed to NAT64 for translation.

Title: Generally Available: Application Routing with Gateway API

Body.Content:
Managing ingress routing while adopting newer Kubernetes standards can require balancing modernization efforts with existing deployments. Application Routing with Gateway API is now generally available on AKS, bringing the Kubernetes Gateway API to ingress management without requiring a service mesh. 

Existing ingress-nginx-based Application Routing remains supported until November, and customers can migrate to the Gateway API-based model at their own pace using the open-source ingress2gateway tool. This enables technical practitioners to adopt a standardized routing model while maintaining a lightweight footprint and supporting a gradual transition from existing ingress configurations.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Maximum allowed failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager

Body.Content:
In fail-fast update rollouts, a small number of member cluster update failures can halt progress across a broader update deployment. Maximum Allowed Failures for update runs in Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager, now available in preview, introduces an optional setting that allows update runs to continue when some member cluster updates fail.

Customers can define failure thresholds at either the stage or group level using fixed counts or percentages. This gives platform teams more control over the balance between rollout correctness and continued update progress, enabling more flexible and failure-tolerant update strategies across fleet-managed clusters.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: HTTP header insertion in Azure Firewall

Body.Content:
Azure Firewall now supports HTTP header insertion, enabling organizations to add or overwrite HTTP/HTTPS request headers directly from Azure Firewall application rules. This capability helps customers enforce security controls, support tenant restriction scenarios, integrate with backend services, and simplify application access management without relying on third-party proxies or on-premises infrastructure. 

The feature is especially useful for scenarios such as Microsoft Entra tenant restrictions, Azure Virtual Desktop, VDI, SaaS access control, and enterprise egress filtering. By enabling header insertion natively in Azure Firewall, customers can reduce proxy dependencies, avoid routing traffic back on premises solely for header injection, and improve operational efficiency.  

HTTP header insertion is supported in Azure Firewall Premium for HTTP traffic and HTTPS traffic decrypted using TLS Inspection. In Standard and Basic SKUs, it is supported for HTTP traffic. The feature can be configured through Azure Portal, Azure CLI, PowerShell, REST APIs, Terraform, and Azure Firewall Draft + Deploy. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure DDoS Protection custom policy

Body.Content:
Azure DDoS Protection custom policy is now in public preview. This capability provides per-resource control over DDoS mitigation thresholds for protected Standard Load Balancer frontend IP configurations. 

Customers can configure fixed inbound detection thresholds for TCP, UDP, and TCP SYN traffic. Thresholds can be set from 50,000 to 2,000,000 packets per second, helping customers account for predictable or unusual traffic patterns, including planned launches, seasonal peaks, gaming events, and sustained high-volume workloads. 

When a custom threshold is configured for a protocol, Azure uses that threshold instead of adaptive auto-tuning for that protocol. Protocols without a custom threshold continue to use Azure DDoS Protection’s adaptive auto-tuning. 

During public preview, customers can create and manage Custom Policy through the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure Resource Manager templates, and the REST API. 

Custom policy currently supports inbound traffic for Standard Load Balancer frontend IP configurations. Regional availability is limited during the preview. 

Learn more:  

  • Read the custom policy overview 
  • Manage custom policy using the Azure portal 
  • Manage custom policy using Azure CLI 
  • Deploy custom policy using an ARM template

Title: Public Preview: Standard service endpoint

Body.Content:
Standard service endpoint is now available in public preview, introducing a scalable and secure way to connect IaaS workloads to Azure PaaS services under the Private Link family. This enhanced capability overcomes the scale and management limitations of traditional service endpoints by integrating with network security perimeter and using Public IPs as network identifiers, enabling large‑scale IaaS‑to‑PaaS connectivity with stronger security controls.

With standard service endpoint, customers can associate a single public IP or prefix with multiple subnets or virtual networks across subscriptions within the same tenant and region. When combined with network security perimeter organizations can define a perimeter around supported PaaS resources—such as Azure Storage, Azure SQL, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Key Vault—and restrict access so that only approved networks and workloads can communicate with those resources.

This public preview builds on extensive private preview validation with enterprise and partner customers, delivering improved reliability, simplified configuration while maintaining a strong security posture for large and complex Azure environments. Additionally, The feature has been battle tested for 1P as part of SFI program providing network identification for 42k+ VNets used by 1P service providers, 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Microsoft Defender security assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

Body.Content:
Microsoft Defender Cloud Security Posture Management (CSPM) assessments for Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server are now generally available. You can use assessments to continuously evaluate the security posture of your Azure PostgreSQL flexible servers and identify vulnerabilities and misconfigurations that may cause security risks. The assessments are tailored to PostgreSQL-specific security best practices and provide actionable recommendations to help you strengthen your security baseline, prioritize remediation efforts, and support compliance requirements. 

If you already have Microsoft Defender CSPM enabled for your Azure PostgreSQL flexible server, no additional setup is required to start using these assessments. An initial set of built-in assessments is available today, with additional assessment coverage planned for future releases. You can see all findings and recommendations in the Azure portal on the resource blade of your Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server or the main Defender for Cloud experience, and the Microsoft Defender portal.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Encryption in Transit for Azure Files NFS Shares in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

Body.Content:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now generally supports Encryption in Transit (EiT) for Azure Files NFS v4.1 volumes through the Azure File CSI driver. With EiT enabled, data transferred between AKS workloads and Azure Files NFS shares is encrypted using TLS, helping customers meet security and compliance requirements for production workloads. The capability is integrated with the AZNFS mount helper and Stunnel and can be enabled through storage class configuration without requiring application changes. This capability is available in all Azure regions that support Azure Files Premium (SSD).

Learn more:  

  • Create and Manage Persistent Volumes with Azure Files in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)
  • Redundancy support for SSD Azure file shares | Microsoft Learn 
  • How to Encrypt Data in Transit for NFS shares 
  • Use Container Storage Interface (CSI) Drivers on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

Title: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration patterns including Magentic in Microsoft Agent Framework

Body.Content:
Microsoft Agent Framework reaches general availability for multi-agent orchestration patterns, including the dynamic Magentic pattern that delivered 38 percent on GAIA and competitive results on AssistantBench and WebArena in published benchmarks. The GA release covers sequential pipelines, parallel collaboration, and Magentic-style coordination, all expressed in the same framework API so teams can swap patterns without rewriting agent code. Customers running complex research, document processing, and operations workflows can now build specialist agents and let the framework handle planning, hand-off, and recovery. The release ships in .NET and Python through the framework on GitHub, with backward compatibility for the preview API and SLA-backed support for production deployments. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: Agent Harness in Microsoft Agent Framework

Body.Content:
Microsoft Agent Framework reaches general availability for Agent Harness, the production runtime for agents built with the framework. Customers running pilots on the preview harness can now move the same agent code into production with backwards compatibility, SLA-backed support, and stable interfaces for tool calls, state, and telemetry. The GA release ships in .NET and Python, supports local development, container deployment, and Foundry Hosted Agents from one binary, and emits OpenTelemetry traces that show up in Foundry observability dashboards without custom wiring. Enterprise customers building internal copilots and customer-facing agents get a single supported runtime instead of stitching together orchestration, retries, and instrumentation. The framework remains open source on GitHub. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: Multi-agent orchestration SDK with the Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework in C# and Python

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry is now introducing Agent Framework, a unified multi-agent orchestration SDK for C# and Python. This release consolidates patterns previously spread across AutoGen and Semantic Kernel, giving developers a consistent set of abstractions for building, coordinating, and deploying agents. The Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework reduces integration complexity, helps teams avoid conflicting libraries, and streamlines long-term maintenance by providing a single, well-supported model for multi-agent workloads. This release applies to scenarios that require deterministic coordination across tasks, tools, and models, while maintaining language parity for mixed-ecosystem teams. To start using the Microsoft Foundry Agent Framework, install the C# or Python packages and review the integration guidance. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: Tracing for Microsoft Agent Framework (Python and .NET)

Body.Content:
In public preview, Microsoft Foundry now offers tracing for the Microsoft Agent Framework in both Python and .NET, helping developers observe how agents reason, call tools, and interact with models during execution. This release is part of the broader hosted agents update and emits OpenTelemetry-compatible spans that you can route to Application Insights or other compatible backends, making it easier to debug failures, identify latency hotspots, and validate behavior before deploying to production. The preview is intended for evaluation and may evolve as schemas, attributes, and sampling controls are finalized ahead of general availability. By giving early access to tracing, Microsoft Foundry helps teams accelerate innovation on multi-step agent workflows without building custom instrumentation. To get started, enable tracing in the Microsoft Agent Framework SDK for Python or .NET and connect your preferred OpenTelemetry exporter. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: CodeAct pattern and Hyperlight containers in Microsoft Agent Framework

Body.Content:
Microsoft Agent Framework adds the CodeAct pattern in public preview, which lets agents collapse a multi-step plan into a single executable code block rather than chaining one tool call at a time. In representative workloads, CodeAct cut end-to-end latency by roughly 50 percent and token use by more than 60 percent compared with step-by-step orchestration. The framework runs CodeAct programs inside Hyperlight, a Microsoft-built sandboxed container runtime that boots in milliseconds and isolates each execution from the host and from other agents. Developers get the productivity of letting the model write code without giving up the safety properties that enterprises require for production agents. Both capabilities ship through the framework on GitHub in .NET and Python. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: Episodic procedural memory in Microsoft Agent Framework

Body.Content:
Microsoft Agent Framework adds episodic procedural memory in public preview, a built-in store that lets agents remember successful task patterns and replay them on similar future requests. The framework records action sequences, tool selections, and intermediate decisions as episodes, then retrieves the closest match when a new user request looks similar. Agents become measurably faster and cheaper at recurring tasks because they reuse proven plans instead of re-deriving them from scratch on every run. The capability targets agent developers who currently bolt on custom caching layers or manual few-shot prompts to get this behavior. Episodic memory is configurable per agent, ships in .NET and Python through the framework on GitHub, and integrates with the existing tracing pipeline. 

Learn more.

Title: Announcing: DevUI Agent Inspector for Microsoft Agent Framework

Body.Content:
Microsoft Agent Framework adds DevUI Agent Inspector in public preview, a local debugging surface that shows agent runs as a navigable tree of model calls, tool invocations, and intermediate state. Developers can pause, replay, and edit prompts mid-run, swap models without restarting, and inspect the full payload sent to each tool. The inspector reads the same OpenTelemetry traces that Foundry observability consumes, so what you see locally matches what shows up in production dashboards. DevUI runs as a sidecar process on a developer workstation and connects to agents built with the framework in .NET or Python. The preview is aimed at agent developers who currently rely on log scraping and ad-hoc print statements. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Front Door edge actions

Body.Content:
Announcing the public preview of Azure Front Door edge actions (serverless compute at the edge).

With edge actions, customers can execute lightweight JavaScript functions during Azure Front Door request processing to make real-time decisions closer to users, improving performance, security, and application flexibility without adding complexity to origin infrastructure.

Common scenarios include A/B testing and canary deployments, header manipulation, request filtering, dynamic origin selection, URL rewrites, authentication at the edge and many more. 

Edge actions integrate seamlessly with Azure Front Door capabilities such as rules engine, caching, routing, and Web Application Firewall (WAF). Built on Hyperlight, Microsoft’s secure micro-VM technology, edge actions provide hardware-backed isolation for customer code execution.

Learn more:

  • Blog announcement 
  • Azure Front Door edge actions documentation

You can refer to the following support lifecycle resources for guidance and upgrade to latest versions

  • Python Version Support Status  

Upgrading is required to maintain support eligibility and ensure continued access to security updates and platform features. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Exceptions in WAF for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door

Body.Content:
Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) helps protect your web applications from common threats and attacks. In some cases, WAF may block requests that are safe and expected for your application. Existing exclusions help reduce false positives by omitting specific request attributes, such as headers, cookies, query string arguments, or body fields, from WAF evaluation while the rest of the request continues to be inspected.

Exceptions provide additional flexibility by allowing specific requests to bypass WAF inspection at the rule, rule group, or managed ruleset level. Exceptions can be defined using request URI, remote IP address, or request header name and value, helping customers tune WAF policies more precisely while keeping other protections active.

To configure Exceptions, navigate to your WAF policy in the Azure portal, select Managed rules, and then add an exception. 

Learn more: 

  • Application Gateway documentation 
  • Front Door documentation

Title: Public Preview: Azure Chaos Studio Workspaces and Scenarios

Body.Content:
Azure Chaos Studio now supports Workspaces and Scenarios, a faster, application-centric way to validate how your workloads hold up during real outages.

Point a Workspace at your application's scope—a subscription, resource group, or service group—and Chaos Studio discovers the resources inside it and recommends Scenarios: preconfigured tests that reproduce real-world outage patterns. Select a Scenario, and Chaos Studio injects the right faults, in the right order, across every affected resource, then produces a Scenario report showing exactly what happened.

With Workspaces and Scenarios, you can:

  • Simulate common outage patterns out of the box, including availability zone failures, DNS and Microsoft Entra ID outages, PostgreSQL and SQL Managed Instance failovers, cache stampedes, and messaging disruptions.
  • Keep tests in sync as your app changes—resources are discovered automatically from the Workspace scope.
  • Control the blast radius with a managed identity governed by Azure RBAC.
  • Generate Scenario reports for game days, retrospectives, and compliance frameworks such as DORA.
Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Export historical data from Log Analytics workspace with Export jobs

Body.Content:
The Log Analytics Export job enables you to export historical data from a Log Analytics workspace to an Azure Storage account based on a specified query and time range. This allows you to extract only the data you need and move it to external systems for further processing or long-term retention.  

Key scenarios include: 

  • Compliance and audit – Export data from specific time periods to support audit requests, legal holds, and regulatory requirements. 
  • Security investigations – Extract relevant datasets for forensic analysis or integration with third-party SIEM solutions.  
  • Advanced analytics and machine learning – Use exported datasets to build and train models in external environments.  
  • Business intelligence and reporting – Combine exported logs with other data sources to enable reporting and analytics across your organization.  
  • Data migration – Move data out of Log Analytics for use in other platforms or long-term storage. 

 Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Network Security Perimeter support for Azure Event Hubs

Body.Content:
Azure Event Hubs now supports Network Security Perimeter (NSP), enabling organizations to define a logical network isolation boundary for PaaS resources and control public network access through perimeter-based access rules.

With Network Security Perimeter, you can help reduce data exfiltration risks by restricting access to Event Hubs namespaces and managing inbound and outbound connectivity using centralized security controls. This capability complements existing network security features and helps organizations implement consistent network isolation policies across Azure services.
Network Security Perimeter support for Event Hubs enables you to:
  1. Define secure network boundaries around Event Hubs resources.
  2. Control public access using perimeter access rules.
  3. Reduce exposure to unauthorized network traffic.
  4. Apply consistent network security policies across supported Azure services.
This capability is now generally available for Azure Event Hubs.

Learn more.

This capability is designed for organizations with heightened security, privacy, and compliance requirements, allowing them to process highly sensitive streaming data with additional protection throughout the data lifecycle. Confidential Computing support for Event Hubs Dedicated helps customers strengthen their security posture while maintaining the scale and performance benefits of a dedicated Event Hubs environment.

This feature is available for Azure Event Hubs Dedicated customers. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Microsoft Entra ID-based access for Azure Blob Storage SFTP

Body.Content:
Microsoft Entra ID-based access for Azure Blob Storage SFTP is now generally available in all regions. You can now use Entra ID identities including guest users via Entra External Identities to securely connect to Azure Blob Storage over SFTP, without provisioning or managing local SFTP users.

Why it matters

  • Eliminates the operational overhead of managing local SFTP users and credentials.
  • Strengthens security with Entra ID authentication, MFA, and Conditional Access.
  • Accelerates onboarding and enables secure external collaboration with partners and vendors via Entra External Identities (B2B).

Key capabilities

  • Single Sign-On and Multi-Factor Authentication using existing corporate credentials.
  • Conditional Access policies based on user location, device compliance, sign-in risk, and other signals.
  • Unified identity lifecycle — SFTP access is automatically updated or revoked through your existing identity governance processes.
  • Native Azure RBAC, ABAC, and ACL integration — SFTP honors the same authorization model as the REST API, Azure CLI, and other data-plane access methods.

New in GA

  • ABAC + Storage Blob Data Owner: resolved an inconsistency that could cause timeouts when combining ABAC conditions with the Storage Blob Data Owner role.
  • ABAC sub-operations: added support for sub-operations, enabling finer-grained conditional access.

Title: Public Preview: Instant Access via application consistent restore points

Body.Content:
Azure introduces Instant Access for VM Restore Points, enabling you to restore disks immediately after a restore point is created—without waiting for background data replication.

Key benefits:
  • Faster recovery (lower RTO): Restore disks instantly—no wait for data hydration.
  • High performance from the start: Restored disks are usable immediately while data copies in the background.
  • Consistent recovery: Application-consistent restore points ensure reliable recovery across all VM disks.
  • Flexible controls: Enable Instant Access and configure duration per restore point or collection.
How it works:
  • Create restore points with Instant Access enabled
  • Restore disks immediately after creation
  • Data continues to hydrate in the background for long-term durability
Pricing:

Public Preview: No additional charges apply when using Instant Access. Standard billing for disks and snapshots remains unchanged.  Post General Availability (GA): Two charges will apply:  
  • Storage Charge: Billed only for the additional storage space consumed by Instant Access Snapshots, based on data changes on the source disk after the snapshot is created.  
  • Restore Charge: A one-time fee applies for each disk restored from an Instant Access Snapshot, calculated based on the disk’s provisioned size at the time of restore.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Storage Mover now supports migration from Google Cloud Storage (GCS)

Body.Content:

Using the S3-compatible interface, customers can migrate data from GCS buckets through a fully managed, agentless experience with HMAC credentials stored securely in Azure Key Vault, no custom tooling required. With this update, enterprises can consolidate their cloud storage into Azure securely and at scale, reducing operational overhead while meeting their network isolation requirements. Get started migrating your cloud data to Azure.

Title: Generally Available: Client-side data integrity protections in Azure Blob Storage

Body.Content:
Azure Blob Storage has long supported data integrity validation, starting with MD5 as part of the original HTTP standards and adding CRC64-NVME support in 2019. Today, CRC64-NVME is now integrated into the latest Azure Blob SDKs for .NET, C++, and JavaScript, extending Azure's data integrity protections all the way into client applications. By extending data protection into client applications, customers can verify end-to-end that data written to and read from Blob Storage remains fully intact—byte-for-byte—from the application layer to Azure’s underlying physical storage, using CRC64-NVME checksums. To get started, upgrade to the latest .NET, C++, or JavaScript SDK.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Toolboxes in Microsoft Foundry

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry brings Toolboxes to GA, providing a unified endpoint to invoke the most-used tools in prompt agents and callable outside of prompt agents. Today every agent team hand-assembles its own tool list to solve the same tasks, with no shared artifact to reuse across agents and no agreed way to consume a set of governed tools. Toolboxes provide that artifact: a curated, governed bundle of tools built once in the Foundry portal or in code, configured with governance policies, and reusable across an organization. The tools agents need span MCP servers, REST APIs, skills, and connectors, each with its own protocol and auth model. Toolboxes expose all of them through a single MCP-compatible endpoint so developers stop writing per-tool integration code and admins keep consistent governance over what agents can call.

Title: Retirement: Migrate from Azure Blueprints by January 31, 2027

Body.Content:
In September 2023, we announced Azure Blueprints would retire on July 11, 2026. We're extending that timeline to January 31, 2027, with phased retirement beginning July 31, 2026.


What's changing?


July 31, 2026, you won't be able to create new blueprint definitions and versions.

October 31, 2026, you won't be able to modify blueprint definitions or create new blueprint assignments.

December 31, 2026, you won't be able to modify existing blueprint assignments.

When Azure Blueprints retires on January 31, 2027:

  • The API will no longer respond.
  • Azure CLI and PowerShell commands will stop functioning.
  • Azure Blueprints will be removed from the Azure portal.
  • Blueprint definitions, versions, or assignments not exported will be automatically deleted.
  • The blueprint locks "Do Not Delete" and "Read Only" on your resources will stop functioning, effectively setting them to a "Don't Lock" state.
  • Resources you've created through blueprints won't be deleted.

Recommended action

To avoid disruptions, act ahead of the phased retirement dates above. Migrate to Azure deployment stacks for resource grouping, lifecycle, and "deny assignments" enforcement. Publish definitions as template specs or store them in a template folder in Git for versioning. Go to the Blueprints portal to identify your impacted blueprint artifacts and export your data before January 31, 2027.

If you don't take action, Azure Blueprints functionality will decrease as the retirement phases progress but your resources will remain.

Title: Public Preview: Application Gateway for Containers – Inference gateway

Body.Content:
Application Gateway for Containers is extending its ingress gateway feature set with new AI gateway capabilities. The new inference gateway capability brings the Kubernetes Gateway API Inference Extension to Application Gateway for Containers, enabling load and model-aware routing for self-hosted generative AI workloads on AKS.

Application Gateway for Containers' inference gateway capability is purpose-built for serving LLMs and other inference workloads, routing requests based on model server signals rather than generic load balancing — improving Time to First Token (TTFT) and reducing timeouts under load.

  • Managed Body-Based Router (BBR): A fully managed router that inspects the request body (such as the model field on OpenAI-compatible APIs) to drive model-aware routing — no custom proxy tier required.
  • Bring your own Endpoint Picker (EPP): Choose the EPP implementation that fits your workload to drive metrics-aware endpoint selection across your InferencePool.
  • Secure inference: Pairs natively with the existing web application firewall (WAF) capability in Application Gateway for Containers, applying OWASP-aligned protections to AI traffic before it reaches your model servers.
  • Improved performance and reliability: Routes around saturated replicas and leverages model server state to lower TTFT, reduce timeouts, and improve GPU utilization.

Learn more:

  • Application Gateway for Containers – AI gateway - Inference gateway
  • Application Gateway for Containers - Overview

Title: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution AV36 Node Retirement now on August 30, 2027

Body.Content:
UPDATED: Microsoft announced the retirement of the AV36 node type on June 30, 2028, that date has changed to align with VMware’s roadmap. Broadcom will end support for the current AV36 version with vSphere 8 on September 30, 2027, and the AV36 SKU is not compatible with VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9, the next-generation platform. 

As part of this transition, and now to align with the AVS License-include service retirement on August 30, 2027, all AV36 SDDCs will be retired after August 30, 2027, regardless of individual RI expiration dates. On August 31, 2027, these SDDCs will no longer be accessible. 

Key dates for AV36 subscriptions: 

  • June 30, 2026 Last day to buy a 1-year RI for AV36 VCF BYOL  

  • August 30, 2027 AV36 SKU retirement and AVS License -included service retirement. 

  • August 31, 2027 SDDC access will be removed. 

Contact your Microsoft Account Team for key dates for AV36 PayGo subscriptions.

Recommended action 

At this time, we recommend that you review your current AV36 SDDCs and then work with your Microsoft Account Team. Identify available AVS node types on the Azure Product by Region page, and visit the AVS Documentation page to learn about HCX migrations between AVS node types.

Help and support 

If you have questions, please reach out to your Microsoft Account Team.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Migrate – GitHub Copilot Modernization integration for at scale code assessments

Body.Content:
Azure Migrate now integrates with GitHub Copilot Modernization (public preview) to deliver at scale code insights. This capability brings together Azure Migrate’s portfolio-level discovery and assessment with GitHub Copilot’s context-aware code analysis. The shared workflow helps migration admins and app developers collaborate more effectively while adhering to organizational security guidelines. Teams can assess multiple applications at once, evaluate Azure compatibility, and make informed refactor-versus-replatform decisions. They can also act on code-fix recommendations and effort estimates to plan modernization with greater confidence and predictability. 

Key benefits:

  • Assess applications at scale: Run Modernize CLI assessments across multiple applications and repositories simultaneously, eliminating repetitive per-app analysis. 
  • Significantly reduce analysis time: AI-driven contextual code changes across large, complex codebases. 
  • Data-driven Refactor versus Replatform decisions: Code insights from GitHub Copilot surface directly inside Azure Migrate, so migration admins and developers work from the same source of truth. 
  • Actionable remediation guidance: Surfaces remediation guidance to fix the issues and make the application ready for Azure.  
  • Plan with confidence: Effort estimates and cloud readiness let teams prioritize workloads and set realistic timelines. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: New project templates and template gallery for Azure Functions in VS Code

Title: Retirement: GPv1 and Legacy Blob storage account creation

Body.Content:
As part of our ongoing efforts to streamline the Azure Storage portfolio and deliver enhanced performance, scalability, and cost efficiency, we are announcing the retirement of all General purpose v1 (GPv1) storage accounts. This includes legacy blob storage and Files accounts configurations. 

Key Dates: 

  • October 1st, 2025: Public announcement. 
  • September 1st, 2026: New account creation blocked 
  • October 13th, 2026: Final retirement. All remaining GPv1 accounts will be transitioned to GPv2. 

What’s Changing: 

The following account types will be retired: 

  • General purpose v1 (GPv1) storage accounts (all redundancy options) 
  • Legacy blob storage accounts. 
  • Files storage accounts hosted on GPv1. 

Customers are encouraged to migrate to General Purpose v2 (GPv2) or specialized alternatives such as BlockBlobStorage or FileStorage, depending on workload requirements. 

Automatic migration warning:

After October 13, 2026, all existing GPv1 accounts will be auto migrated over to a GPv2 account, which may result in higher billing costs. Your decision not to migrate an existing GPv1 account will be construed as consent for Microsoft to migrate the account on your behalf. 

Learn more: 

  • https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-upgrade  
  • GPv1 storage account retirement overview - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn 
  • Legacy Blob Storage account retirement overview - Azure Storage | Microsoft Learn

Title: Retirement: D-series, Ds-series, Dv2-series, Dsv2-series, and Ls-series Virtual Machines for Azure Batch pools

Body.Content:
Azure Compute will retire the following Virtual Machine series on May 1, 2028, impacting Azure Batch pools that rely on them:

  • D-series, Ds-series
  • Dv2-series, Dsv2-series
  • Ls-series

After this date:

  • New Batch pools using these VM series cannot be created
  • Existing pools cannot scale out
  • Pools may be forcibly resized to zero nodes
  • Remaining VMs will be stopped/deallocated and no longer covered by SLA

Timeline

  • Now – May 1, 2028: Existing pools continue to run; migration is recommended
  • May 1, 2028: Full retirement; affected pools may become unusable

Required action
Migrate your Batch pools to supported VM families before the retirement date to avoid disruption.

Recommended replacements:

  • For general-purpose pools (D/Ds/Dv2/Dsv2): Dsv5/Ddsv5 or Dasv5/Dadsv5; or Dsv6/Ddsv6 / Dasv6/Dadsv6 for NVMe workloads
  • For storage-optimized pools (Ls): Lsv3/Lasv3 or Lsv4/Lasv4

Migration options:

  1. Scale pool to zero and update VM size using Batch API (2024-07-01 or later)
  2. Create a new pool with supported VM sizes and migrate workloads

Note: VM pricing may change after migration. Refer to Azure VM pricing for details.

Title: Retirement: Azure Load Balancer Inbound NAT rule version 1 for Azure VMSS (aka Inbound NAT Pools)

Body.Content:
Update to our previous communication: We previously announced the retirement of all Inbound NAT rules version 1 resources, which included both single-VM NAT rules and NAT pools for Virtual Machine Scale Sets. We have narrowed the scope of this retirement to Inbound NAT pools only. 

NAT pools are being retired because they provide the same functionality as Inbound NAT rules v2, which offer improved performance and is the recommended option for Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS). 

Understanding the difference: 

Inbound NAT rules version 1 includes two resource types: 

  • Inbound NAT rules version 1: Port forwarding to a single virtual machine. This feature is not affected. 
  • Inbound NAT pools: Port forwarding to Virtual Machine Scale Set instances. This feature is retiring. 

On September 30, 2027, Inbound NAT pools in Azure Load Balancer will be retired. Starting November 15, 2026, you will no longer be able to create new Inbound NAT pools. Existing configuration will continue to function until September 30, 2027. 

Recommended action: 

To avoid potential service disruptions, we recommend that you migrate to Inbound NAT rules version 2 in Azure Load Balancer by September 30, 2027.

Title: Generally Available: Microsoft Entra server principals on Azure SQL Database

Body.Content:
Microsoft Entra server principals (logins) for Azure SQL Database is now generally available. You can now use CREATE LOGIN ... FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER in the virtual master database, bringing parity with SQL logins for your Microsoft Entra identities.

With Entra logins, you can assign server roles to Entra principals, automate user and database provisioning using service principal logins, and enable Entra-only authentication to disable SQL authentication entirely. If you're already using Entra logins on Azure SQL Managed Instance or SQL Server 2022, you now get the same experience on Azure SQL Database. 

Learn more.

Title: Retirement: Azure Synapse Link for Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL

Body.Content:
As of March 31, 2026, new Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL accounts can no longer enable Azure Synapse Link. Existing customers will remain fully supported until March 31, 2029, when Azure Synapse Link will reach end of life.

We encourage all customers to begin migrating to Mirroring for Microsoft Fabric — the recommended go-forward solution for Cosmos DB analytics workloads.

Mirroring for Microsoft Fabric delivers the same zero-ETL hybrid transactional and analytical processing (HTAP) capabilities as Azure Synapse Link, with meaningful improvements:

  • Open Delta Parquet format stored in Microsoft Fabric OneLake — accessible by Fabric Spark, Fabric SQL, Power BI Direct Lake, Azure Databricks, and more

  • No schema nesting limits — removes the 1,000 property and 127-level depth restrictions of Synapse Link

  • Free replication storage — mirrored data storage is included at no cost up to your Fabric capacity limit (e.g. F64 = 64 TB of free OneLake storage)

  • Free replication compute — data replication does not consume Request Units (RUs) or impact transactional performance

  • Full Microsoft Fabric ecosystem integration — unified data management across OneLake, enabling AI and analytics scenarios at scale

To get started with migration, visit Cosmos Mirror Synapse Migration. 

If you have questions about this retirement or your migration path, please contact your Microsoft account manager or reach out directly at cosmosdbsynapselink@microsoft.com

Title: Retirement: Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) will be retired on August 31, 2026

Body.Content:
The Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) has remained in public preview and does not have a path to general availability (GA). 

As part of our ongoing efforts to align Azure networking services with current security and reliability standards, this preview client will be retired.

Timeline and Impact: 

  • August 31, 2026 – Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) is retired

  • September 1, 2026 – The Linux preview client is no longer supported for Azure VPN Gateway Point-to-Site (P2S) connections

After August 31, 2026, connections using the Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) may fail, which could result in loss of access to Azure resources through Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN connections.  

Recommended action:

To help ensure uninterrupted connectivity, transition your Azure VPN Gateway Point-to-Site (P2S) configuration to support alternative Linux VPN clients and distribute said clients to users before September 1, 2026.

For guidance on supported Point‑to‑Site VPN options and configuration steps, see the Azure VPN Gateway documentation.  

Risk/mitigation:

Update your VPN gateway configuration and your end-user clients through your standard change management process to minimize user disruption.

Help and Support :

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A  If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request.

Title: Generally Available: Azure NC RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition v6 Series Virtual Machines

Body.Content:
Azure NCv6-series virtual machines (VMs) are now generally available in the Azure Southeast Asia and West US 2 regions. NCv6 VMs are powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition graphics processing units (GPUs) with each GPU featuring 96 GB of GDDR7 memory, and enable both leading-edge graphics and generative artificial intelligence (AI) compute workloads. The VM host is equipped with Intel Xeon™ 6 "Granite Rapids" 6900P series central processing units (CPUs), providing all-core turbo frequencies up to 4.2 GHz for demanding pre- and post-processing steps.  

NCv6 offers fractional GPU support and general purpose and compute optimized VM sizes. The general purpose NCv6 VM sizes provide larger amounts of CPU memory for demanding generative AI inference and independent software vendor (ISV) computer-aided design (CAD)/computer-aided engineering (CAE) simulations, while the compute optimized NCv6 VM sizes offer reduced memory to enable customers with less memory intensive workloads to cost optimize their deployments. 

Note: For customers using the NCv6-series VMs under public preview, please see here for guidance on how to navigate the preview to general availability transition.

Title: Generally Available: Premium SSD v2 disks now support non-zonal Azure Virtual Machines

Body.Content:
Azure Premium SSD v2 disks now support non-zonal, single-instance Azure virtual machines in select Azure regions with Availability Zones (AZs). Customers can now deploy Premium SSD v2 with non-zonal virtual machines without selecting an Availability Zone. This allows customers to bring the performance and price benefits of Premium SSD v2 to workloads that have not transitioned to zonal configurations. 

Azure Premium SSD v2 is a next-generation block storage option for Azure virtual machines that delivers sub-millisecond latency and strong price performance for IO-intensive workloads such as SQL Server, Oracle, SAP, Cassandra, MongoDB, big data and analytics, and gaming workloads running on virtual machines or stateful containers. 

Pricing for non-zonal Premium SSD v2 disks is the same as zonal Premium SSD v2 disks. Customers pay for provisioned storage capacity, along with any additional IOPS and throughput provisioned above the baseline performance.   

Learn more:     

  • Documentation  
  • Premium SSD v2 Disk Storage pricing.

Title: Generally Available: Maintenance control for Azure Database for PostgreSQL - reschedule, apply on demand, view and download

Body.Content:

These new capabilities give you greater visibility and flexibility in managing platform maintenance events, helping reduce disruption to your workloads. You can now view upcoming maintenance events directly in the Azure portal, CLI, and APIs, including details such as maintenance type, expected downtime, and deferral eligibility. Additionally, you can choose to apply maintenance on demand at a time that works best for your environment, improving predictability and control. These enhancements eliminate the need for support requests to defer maintenance and help reduce the risk of unexpected downtime, making it easier to operate production workloads with confidence. These capabilities are available in all regions where Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server is offered. 

Learn more.

Title: Private Preview: Guest RDMA on Azure Boost

Body.Content:
Guest RDMA is now in preview on Azure, starting in the UK South region, bringing high-throughput, ultra-low latency networking directly into guest VMs within the same region. 

By using Azure Boost to enable RDMA in the guest OS, applications can bypass the traditional networking stack and offload transport to the NIC, reducing CPU overhead and improving communication performance.  

Key benefits include low latency through kernel bypass, high throughput of up to 100 Gb/s in preview depending on VM SKU, and lower CPU usage from hardware-based data movement.  

The preview is designed for workloads with frequent or large data transfers, including AI/ML training and inference, distributed storage and databases, and HPC workloads.  

In preview, Guest RDMA supports VM-to-VM connections within the same VNet and region. Load balancers, private endpoints, VNet encryption, flow logging, UDRs, and IP forwarding are not yet supported, but are planned for GA.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Files assessments are now available worldwide using Azure Migrate

Body.Content:
We’re pleased to announce that Azure Migrate now generally supports discovery and assessment of SMB and NFS file shares hosted on Windows and Linux servers. This gives customers a complete, data-driven view of their file share environment and a clear path to migrate to Azure Files. The capability entered preview in mid-February and is now generally available worldwide. The adoption during public preview has been strong, with hundreds of customers creating file share assessments, actively planning and executing migrations to Azure Files. 

Key benefits include:   

  1. Discover and review on-premises SMB/NFS shares from Windows/Linux environments   
  2. Group, tag, and filter shares for better planning   
  3. Generate business cases comparing Azure Files and on-premises costs   
  4. Assess shares with Azure Files SKU recommendations based on region, redundancy, media type, and performance   
  5. Alternately, evaluate move to Azure VMs for quick lift and shift rehost  

This enhancement streamlines migration planning, reduces guesswork, and speeds up transitions to Azure Files, especially for complex environments.    

Getting started: Use Azure portal to set up discovery and run Azure Files assessments in your Azure Migrate project. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Ingest OTLP signals into Azure Monitor with the OpenTelemetry Collector

Body.Content:
Azure Monitor's support for native ingestion of OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) signals is now generally available. This enables you to send telemetry data directly from OpenTelemetry-instrumented applications and platforms to Azure Monitor. You can configure your OpenTelemetry Collector to send data directly to Azure Monitor cloud ingestion endpoints to ingest OTLP metrics, logs and traces using Microsoft Entra for authentication.

You can enable OTLP data ingestion in Azure Monitor using Application Insights OR by manually creating the required data collection endpoints, rules and workspaces. The Application Insights-based approach is recommended for most scenarios as it automates resource creation and includes built-in application performance management experiences.

Ingested OTLP metrics are stored in Azure Monitor Workspaces and can be queried and alerted upon with Prometheus query language (PromQL). OTLP logs and traces are stored in Log Analytics workspaces using new OpenTelemetry tables and semantics.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: AI pipelines in Azure HorizonDB

Body.Content:
AI pipelines for Azure HorizonDB is now available in public preview. AI pipelines let you describe an AI data ingestion workflow, chunking, embedding, extraction, generation, and ranking, declaratively in SQL, and run it as a fault-tolerant pipeline inside the database.  

Execution is durable: pipelines survive crashes, retry failed steps automatically, checkpoint incremental work, and resume long-running jobs from the last completed step. 

This removes the boilerplate ingestion service that many GenAI applications rebuild today. Pipelines run on change, so embeddings stay in sync as source rows are inserted or updated, and only new or changed rows need to be re-embedded. 

When the embedding model, dimensions, or chunk size change, backfill reprocesses every row as a single durable instance that resumes from the last checkpoint instead of restarting from zero. AI pipelines are part of the azure_ai extension, built on pg_durable, and work with AI model management, pgvector, DiskANN vector search, and full-text search to provide an end-to-end retrieval path inside one database. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Microsoft Foundry IQ

Teams connect SharePoint, OneLake, Azure Blob, and other sources once, then Foundry IQ handles ingestion, chunking, vector indexing, and access enforcement using the calling user's permissions. Agents query a single knowledge base and receive ranked, source-cited results, so answers stay tied to the documents customers control. Foundry IQ runs inside the same Foundry project as the agent and shares its identity, observability, and content safety configuration. Customers can ship grounded copilots faster, reduce duplicated retrieval code across teams, and keep sensitive data inside the tenant boundary.

Title: Generally Available: Private Connectivity for Azure AI Search and Foundry Knowledge Bases

Body.Content:

Customers can route ingestion, enrichment, retrieval, and agent traffic over Shared Private Link or Network Security Perimeter so data never traverses the public internet. This release is built for organizations running RAG pipelines, Knowledge Bases, and Foundry agents on regulated or sensitive data, where compliance teams require full network isolation. Existing search indexes, indexers, and Knowledge Base configurations continue to work; customers add private connectivity through the portal or ARM templates. Combined with Azure RBAC and customer-managed keys, this brings Foundry knowledge workflows in line with the same network controls already used for Azure AI Search production deployments. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in Azure AI Search

Body.Content:
Azure AI Search now supports Content Understanding chunking and image verbalization in public preview, expanding the built-in skill that parses rich documents during indexing. Indexers can split documents into semantically meaningful chunks and generate text descriptions of embedded images, charts, and diagrams in the same pass. Retrieval-augmented generation apps benefit because each chunk carries the visual context that used to be lost when images were stripped out. Customers indexing slide decks, technical manuals, and scanned forms get higher answer quality without running a separate vision pipeline. The skill plugs into existing integrated vectorization workflows, so teams can add it to current skillsets without rebuilding indexes from scratch. This release ships under the same Azure AI Search billing and data residency commitments customers already use today. 

Learn more.

Body.Content:

Agents can call other agents by name through a managed endpoint, with identity, content safety, and audit logging applied to every hop. Developers can model multi-step business processes as a small set of cooperating agents instead of a single monolithic prompt, then trace the full conversation across agents in Application Insights. Because A2A is a first-class protocol in Agent Service, agents written with Agent Framework, LangGraph, or direct code can all participate in the same network without protocol shims. This release helps teams move from single-agent prototypes toward production multi-agent systems with the same enterprise controls already used for individual agents.

Microsoft Foundry Agent Service adds agent-to-agent (A2A) communication in public preview for Prompt agents and Hosted agents that use the responses protocol. Agents can call other agents by name through a managed endpoint, with identity, content safety, and audit logging applied to every hop. Developers can model multi-step business processes as a small set of cooperating agents instead of a single monolithic prompt, then trace the full conversation across agents in Application Insights. This release helps teams move from single-agent prototypes toward production multi-agent systems with the same enterprise controls already used for individual agents.

Title: Public Preview: Evaluations with Intelligent Trace Sampling

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry observability introduces intelligent trace filtering and sampling for evaluations in public preview. Instead of running evaluations against all production traces, Foundry now select a representative subset of traces using a multi-stage MinHash farthest-first diversity algorithm, including deduplication, hard filers, aggregation and diversity-based selection for evaluation. This approach improves cost efficiency while producing significantly higher lexical diversity and diverse coverage compared to random sampling. Intelligent sampling is particularly effective for: evaluation and benchmarks, rubric generation and finetuning dataset curation.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Secure, Modern Access to Azure Files on macOS with MS Entra ID

  • Accelerated AI workflows: Seamless access to large datasets from macOS to support faster experimentation and development 

Reach out to azurefiles@microsoft.com with questions.

Title: Generally Available: File share centric management model (Microsoft.FileShares) for Azure Files

Body.Content:
The new file share service management experience for Azure Files is now generally available for NFS 4.1 shares on SSD storage. Powered by the Microsoft.FileShares resource provider, file shares are now top-level Azure resources that you can create, secure, scale, and bill independently, without a storage account.

Key benefits:
  • Top-level resource with a familiar, NAS-like management model.
  • Independent performance for each share through the provisioned v2 billing model, with dynamic scaling up and down and no noisy-neighbor impact.

  • Support for up to 10,000 shares per subscription per region, with approximately 2.5× faster provisioning.
  • Snapshot support: up to 200 incremental, point-in-time snapshots per share, with metadata editing capability.
  • Per-share billing for cost tracking.

Title: Public Preview: Azure API Management introduces a Unified Model API for multi-model AI applications.

Body.Content:
As organizations adopt multiple LLM providers, developers often need to handle different API formats, SDKs, and integration patterns for each model vendor. This increases application complexity and makes provider switching, failover, and governance more difficult. 

With the Unified Model API, Azure API Management enables organizations to standardize on a single client-facing API format — such as the OpenAI Chat Completions API — while transparently transforming requests to various backend providers, including OpenAI and Anthropic models. 

This allows teams to: 

  • Use a consistent client SDK and API format across multiple LLM providers 

  • Switch or fail over between model providers without client-side changes 

  • Simplify application development for multi-model AI architectures 

  • Apply centralized governance, security, and observability across heterogeneous model backends 

By abstracting provider-specific differences behind a unified API layer, Azure API Management helps organizations build more portable, resilient, and governable AI applications. 

Learn more.
