Title: Generally Available: Unified Text Translation API in Azure AI Translator

Title: Generally Available: Azure API Management Premium v2 and Standard v2 now support wildcard custom hostnames.

Body.Content:
As API estates grow, managing individual custom domains and certificates for every subdomain can quickly become operationally complex and difficult to scale. Without wildcard support, every new subdomain — whether payments.api.contoso.com, inventory.api.contoso.com, or orders.api.contoso.com — requires its own hostname registration and certificate, meaning a team onboarding ten new API surfaces generates ten separate domain and certificate management tasks.  

With this update, Azure API Management Premium v2 and Standard v2 now support wildcard entries in custom hostnames,  allowing a single entry like *.api.contoso.com  and a single wildcard certificate to cover all subdomains automatically — no per-subdomain configuration required. This helps teams:  

  • Simplify certificate and domain management at scale  
  • Reduce operational overhead for rapidly growing API environments  
  • Maintain consistent branded API endpoints across dynamic subdomains  
  • Accelerate onboarding of new API surfaces without repeated hostname configuration  

By extending this capability to both Premium v2 and Standard v2, Azure API Management makes flexible and scalable domain management accessible to more organizations without requiring higher-tier deployments.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Backup for Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
You can now enable vaulted backups for Azure Cosmos DB accounts, protecting mission-critical data with secure, isolated, and resilient backups. Azure Backup for Cosmos DB, now in preview, supports cyber-resiliency and compliance needs, even in scenarios involving accidental deletion, malicious activity, or ransomware. With vaulted backups, Azure Backup maintains an independent copy of your Cosmos DB data in a vault that is isolated from the source account, strengthening protection against operational and security risks.  

Key capabilities:  

  • Off-site, isolated protection. Store Cosmos DB backups in an Azure Backup vault, isolated from the source account to enable recovery even if the source is compromised.  
  • Resilience. Vaulted backups protect against accidental deletion, insider threats, and ransomware scenarios.  
  • Policy-based, automated backups. Configure scheduled backups using Azure Backup policies, reducing manual efforts and improving consistency. 
  • Long-term retention for compliance. Retain backups for extended durations of up to 10 years to meet regulatory and audit requirements.  
  • Built-in protections such as encryption, soft delete, immutability, and role-based access control help safeguard backup data in the vault.  

Billing will be enabled from July 1, 2026.  

Learn more: 

  • Documentation  
  • Azure Backup pricing 
  • Pricing calculator

Title: Generally Available: Voice Live integration with Microsoft Foundry Agent Service

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service is now generally available for Voice Live integration, allowing developers to connect real-time speech-to-text and text-to-speech to a Foundry Agent without writing their own audio pipeline. Existing agent capabilities — including tool calling, knowledge, memory, guardrails, and enterprise integrations — continue to work seamlessly and are now enhanced with low-latency speech interactions. The agent provides a real-time streaming voice channel with interrupt handling, turn-taking, barge-in support, connection management, natural voices, and avatars for production phone and web experiences. For customers building customer service agents, learning companions, and in-car assistants, this provides a single supported path from Foundry agent logic to live audio input and output, instead of requiring them to stitch together Speech, the agent runtime, and WebRTC on their own.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Policy Coverage for Model Router in Foundry Models

Body.Content:
Azure Policy now provides centralized governance for deployments using the model router. Organizations can define and enforce routing standards across their environment, helping ensure that model selection aligns with security, compliance, and operational requirements.

Built-in policy definitions allow teams to govern deployment regions, approved model lists, required routing rules, and logging configurations. Administrators can apply policies across management groups and subscriptions, identify deployments that drift from approved configurations, and remediate issues using existing Azure governance workflows.

Because the integration is built on Azure Policy’s native framework, customers can use familiar tools for compliance monitoring, exemptions, remediation, and reporting without additional engineering effort. This enables regulated organizations to adopt new models more quickly while maintaining consistent governance and control across the enterprise. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts

Body.Content:
We’re excited to announce the General Availability of Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts! Using dynamic thresholds means you don't have to know the right threshold for each Log alert rule - Dynamic thresholds calculate the most appropriate thresholds for you.

Key benefits
Dynamic thresholds apply advanced machine learning and use a set of algorithms and methods to:
  1. Learn the historical behavior of log query results.
  2. Analyze these results over time and identify hourly / daily / weekly seasonal patterns.
  3. Calculate the most appropriate thresholds for log alert rules.
  4. Adapt automatically to changes in data patterns and adjust the threshold accordingly.
  5. At-scale monitoring - in rule monitoring multiple dimensions - the Dynamic threshold is calculated individually, per dimension combination.
Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Rolling updates in Flex Consumption

Body.Content:
Rolling updates are now generally available in the Flex Consumption plan, delivering zero-downtime deployments with a simple configuration change.

Instead of forcefully restarting all instances during code or configuration updates, the platform gracefully replaces live instances by draining batches every few seconds while dynamically scaling out the latest version to meet demand. This approach ensures uninterrupted execution and resilient throughput across HTTP, non-HTTP, and Durable workloads - even during intensive scale-out scenarios.

How to enable:

  1. In the Azure Portal, enable it from the Configuration blade 

  2. Update your ARM/Bicep template with `properties.functionAppConfig.siteUpdateStrategy.type` set to `RollingUpdate`

  3. For Durable Functions, configure an orchestration match strategy (see guidance).

Known limitations:

  • Scale-out issues may occur with low HTTP concurrency; recommended value is 16.

  • No automatic rollback; roll forward by redeploying the last healthy version.

Learn more.

Title: Private Preview: Storage optimized Lasv5 and Laosv5 Azure VM series

Body.Content:
The Lasv5 and Laosv5 storage optimized VMs, based on the 5th Gen AMD EPYC™ processor (Turin), are in preview. 

Lasv5-series is designed for storage-intensive workloads requiring high disk capacity, throughput, and I/O, while Laosv5-series is well-suited for workloads requiring significantly higher local storage capacity and performance. 

Lasv5 and Laosv5 VMs have sizes ranging from 2-160 vCPUs, with 8GiB of memory and 720GB of local NVMe disk capacity per vCPU. Both support 200Gbps of network bandwidth and deliver up to 35% better average CPU performance. The Lasv5 VMs offer up to 30.7TB of local storage capacity, while the Laosv5 VMs offer up to 138TB of local storage capacity. 

Compared to the previous generation Lasv4 VMs, Lasv5 VMs have: 

  • 33% larger maximum local storage capacity 
  • New 128 and 160 vCPU sizes 

Compared to the previous generation Laosv4 VMs, Laosv5 VMs have: 

  • 500% larger maximum local storage capacity 
  • New 48, 64, 96, 128, and160 vCPU sizes 

Learn more.

Title: Private Preview: multiparty analytics with Azure Confidential Clean Rooms

Body.Content:
Microsoft is announcing the preview of multiparty analytics with Azure Confidential Clean Rooms, resulting in fully managed service that allows customers and their partners to securely analyze privacy sensitive datasets with Apache Spark based big-data analytics (Spark SQL) in a confidential computing based environment which protects their raw data from other collaborators and from the Azure operator by performing the computation in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE). Privacy sensitive datasets include personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI) and cryptographic secrets.

Organizations across industries are increasingly looking to supplement their data with data from business partners, to build a complete view of their business. For example, brands, publishers, and their partners need to collaborate using datasets containing Intellectual Property (IP) to improve the relevance of their campaigns. Data clean rooms help solve this challenge by allowing multiple organizations to share granular data and analyze combined datasets in a secure environment which provides guarantees against exfiltration of raw data.

Learn more.

Body.Content:

Title: Azure Container Linux (ACL) now generally available on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS)

Body.Content:
Azure Container Linux is a container-optimized, immutable operating system for AKS node pools — derived from Flatcar Container Linux and built on Azure Linux RPM packages. It delivers a locked-down, minimal host purpose-built for running containerized workloads at scale. 

Key features include: 

  • Immutable by design — The root /usr directory is read-only with dm-verity integrity verification. There is no package manager on the host — what ships in the image is what runs in production. This eliminates configuration drift and ensures consistent node state across your fleet. 
  • Container-optimized — Minimal OS footprint with only the components needed to run Kubernetes workloads. 
  • Out-of-the-box security — SELinux in enforcing mode applies strict least-privilege policies to all processes. Trusted Launch with a Unified Kernel Image (UKI) verifies boot integrity from firmware through kernel, ensuring nodes haven't been tampered with before they join your cluster. 
  • Derived from Flatcar — Built on Flatcar Container Linux's proven architecture: declarative node configuration, systemd-first service management, and an operational model designed for fleets of immutable nodes. 

  • Built on Azure Linux — Powered by the Azure Linux RPM ecosystem with Microsoft's security patching cadence, CVE response SLAs, and integrated support through Azure. 

Learn more and get started:  

  • Tech Community blog post 
  • Azure Container Linux Documentation 
  • Azure Linux Documentation 
  • Azure Linux on GitHub

Title: Public preview: Azure Linux 4.0 for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets

Body.Content:
Azure Linux 4.0, Microsoft's first-party Linux distribution purpose-built for Azure, is now available in public preview for Azure Virtual Machines and VM Scale Sets. It brings a modernized stack — including Linux kernel 6.18 LTS, dnf5 package manager, glibc 2.42, OpenSSL 3.5, and Python 3.14 — optimized for Azure compute, storage, and networking. It delivers faster VM startup and provisioning with a reduced package footprint and a security-first design. 

  Key highlights: 

  • Azure-tuned kernel — Linux 6.18 LTS with improved Hyper-V integration, GPU/AI accelerator support, and new hardware drivers 
  • Secure by default — Secure Boot, Trusted Launch, SELinux support, kernel hardening, and SBOMs published with target SLSA Level 3 
  • Minimal footprint — Ships only the packages required for cloud workloads, reducing attack surface from day one 
  • No additional OS licensing cost — Included with Azure compute; no separate OS licensing fees or support contracts 
  • Microsoft-owned supply chain — From kernel to CVE response, enabling fast-track Critical/High CVE patches with monthly security updates 
  • Predictable lifecycle —full support with LTS kernel and annual HWE kernel updates for new hardware platforms 
  • Container images — Base, and distroless images available on Microsoft Container Registry (MCR)

 Learn more:

  • Azure Linux 4.0 Build blog post   
  • Azure Linux on GitHub 
  • Release notes

Title: Generally Available: OpenTelemetry Metrics, Visualizations, and Enhanced Monitoring in Azure Monitor for Azure VMs and Arc Servers

Body.Content:
OpenTelemetry metrics and visualizations in Azure Monitor are generally available, delivering an enhanced, unified monitoring experience for Azure Virtual Machines and Arc Servers. This release consolidates key monitoring capabilities into a single experience and introduces a simplified onboarding experience, helping customers more efficiently observe, diagnose, and optimize their environments. 

Previously, VM monitoring visualizations were powered by metric data from Log Analytics which continues to be fully supported. Customers now also have the option to power these visualizations using OpenTelemetry (OTel) Gues OS metrics, offering a more cost-efficient and performant solution.  

With this release, you can: 

  • Reduce monitoring costs and improve troubleshooting efficiency with faster metric query response times using OTel metrics 
  • Simplify setup with a unified onboarding experience, including support for selecting existing Data Collection Rules (DCRs) 
  • Onboard and configure monitoring at scale through the Monitoring Coverage, ARM templates, or Bicep templates 
  • Enable recommended alerts to accelerate issue detection and reduce configuration overhead 
  • Leverage Dashboards with Grafana for at-scale visibility and per-process insights across your VM environments 

Learn more: 

  • https://aka.ms/vmiv2docs   
  • Collect and customize OpenTelemetry metrics for Azure virtual machines - Azure Monitor

Title: Public Preview: Automatic OS Image Upgrades for VMSS Flex

Body.Content:
Automatic OS Image Upgrades for Virtual Machine Scale Sets (VMSS) using Flexible Orchestration are now in public preview, enabling consistent, fleet-wide OS updates with reduced manual effort. This capability extends automated image upgrades to VMSS Flex, helping customers maintain secure, compliant, and up-to-date infrastructure at scale while lowering operational overhead. 

With this release, Azure shifts from per-VM patching to platform-driven, orchestrated updates applied across the entire scale set. Updates are rolled out using health-based progression, ensuring upgrades continue only when instances remain healthy, improving reliability and reducing risk.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Functions now supports hosting MCP Apps

Body.Content:
Developers building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers often rely on plain text responses even when user interactions required richer experiences, such as visual data exploration, complex configuration, real-time status monitoring, or multi-step workflows, which leads to excessive back-and-forth and limited usability. 


Azure Functions now supports building and hosting MCP Apps using the Azure Functions MCP Extension. MCP Apps enable servers to return interactive user interfaces that render directly within chat experiences, including forms, dashboards, and rich media viewers. This capability is available for Python, TypeScript, .NET, and Java, allowing developers to build MCP Apps using familiar languages.

With MCP Apps on Azure Functions, developers can now deliver richer and interactive experiences directly in conversations, reducing conversational friction, streamlining complex workflows, and making it easier for users to explore data and monitor live information without leaving the chat.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Functions now includes managed connectors to integrate with 1400+ of your favorite systems

Body.Content:
Azure Functions now includes managed connectors - the same 1,400+ connector ecosystem behind Logic Apps and Power Platform - as first-class triggers and operations. This enables customers to build integrated systems across the broader ecosystem such as Office 365, Teams, SharePoint, Salesforce, and other SaaS services, using familiar Functions workflows. 

With connectors natively available, developers can build event-driven integrations without custom polling logic or manual SDK integration, simplifying development and reducing integration friction. 

This feature eliminates the need to build custom integration logic, enabling direct connections to services like Microsoft 365, Salesforce, ServiceNow, SAP, Dynamics, and 1400+ other systems. You can now write event-driven Functions that respond to SaaS events or output to external systems using familiar Functions syntax, reducing integration complexity and time-to-market. 

Learn more:

  • Azure Functions integration with managed connectors in Azure Functions samples

Title: Public Preview: Serverless agents runtime for Azure Functions

Body.Content:
Azure Functions now supports building AI agents as a first-class workload using a markdown-first programming model in public preview. With this release, developers can author event-driven serverless agents in natural language. 

The serverless agents runtime helps developers build agents that respond to conversations, react to events, and take actions across enterprise systems without writing framework boilerplate or per-service integration code. Developers can use any Azure Functions trigger — HTTP, timer, queue, Service Bus, Event Hub, Cosmos DB, blob, Event Grid, and new connector-backed triggers (Teams messages, Outlook mail, calendar events) — to run an agent. Agents can also call connectors as tools, consume remote MCP servers, run sandboxed code and browser automation in Azure Container Apps dynamic sessions, and optionally expose a built-in chat UI, HTTP chat API, and MCP server endpoint with no extra code. 

In preview, the serverless agents runtime is supported on the Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan. This enables scale-to-zero economics, managed identity, VNet integration, and Application Insights observability for agent workloads on Azure.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Copilot-assisted coding & agent skills to build, deploy, and run Azure Functions faster in VS Code, CLI, and azd

Body.Content:
Developers are already using AI coding assistants to build Azure Functions apps today, but the quality of the help varies widely. It depends on which underlying model the assistant is using and how recent its training data is, which means developers often get advice based on outdated APIs, deprecated patterns, or generic guidance that misses Azure Functions best practices. 

Azure Functions now provides a set of AI assistant plugins and agent skills in public preview that close that gap. With a quick one-step install, developers can equip their AI coding assistant — including GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex — with current, Azure Functions expertise that activates automatically as they work in VS Code, the CLI, and azd. The skills cover the end-to-end developer loop: local setup, project and function creation, deployment with tools, diagnostics for deployment and runtime issues, app health and inventory inspection, and best-practices review of existing Function Apps. They follow the Agent Skills open standard, are grounded in official Azure documentation, and integrate with relevant MCP servers so the assistant always works from the latest guidance and Azure best practices — not whatever its base model happened to learn at training time. 

The result is more accurate, more consistent, and more current AI assistance for Azure Functions, regardless of which assistant or model the developer chooses.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Built-in Grafana dashboards for Azure Functions

Body.Content:
Azure Functions now provides built-in Grafana dashboards. Customers now get a zero-setup, single pane of glass for the health, performance, and scale of their function apps directly in the Azure portal: no Grafana instance to provision, no data sources to wire up, and no extra cost.

Customers can duplicate and customize the dashboard to fit their team's needs.

Title: Generally Available: Override Scale Rules in Azure Functions on Azure Container Apps

Body.Content:
Azure Functions on Container Apps has traditionally used platform-managed scaling, where triggers are automatically translated into KEDA scale rules. With the new allowScalingRuleOverride property, customers can now choose to override platform-managed scaling and define their own custom KEDA scaling rules.

When scaling override is enabled, the platform skips automatic KEDA rule generation and applies customer-defined scaling rules while continuing to run on the same native Functions on Container Apps architecture, available in API version 2026-03-02-preview and later.

This enhancement is especially useful for scenarios where there are gaps in platform trigger support, where automatically generated KEDA rules may lead to unintended scaling behavior, or where workloads require custom queue thresholds, HTTP concurrency tuning, or standardized scaling policies across services.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Additional support for OpenTelemetry destinations (New Relic, Dynatrace, Elastic)

Body.Content:
Azure Container Apps enhances its OpenTelemetry (OTel) capabilities by expanding support for third-party observability platforms. This update introduces additional endpoint options for commonly used monitoring tools such as New Relic, Dynatrace, and Elastic, extending the existing managed OpenTelemetry experience with simpler setup for additional third-party observability platforms.  

This update makes it easier to send logs, metrics, and traces to more destinations without deploying or managing your own agents. Teams can now use a more consistent OpenTelemetry-based pipeline across Azure Monitor, Datadog, New Relic, Dynatrace, Elastic, and OTLP-compatible endpoints, with less configuration overhead and more flexibility to route telemetry where they need it, including support for OTLP/HTTP endpoints, enabling integration with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Monitor HTTP traffic in Azure Container Apps

Body.Content:
In addition to platform-level logs, Azure Container Apps now adds a dedicated Azure Monitor diagnostic setting category, ContainerAppHTTPLogs, that exposes detailed HTTP access logs for incoming traffic and is designed for high-volume request data. With this capability, customers can now troubleshoot ingress and request-flow issues with much greater precision, making it easier to investigate failed requests, latency, retries, WebSocket disconnects, routing behavior, and backend connectivity problems.  

This gives teams a dedicated, scalable traffic logging surface for scenarios where platform-level signals alone were not enough to quickly understand request-level behavior. The result is faster issue resolution, less operational friction, and stronger confidence in running and scaling high-traffic, business-critical applications on Azure Container Apps.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Confidential Compute support on Azure Container Apps

Body.Content:
Customers running regulated or sensitive containerized workloads often need stronger protection for data while it is actively being processed, especially in scenarios that require higher isolation and stricter compliance controls. 

Confidential Compute in Azure Container Apps provides hardware-backed Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) through workload profiles, extending protection to data in use in addition to data at rest and in transit. With this capability now generally available, teams can run higher-trust workloads in Azure Container Apps with stronger isolation for sensitive data and a clearer path to meeting stricter compliance and data sovereignty requirements. 

This release enables Azure Container Apps workloads to use hardware-enforced isolation mechanisms that protect sensitive data while it is being processed and help prevent unauthorized access to in-memory data, including from the underlying infrastructure. Teams can now deploy confidential workloads on a serverless container platform with stronger protections for data in use. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator (vNext)

Body.Content:
We are announcing the general availability of the Azure Cosmos DB Linux emulator (vNext), a cross-platform, Docker-based emulator for local development and testing against Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL. 


The vNext emulator runs as a lightweight Docker container on Linux, macOS, and Windows, with native support for both x64 and ARM64 architectures. You can use it to develop and test your applications locally without incurring Azure service costs or needing an internet connection. 


Since public preview, the emulator has shipped continuous updates that have significantly improved SDK compatibility and expanded Cosmos DB feature coverage. 


With this release, you get a local development experience that includes support for core operations, a wide range of query capabilities, and added support for vector search and Azure Cosmos DB Shell integration. The emulator also includes health probe endpoints for readiness checks, and OpenTelemetry integration for observability. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: OmniVec, an open-source embedding toolkit for Azure

Body.Content:
You can now automate embedding generation from multiple data sources into Azure Cosmos DB and other Azure destinations. Building AI applications often requires stitching together data extraction, embedding generation, and writing to vector databases into a custom pipeline. You have to write extraction logic for each source, integrate with embedding APIs, and build your own sync mechanism to keep embeddings current as source data changes. OmniVec, now in public preview as an open-source project, handles this pipeline end to end, deployed in your own Azure subscription. 


You configure your data sources, select an embedding model, and deploy with a single azd up command. OmniVec pulls data from sources like Azure Cosmos DB, Azure Blob Storage, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server; generates embeddings; and writes them to Azure Cosmos DB and other destinations on Azure. 


OmniVec handles content extraction, chunking, and incremental sync out of the box. It supports Microsoft Foundry as well as self-hosted models. You get a web UI, CLI, and REST API for managing sources, models, destinations, and pipelines. 


The project is MIT-licensed and available on GitHub.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Integrated embeddings for Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL

Body.Content:
Building AI applications on Azure Cosmos DB just got simpler. With integrated embeddings, now in public preview, Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL can automatically generate and maintain embeddings for your data, without the need to build a separate pipeline. 


Now you can configure your container's vector embedding policy with one or more source properties, a target property, and a Microsoft Foundry model endpoint. Cosmos DB handles the rest: as items are created or updated, embeddings are generated and kept in sync automatically. 


Before this announcement, developers had to write integration code to call embedding APIs, build change-tracking logic to keep embeddings current, and manage the glue code that connects data changes to embedding generation. Integrated embeddings removes this entire layer of complexity, letting you focus on your application logic. 


 Azure OpenAI embedding models via Microsoft Foundry are supported in the initial release. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Safe key rotation for Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
The safe key rotation feature helps you confidently rotate your Azure Cosmos DB account keys by providing visibility into when each key was last used. Without this insight, you risk rotating a key that may still be actively used by your applications, which can lead to unexpected service disruptions. 


With safe key rotation, you can identify active and inactive keys before taking action, enabling you to make informed decisions and improve your security posture. This capability supports safer migrations, including transitioning to Microsoft Entra ID, by ensuring keys are no longer in use before disabling access. By reducing operational risk and increasing transparency, safe key rotation helps you maintain application reliability while strengthening key management practices.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Agent Memory Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
You can now accelerate the development of agentic applications with the new Agent Memory Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB. This toolkit provides a customizable, code-first solution to help you build scalable, durable, and cost-efficient memory systems for your AI agents, without having to design complex pipelines from scratch. 


With the Agent Memory Toolkit, you can easily store, update, and retrieve agent memories using a simple interface, while the toolkit handles key tasks such as data processing, embedding generation, and retrieval orchestration behind the scenes using Azure Durable Functions. The toolkit eliminates the need to manually integrate multiple services and simplifies a common architecture pattern used for agent memory systems. 


You benefit from faster time to production, improved retrieval relevance, and a more consistent and scalable memory foundation for your applications. Whether you are building conversational agents, copilots, or multi-agent workflows, the toolkit helps you focus on your application logic instead of infrastructure. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Semantic reranker in Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
You can now improve the relevance of any Cosmos DB query or search with the public preview of semantic reranker in Azure Cosmos DB. Semantic reranker analyzes the meaning of your queries and your data to reorder results based on contextual relevance rather than keyword matching alone. This ranking is especially useful for AI-powered applications such as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), question answering, and agentic apps. 


With semantic reranker, you can deliver more precise and reliable results without building complex ranking pipelines or tuning scoring logic manually. It works directly with your existing Cosmos DB queries—including vector, full-text, and hybrid search—enabling you to quickly enhance result quality while maintaining low operational overhead.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Agentic Retrieval Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
We are announcing the public preview of the Agentic Retrieval Toolkit for Azure Cosmos DB. Motivated by GraphRAG and multiple-hop reasoning problems, this new capability helps you build advanced retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications that go beyond single-pass retrieval by dynamically identifying information gaps and iteratively retrieving additional context. The toolkit combines hybrid search across vector and full-text indexes, diversity-aware document selection, and multiple-round reasoning to produce more complete, grounded responses. 


With agentic retrieval, you can improve answer quality for complex, multiple-step questions where relevant information is spread across many documents or data sources. The retrieval pipeline adapts in real time by generating follow-up queries, retrieving new evidence, and refining responses until it has sufficient coverage. This approach reduces redundancy, increases recall, and delivers higher-fidelity results for copilots, agents, and knowledge-intensive applications built on Azure Cosmos DB. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB global secondary indexes

Body.Content:
Global secondary indexes (GSIs) for Azure Cosmos DB are now generally available, giving you a powerful way to accelerate query performance without adding complexity to your application code. GSIs are read-only containers that automatically stay in sync with your source container using the change feed. Each GSI has its own throughput, partition key, and indexing policy, so you can optimize them for any query pattern. 


With GSIs, you can convert expensive cross-partition queries into efficient single-partition lookups by storing data under a different partition key. Using GSIs means lower Request Unit (RU) consumption, reduced latency, and better performance isolation for your workloads. You can isolate a subset of your workload, such as creating vector or full-text search indexes in the GSI to support AI applications, without impacting transactional operations on the source container. 


Adding a GSI to a new or existing container allows you to maintain query efficiency even as your workload requirements evolve.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure API Management adds support for Agent-to-Agent (A2A) APIs

Body.Content:
As organizations build more agentic applications, agent-to-agent communication is becoming a critical part of enterprise AI systems. But in many environments, agent traffic operates outside existing API governance layers — making it difficult to apply consistent security, visibility, and operational controls.  

With support for JSON-RPC–based A2A APIs, Azure API Management enables platform teams and developers to manage agent interactions alongside REST, GraphQL, MCP tools, and AI model APIs using the same API management platform they already rely on. This allows organizations to apply existing security, mediation, and governance policies to agent traffic, observe and trace agent interactions end-to-end, and manage agent APIs within a unified operational model instead of introducing separate gateways or disconnected tooling for agents.  

By bringing A2A APIs into the same governance and observability framework as the broader API ecosystem, Azure API Management helps organizations scale agentic systems with enterprise-grade security, control, and operational consistency.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure API Management workspaces now support the built-in gateway

Body.Content:
Organizations using workspace-based API management models previously needed a dedicated workspace gateway and Premium tier deployment to take advantage of API Management workspaces increasing both cost and operational complexity.  

With this update, Azure API Management customers can now associate workspaces directly with the built-in gateway, extending workspace support across additional tiers and all regions supported by API Management. This helps organizations:  

  • Use workspaces in any API Management tier (except for Consumption)  
  • Create workspaces in any region supported by API Management  
  • Take advantage of built-in gateway capabilities that are not available in workspace gateways, such as multi-region deployments, custom hostnames, or Private Link connectivity  

By bringing workspaces to the built-in gateway, Azure API Management makes it easier and more cost-effective for organizations to adopt team-based API governance and delegated API management models at scale.  

This feature is currently rolling out to v2 tiers of API Management and will start rolling out to classic tiers around July or August.  

Learn more.

Title: Public preview: Connector Namespace

Body.Content:
Integrating apps with SaaS and line-of-business systems today means writing custom API client code, managing credentials, and handling retries, pagination, and webhooks for every service.

Connector Namespace is a fully managed service providing pre-built connectors to services like SharePoint, Salesforce, Outlook, and SAP.   • Managed connections: reusable, authenticated bindings with built-in credential storage and rotation

  • Managed connector MCP servers hosting: deploy connector-as-MCP-server so agents can invote them as tools with custom wrappers

  • Flexible compute: use with Azure Functions, Container Apps, App Service, or your own infra 
  • Enterprise security: VNet, private endpoints, RBAC, and Azure Monitor built in.  

With Connector Namespace, you integrate apps and AI agents through a consistent model, reuse connections, go from connector to MCP server in minutes, and let the platform handle auth and reliability so you ship faster with fewer moving parts. 

Learn more.

  • Gain deeper operational visibility into evolving model behaviors and token economics  

By expanding token observability, Azure API Management helps organizations better manage AI usage, optimize costs, and improve governance across modern generative AI applications.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager for Arc-enabled clusters

Body.Content:
Managing Kubernetes clusters across hybrid and multi-cloud environments is fragmented by default: different consoles, different tools, different operational models. Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager now supports Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes in GA, so any CNCF-compliant distribution can join a fleet as a member cluster.

For customers running mixed estates today, this reduces reliance on third-party multi-cluster tools (and the ongoing licensing that comes with them) while keeping a consistent operational model across AKS, on-premises, and other clouds.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB all versions and deletes change feed mode

Body.Content:
The Azure Cosmos DB all versions and deletes change feed mode is now generally available, giving you complete visibility into every change that happens in your containers. Unlike the default latest version mode, which surfaces only the most recent state of an item, all versions and deletes captures every create, update, and delete operation in the order it occurred, including intermediate changes between reads and TTL expirations. 


This mode opens up scenarios that were previously difficult to build. You can replicate data between locations without implementing soft deletes, trigger logic on every incremental change even when multiple updates happen between polls, and set up auditing workflows that fire on delete operations. Each change includes metadata identifying the operation type, so your application can handle creates, updates, and deletes with distinct processing logic. 


To get started, enable continuous backups on your Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account, which automatically creates the all versions and deletes change log. You can then consume it through the change feed pull model or change feed processor in supported SDKs. Changes are available to read within your configured continuous backup retention period. 

Learn more.

Unlike the default latest version mode, which surfaces only the most recent state of an item, all versions and deletes captures every create, update, and delete operation in the order it occurred, including intermediate changes between reads and TTL expirations.

This mode opens up scenarios that were previously difficult to build. You can replicate data between locations without implementing soft deletes, trigger logic on every incremental change even when multiple updates happen between polls, and set up auditing workflows that fire on delete operations. Each change includes metadata identifying the operation type, so your application can handle creates, updates, and deletes with distinct processing logic.

To get started, enable continuous backups on your Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL account, which automatically creates the all versions and deletes change log. You can then consume it through the change feed pull model or change feed processor in supported SDKs. Changes are available to read within your configured continuous backup retention period.

Learn more .

Title: Generally Available: Per-partition automatic failover for Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
Per-partition automatic failover (PPAF) is now generally available in Azure Cosmos DB, bringing faster recovery and higher availability to your mission-critical applications. 


With PPAF, you no longer need to fail over an entire account during a regional disruption. Azure Cosmos DB automatically fails over only the impacted partitions, while healthy partitions continue serving traffic. This approach sharply reduces disruption, shortens recovery times, and removes the need for manual intervention during outages. 


PPAF helps you meet stringent availability and durability requirements without redesigning your application or operating multiple write regions. You can run highly resilient workloads with predictable performance, while Azure Cosmos DB transparently handles partition-level recovery behind the scenes.

Title: Generally Available: Graceful failover with zero data loss guarantee

Body.Content:
Azure DocumentDB is excited to announce the general availability of graceful failovers that promote replica clusters while guaranteeing zero data loss. This feature is an addition to the already existing force promote feature, which immediately promotes a replica cluster in the event of availability loss.


Force promote favors availability over consistency and thus does not wait for unreplicated data to make its way to the replica cluster before being promoted. 


With the graceful promote feature, you can now promote a regional cluster to the primary in the event of changing application traffic patterns. This feature is ideal when there is no availability loss on the primary but simply a change in traffic that requires database requests to be made to the closer regional cluster.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Advanced filtering for DiskANN vector search in Azure HorizonDB

Body.Content:
Advanced filtering for DiskANN vector search in Azure HorizonDB is now available in public preview. With this release, you can combine vector similarity search with metadata filters such as category, date range, price, or tenant ID without the performance penalties that typically come with filtered vector queries. DiskANN advanced filtering delivers lower latency on filtered vector search compared to traditional approaches, enabling you to build AI-powered retrieval applications that are both precise and fast at scale. Whether you are building an agentic application, a product recommendation engine, or an enterprise search experience, you can now apply complex filters alongside vector similarity in a single query and get results in milliseconds, even across millions of vectors. This capability runs natively inside your Azure HorizonDB instance alongside your relational data, eliminating the need for a separate vector database or external search service. You retain full transactional consistency, use familiar PostgreSQL SQL, and benefit from DiskANN's industry-leading performance on disk-resident indexes. Advanced filtering works seamlessly with pgvector, Azure AI integrations, and the broader HorizonDB AI retrieval stack, including BM25 full-text search and graph traversal. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: BM25 full-text search in Azure HorizonDB

Body.Content:
BM25 full-text search is now available in public preview for Azure HorizonDB. Now you can get production-quality keyword search powered by BM25, the same relevance ranking algorithm used by Elasticsearch, Solr, and Azure AI Search, running entirely inside your PostgreSQL database as a native extension. 


You no longer need to deploy and manage a separate search service to get high-quality text search. The full-text search extension replaces PostgreSQL's built-in ts_rank with BM25 scoring, which delivers significantly better relevance through term frequency saturation, document length normalization, and inverse document frequency weighting. It's faster than native PostgreSQL full-text search with Generalized Inverted Index (GIN) indexes on complex, multi-keyword queries. The extension also supports fuzzy matching for typo tolerance, phrase search with configurable word proximity, and Boolean query syntax (AND, OR, NOT) capabilities that previously required an external search engine. 


By combining pgvector with DiskANN for vector similarity search, you can now build hybrid search applications that deliver both keyword precision and semantic understanding in a single SQL query using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Your data stays in one place, you use familiar PostgreSQL, and you eliminate the operational burden of syncing data to an external search service. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot in MSSQL extension

Body.Content:
The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now offers data API builder with built-in GitHub Copilot integration as generally available, bringing guided back-end generation into your development workflow. 


You can generate REST, GraphQL, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints from your SQL database schema inside Visual Studio Code without manually configuring infrastructure or connection strings. You select tables, define CRUD operations, and configure settings such as authorization roles, primary keys, route behavior, and column-level exposure through an API design interface. 


The generated data API builder configuration file stays synchronized with your selections, can be previewed in the extension, and added to your workspace for transparency and version control. You can modify it manually or use GitHub Copilot to plan and generate updates. 


This release also streamlines endpoint design, configuration review, and guided generation. You can now go beyond table-level selection and choose which columns are exposed in the generated API. Columns are exposed by default, but you can turn off exposure for sensitive, unsupported, or unnecessary fields such as password hashes, social security numbers, internal flags, or stale data. 


With a few steps, the extension runs a local data API builder container using your database connection. This workflow helps you move from validated schema to a working back end, so you can build faster without switching tools. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Database for MySQL now available in new regions and expanded availability zones

Body.Content:

You can now deploy Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server in the Denmark East, Austria East, and Belgium Central regions, bringing Azure-managed MySQL closer to your workloads with full support for zone-redundant high availability and geo-redundant backup. These updates reinforce our commitment to providing you with a globally distributed, highly available managed MySQL service. To get started, visit the Azure portal to create or migrate your Azure Database for MySQL Flexible Server in these regions.

Title: Public Preview: Benchmark evaluations for fine-tuned models in Microsoft Foundry

Body.Content:
Choosing the right AI system is rarely as simple as picking the newest or largest model — and agents add their own layer of variability on top. A model that wins on a public leaderboard can still underperform on the reasoning, math, or domain-knowledge questions that matter for your application, and an agent that solves one task well can regress on another after a prompt or tool change. The only way to know is to measure, on the same benchmark, under the same conditions, every time something changes. 

Benchmarks in Microsoft Foundry (preview) make that kind of measurement a first-class part of the development workflow. You can run well-known open-source benchmarks against any model deployment or agent in your project, compare runs side by side in the evaluation group view, and drive the whole flow from the portal or the REST API. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: CLI and SDK support for Deployment Templates

Body.Content:
Deployment templates in Azure Machine Learning add CLI and SDK support in public preview, so platform teams can create, update, delete, and manage templates from infrastructure-as-code pipelines instead of only the portal. The new commands work with az ml deployment-template create, list, show, update, and delete, and the Python SDK exposes the same operations through the azure-ai-ml client. Teams can check deployment templates into Git, review them in pull requests, and manage them through Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions exactly like other Azure resources. They can deploy the model packaged with deployment templates by using az ml online-deployment create or the equivalent operation in the SDK. This enables repeatable, auditable rollouts of standardized model deployments across many projects in an organization without manual portal steps. 

Learn more

Title: Generally Available: Region-agnostic reservations for Global PTU in Microsoft Foundry

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry adds region-agnostic reservations for Global Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) at general availability, letting customers commit to PTU capacity once and consume it from any supported region. Previously, a reserved PTU commitment was tied to a single region, which created friction for customers that operated multi-region applications or wanted to shift workloads as traffic patterns changed. With region-agnostic reservations, finance teams can sign one reservation contract and engineering teams can deploy models in whichever Azure region best fits a given workload, with the reservation discount applied automatically. Reservations cover supported Foundry Models including Azure Direct first-party models such as GPT-5 and GPT-4.1. Existing region-bound reservations continue to honor their original terms. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: OneLake Catalog integration for Foundry IQ Knowledge Sources

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry IQ adds public preview support for OneLake Catalog as a knowledge source, so agents can ground responses on lakehouse tables, files, and shortcuts already governed in Microsoft Fabric. Data engineers register the OneLake catalog once and Foundry IQ ingests the cataloged items, respecting Fabric permissions and sensitivity labels at query time. Analysts get agent answers that cite the same curated datasets used in dashboards and reports, instead of duplicate copies sitting in a separate vector store. The integration removes a common gap between BI data and AI applications, letting customers reuse their Fabric investment for agent grounding. Setup uses the same connection flow as other Foundry IQ knowledge sources. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Image serving in Foundry IQ knowledge bases

Body.Content:
Foundry IQ knowledge bases now surface document-extracted images at query time in public preview. When ingestion pulls figures, screenshots, and diagrams out of PDFs, slides, and Office files, Foundry IQ retains each image alongside the text it appeared with and can return it as part of a retrieval result. Agents can show the original chart to the user instead of describing it secondhand, so answers about technical diagrams, product photos, and report figures stay anchored to the source artwork. Customers building support assistants, internal research tools, and knowledge portals can render visual context inline without building a separate image pipeline. The capability is available across all Foundry IQ-supported document types. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Managed identity for Foundry billing calls from Azure AI Search

Body.Content:
Azure AI Search now supports managed identity authentication for the billing operations it issues against Microsoft Foundry resources, replacing the prior key-based flow. Customers assign a system-assigned or user-assigned identity to the search service, grant it the appropriate role on the Foundry account, and skill executions that call Foundry models for embeddings, chat completions, or extraction bill through that identity. Security teams remove another long-lived secret from their environment, simplify rotation, and gain Entra-based audit trails for cross-service calls. The change is available in all regions where Azure AI Search and Microsoft Foundry are colocated, and applies to indexer skillsets that invoke Foundry models. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: GenAI prompt skill and chat completion in Azure AI Search knowledge sources

Body.Content:
Azure AI Search makes the GenAI prompt skill generally available, letting indexers call chat completion models during enrichment without custom code. Authors point the skill at a Foundry-hosted model, write a prompt template that references field values, and receive structured output written back to the index. The same chat completion capability is also available inside knowledge sources, so retrieval-augmented agents can run a quick model call against retrieved chunks before returning results. Customers use the skill for content classification, summarization, entity normalization, and field cleanup in the ingestion pipeline, replacing prior workflows that required separate functions or Logic Apps. Authentication supports managed identity, so calls stay inside the customer tenant. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Content Understanding extractionMode for documents

Body.Content:

Pick a layout-aware mode for structured documents where tables, sections, and reading order matter, or a faster text-only mode when you only need clean Markdown for downstream RAG indexing. Title: Public Preview: SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer supports ASPX pages and Lists

Body.Content:
The Azure AI Search SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer now indexes ASPX site content and SharePoint Lists in addition to document libraries. The indexer connects through a Microsoft Entra application registration with application or delegated permissions, picks up new and changed items incrementally, and removes deleted items on the next run. Inclusion and exclusion rules let you scope ingestion to specific sites, libraries, lists, or folders, and additional columns can be brought through as searchable fields. The same indexer continues to support basic ACL preservation and Microsoft Purview sensitivity label ingestion in preview.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Microsoft Purview sensitivity label auditing in Azure AI Search

Body.Content:
Azure AI Search now emits audit events for Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels carried alongside indexed documents. When the SharePoint in Microsoft 365 indexer is configured to preserve and honor sensitivity labels, query-time filtering decisions and label changes flow into Microsoft Purview activity logs. Security and compliance teams can review who queried labeled content, when label values changed, and how those changes affected search visibility. The capability builds on the existing sensitivity label ingestion preview and requires no schema changes to existing indexes. Configure auditing through your Microsoft Purview tenant settings. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Photo Avatar standard and custom in Azure AI Speech

Body.Content:
Photo Avatar in Azure AI Speech is now generally available in standard and custom flavors. Standard Photo Avatar produces a talking head video from a single photo at 512x512 resolution, and custom Photo Avatar lets you fine-tune the look from your own image with one minute of consent audio for the matching voice. Both modes run through the same batch synthesis and real-time synthesis APIs already used for video avatars, so existing avatar code paths keep working. Photo Avatar is built on the VASA-1 model family and integrates with Voice Live for low-latency, two-way conversational scenarios where you need a face on the agent. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Adaptive custom translation in the Azure AI Foundry NextGen playground

Body.Content:
Adaptive Custom Translation (AdaptCT) is generally available in the Azure AI Foundry NextGen playground for Azure Translator. AdaptCT enables enterprises to adapt translations to domain‑specific terminology using small datasets—eliminating the need for traditional model retraining. AdaptCT allows developers to update multilingual content in minutes by indexing high‑value examples and applying them dynamically at translation time (few-shot) to ground selected LLM. 

This approach helps organizations: 

  • Launch multilingual product features faster 
  • Maintain terminology consistency across evolving content 
  • Reduce operational overhead for translation workflows 
  • Deliver localized customer experiences at scale 

AdaptCT turns translation into an agile enabler for global growth—supporting real‑time updates across support content, product documentation, and dynamic digital experiences. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure AI Translator SDKs for the latest text translation API

Body.Content:
Azure AI Translator publishes generally available SDKs that target the latest text translation REST API across four languages: C#/.NET, Java, JavaScript, and Python. The SDKs expose Translator API v4 SDK to GA across all four supported programming languages, giving developers a single client surface to choose between traditional neural machine translation and LLM-based translation per request. Teams building multilingual products and support content have had to manage two parallel translation paths, with different SDKs, request shapes, and quality profiles, making it hard to mix models within one workflow. 

With the new SDK, developers can set the translation model, output tone, target gender, and adaptive settings on every call from the same Translator client. The release simplifies integration code, makes feature parity across .NET, Python, Java, and JavaScript clients consistent, and aligns the SDK surface with Translator API v4 capabilities including LLM model selection and the latest adaptive translation features.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Document translation for image files (synchronous, single document)

Body.Content:
Azure AI Translator now supports synchronous single-document image translation at general availability. Customers can submit a standalone image file (JPEG, PNG, and similar formats) through one synchronous API call and receive the translated result immediately, with original layout fidelity preserved. The service combines OCR and translation behind a single endpoint, so teams no longer need to build and maintain a custom OCR plus translation pipeline. Pricing is clear on a per-image basis, and the feature inherits the enterprise security posture and regional coverage of Document Translation. Common scenarios include real-time translation for mobile apps, retail signage, restaurant menus, kiosks, and form-based experiences. Early customers include Stanley Black and Decker, USCIS, and UD Trucks. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Incremental SharePoint permissions sync for Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ

Body.Content:
Azure AI Search and Foundry IQ Knowledge Sources add incremental SharePoint permissions sync in public preview, keeping document-level, site, and library access control lists current as SharePoint permissions change. Enterprises store business-critical content in SharePoint and expect AI-powered search, RAG, and agent experiences to enforce the same access rules. 

Today, carrying SharePoint permissions forward into indexing workflows is partial, so downstream AI experiences can drift from current SharePoint state. With incremental sync, permission updates apply on every indexer run, removing the need for full re-indexing when ACLs change. Supported scopes cover document-level ACLs, site (ASPX) ACLs, and list and library ACLs. SharePoint policy evaluation stays out of scope. Security and compliance teams gain a more reliable foundation for enterprise agents and RAG apps built on SharePoint content. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: MCP Server Knowledge Source in Microsoft Foundry IQ

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry IQ now supports external MCP servers as federated knowledge sources in public preview, expanding retrieval beyond data customers index themselves. Teams can register MCP servers from systems like Salesforce, Atlassian, Confluence, and ServiceNow, then query them alongside indexed sources in a single agentic retrieval call. Foundry IQ handles cross-source selection automatically, choosing which sources to consult per query and merging results with citations. Because the federation uses MCP, partners and customers can plug in any compliant server without building a custom connector. Source-system permissions still gate the data, so an agent only retrieves records the calling user can see. This release helps organizations make agents useful against systems of record without copying data into a separate index. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Trace Replay and trace visualizations for Foundry agents

Body.Content:

The replay view rewinds a captured trace step by step, showing the model, tool, and inter-agent calls in the order they happened along with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage. Updated visualizations group nested spans by agent and tool so engineers can spot the step that introduced an error or a latency spike without scrolling through raw OpenTelemetry data. Traces flow into Azure Monitor Application Insights, so teams keep one observability backend for production AI workloads and the rest of their Azure services. Setup uses the existing Foundry tracing configuration.

Approved customers can upload an actor's video recording, fine-tune a custom video avatar, and generate synthetic talking-head videos through the same Foundry project that runs their text-to-speech and Voice Live workloads. The portal also supports Photo Avatar, where a single reference image plus the Microsoft VASA model produces a head-only avatar. Title: Public Preview: Toolbox connectors and triggers in Microsoft Foundry

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry adds connectors and time-based triggers to the Foundry Tools toolbox in public preview, giving enterprise developers and automation engineers a native way to build event-driven AI agents. Foundry agents today are invoked only through direct API calls or user interactions, leaving teams to build custom orchestration outside Foundry whenever an agent needs to react to a business event. With this release, agents respond automatically to events from Microsoft 365, Azure, and third-party systems, and fire on schedules such as every day at 7am. Developers use the same centrally managed toolbox endpoint for discovery and authentication, while admins retain governance over which connectors and triggers are approved for enterprise use. Reactive, event-driven agent automation now ships without custom orchestration code or per-connector integration work. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Neural HD voice update (HDv2.5) in Azure AI Speech

Body.Content:
Azure AI Speech is rolling out an updated Neural HD text-to-speech model, moving customers from DragonHDLatest to HDv2.5. The update raises audio quality scores, adds style and paralinguistic tag support for English voices, and reduces word error rate in secondary locales such as Spanish, French, German, and Japanese. Customer-facing voice experiences (call center agents, IVR menus, assistant readouts) sound more natural and expressive without changes to the calling code; the existing endpoints and SSML markup continue to work. Speech teams operating multilingual deployments get more consistent quality across markets, which reduces the gap between primary and secondary languages. HDv2.5 is rolling out in public preview across existing Neural HD regions; rollout completes alongside the broader Speech monthly update cycle. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Serverless indexers in Azure AI Search

Body.Content:
Azure AI Search now offers a serverless option for native indexers in public preview, removing the requirement to provision and manage indexer compute for ingestion workflows. Indexer execution scales with workload demand, so customers stop paying for idle capacity during off-peak hours and stop over-provisioning to handle bursts. The MVP supports document ingestion and enrichment patterns commonly used in RAG pipelines, Foundry Knowledge Bases, and AI-driven applications backed by Azure AI Search. Existing native indexer definitions continue to work; customers opt into serverless execution on a per-indexer basis and keep their current data sources, skillsets, and target indexes. The release is aimed at enterprise developers and platform engineers running large or bursty ingestion jobs who want lower operational overhead and usage-aligned cost.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Purview sensitivity labels in Azure AI Search knowledge sources

Body.Content:

Labels applied at the source system flow through ingestion into Azure AI Search and into the knowledge bases that ground Foundry agents and copilots, so chunk retrieval, vector search, and multi-step agent reasoning all respect the same access and privacy classifications defined by enterprise security teams. Title: Generally Available: Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service

Body.Content:
Hosted agents in Foundry Agent Service are now generally available, running on Azure Developer Compute with microVM-level isolation. You bring a container-based agent built with the Microsoft Agent Framework or any third-party SDK, and the platform operates it: no manual start and stop, no always-warm instances to pay for, and no hosting infrastructure to patch. Every agent session executes in its own isolated sandbox with a clean environment and strong compute boundaries between tenants, so there is no shared state or cross-session data leakage, which matters for financial, healthcare, and legal workloads. 

Pre-built snapshots deliver session starts in under 100 milliseconds, Microsoft Entra identity and virtual network support reach internal data and APIs privately, and regional data residency is available across roughly 20 Azure regions. Agents are suspended between conversation turns, so you pay only for active execution. To get started, deploy your container-based agent to Foundry Agent Service. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Foundry Memory preview refresh

Body.Content:
Microsoft Foundry refreshes the Foundry Memory public preview with a redesigned storage model, new retrieval controls, and tighter integration with the Foundry Agent Service tool surface. Agents using Memory can now write, search, and update user-scoped and session-scoped memories through a single tool, with built-in semantic deduplication and TTL controls that keep memory stores from drifting over time. Customers running pilots on the previous Memory preview continue to work; the refresh ships as an opt-in upgrade in the Foundry portal and through the agent tool catalog. The release targets agents that need stable user context across multi-turn and multi-session interactions.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Database PostgreSQL - Flexible Server cross-tenant customer-managed keys

Body.Content:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL - Flexible Server now supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK), in public preview, allowing you to encrypt your data at rest using an Azure Key Vault key that resides in a separate Microsoft Entra tenant from the database service. 


This capability is designed for software as a service (SaaS) providers and enterprises that need to maintain strict separation of duties and ownership of encryption keys, enabling their customers to retain full control over key lifecycle management while PostgreSQL runs in a service provider's tenant. 


With cross-tenant CMK: Your PostgreSQL data is encrypted using a key you own and manage. The database service never has access to your key material. You can rotate or revoke keys at any time without downtime. 


Authentication between PostgreSQL Flexible Server and the customer-owned key vault is handled using federated identity with Microsoft Entra ID access across tenants. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Pre-upgrade validation checks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

Body.Content:
You can now proactively validate Major Version Upgrade (MVU) readiness for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server before initiating the actual upgrade process. New pre-upgrade validation checks allow you to independently run upgrade compatibility validations and identify potential blockers ahead of time, helping reduce failed upgrade attempts and improve operational predictability. 


The validation process checks your server against Azure PostgreSQL upgrade policies and PostgreSQL pg_upgrade -check compatibility requirements. It surfaces actionable guidance for issues such as unsupported extensions, replication slots, prepared transactions, configuration mismatches, and other upgrade constraints. You can resolve identified issues, rerun validations as needed, and proceed with the upgrade only when your environment is ready. 


By shifting validation from inline execution during upgrade to a proactive pre-flight step, this capability helps improve first-time upgrade success rates, reduce troubleshooting effort, and simplify upgrade planning for production workloads.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Oracle schema conversion to Azure PostgreSQL in Visual Studio Code

Body.Content:

Pricing is calculated per image translated, alongside standard character-based pricing for the surrounding document text. Output documents are written to the target container in their translated form for downstream review.

Title: Public Preview: Snapshot backup for SQL Server in Azure VMs

Body.Content:

This new capability uses Azure disk snapshots combined with native SQL transaction log backups to deliver near-instant, low-impact full backups for large SQL databases, significantly improving backup performance and reducing the load on production workloads compared to streaming backups. You can protect multiple databases under a SQL instance with a single policy and restore using different mechanisms with point-in-time recovery enabled by log chaining on top of snapshot recovery points.
All restore points get stored in Azure Recovery Services Vault which provides long term retention and added security for your data in case of Ransomware attacks and any other disasters.

Title: Retirement: Azure VMware Solution AV36 node End of Support now August 30, 2027

Body.Content:
Updated: Microsoft’s support lifecycle is evolving in alignment with VMware’s roadmap. Broadcom will end support for the current AV36 VCF version on September 30, 2027, and the AV36 SKU is not compatible with VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) 9, the next-generation platform.

As part of this transition, and to align with the AVS License-include service retirement, all AV36 SDDCs will be retired after August 30, 2027, regardless of individual RI expiration dates. On August 31, 2027, these SDDCs will no longer be accessible.

Key dates for existing AV36 subscriptions

June 30, 2026 Last day to buy a 1-year RI for AV36 VCF BYOL

August 30, 2027 AV36 SKU Retirement and AVS License-included service retirement

August 31, 2027 AV36 SDDC access will be removed. Microsoft will retain the data for up to 60 days so the customer can retrieve it.

Reach out to your Microsoft Account Team for key dates for AV36 PayGo subscriptions.

Title: Generally Available: Application Gateway for Containers – Service Mesh integration with Istio

Body.Content:
Application Gateway for Containers service mesh integration with Istio is now generally available. This capability simplifies secure north-south traffic into workloads running in an Istio service mesh by automating mutual TLS (mTLS) connectivity between Application Gateway for Containers and mesh-enabled services.  

With general availability, customers can use this integration with both upstream open-source Istio and the Istio-based service mesh add-on for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). This gives teams flexibility to adopt a managed AKS experience while using Application Gateway for Containers as their ingress path for services inside and outside the mesh.  

  • Single ingress solution: Route traffic to services both inside and outside the mesh through one gateway.  
  • Reduced operational overhead: Simplify ingress configuration and avoid repetitive mTLS definitions.  
  • Managed certificate lifecycle: Automate certificate trust and rotation for secure communication with mesh workloads.  
  • Flexible deployment options: Support both upstream Istio and the AKS Istio-based service mesh add-on.  

Learn more:  

  • Application Gateway for Containers + Istio service mesh  
  • Application Gateway for Containers overview  
  • Original public preview announcement

Title: Public Preview: Azure Virtual Network Manager integration with Virtual WAN

Body.Content:
Azure Virtual Network Manager integration with Virtual WAN is now in public preview, enabling you to use an Azure Virtual WAN hub as the hub in Azure Virtual Network Manager hub-and-spoke connectivity configurations, bringing together Azure Virtual Network Manager 's at-scale network management with Virtual WAN's managed routing, security, and hybrid connectivity.

Title: Generally Available: Entra-only identities with Azure Files

Body.Content:
Azure Files announces general availability of Entra-only identities for SMB access, enabling organizations to securely access file shares using cloud-native identities without requiring Active Directory or hybrid identity infrastructure. With Microsoft Entra ID as the authentication authority, users can access Azure Files using Kerberos-based authentication backed entirely by cloud identities - eliminating dependency on domain controllers and simplifying storage and identity architecture.

  • Cloud-native authentication with Entra ID: Secure SMB access using Kerberos without Active Directory or domain controllers 
  • Simplified permissions management: Configure granular NTFS ACLs for Entra users and groups directly through the Azure portal 
  • Role-based access control (RBAC): Assign share-level access using built-in roles for least-privilege administration 
  • Secure access from anywhere: Enable identity-based access over the internet without VPN dependencies 
  • Support for modern workloads: Power Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD), general-purpose file sharing, and distributed collaboration scenarios 

Please reach out to azurefiles@microsoft.com if you have any questions about adopting Entra-only Identities for secure SMB access with Azure Files. 

Learn more.

Title: Retirement: TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 in Azure App Service, Azure Functions, and Azure Logic Apps

Body.Content:
As part of Azure’s ongoing security improvements, App Service, Functions, and Logic Apps will no longer accept connections using TLS 1.0 or TLS 1.1 after May 31, 2027. View the resources in your subscription that still allow TLS 1.0 or 1.1 in the Azure Retirement Workbook.

Next steps 

Test client compatibility with TLS 1.2 or later. Review the TLS version deprecation overview for configuration guidance and see the service‑specific Q&A links below for common questions.

Title: Public Preview: TLS/SSL certificate support for Azure Functions Flex Consumption

Body.Content:
Flex Consumption introduces a site-scoped certificate model in public preview in all the regions where Flex Consumption is available. Unlike webspace-scoped certificates on other hosting plans which are shared across apps in the same region + resource group, Flex certificates are scoped to an individual function app. 

Each function app can hold up to 3 private (.pfx) and 3 public (.cer) certificates uploaded directly, imported from Azure Key Vault, or issued as free App Service Managed Certificates to enable custom domains, client-certificate authentication, and mutual TLS scenarios on Flex Consumption. 

To access certificates from code Flex Consumption uses a per-certificate "Accessible to app code" toggle in the portal instead of the WEBSITE_LOAD_CERTIFICATES app setting used on other plans. Because Flex Consumption runs on Linux, code reads certificates from file paths (/var/ssl/certs for public, /var/ssl/private for private) rather than from a Windows certificate store.  

Currently, the Azure portal is the recommended path for configuring certificates during preview. Apps migrating from another plan should add their certificates to the new Flex Consumption app rather than carrying webspace-scoped certificates across.  

Learn more: 

  • Configure site-scoped certificates  
  • Infrastructure as code instructions  
  • Cross-plan certificate comparison

Title: Generally Available: Schedule one-time or recurring migrations with Azure Storage Mover

Body.Content:
Azure Storage Mover now supports built-in job scheduling, giving customers more control over when migrations run and making it easier to automate repeatable data transfers into Azure. Customers can configure jobs to start automatically at a specific date and time, or set up recurring runs to keep their target storage in sync with data from on-premises environments.

In the portal, customers can choose No schedule, a one-time schedule, or a recurring schedule. Recurring schedules support daily, weekly, and monthly frequency options. Schedules can also be enabled or disabled as needed, giving teams flexibility to align migrations with maintenance windows, business operations, or phased cutover plans. 

Scheduling is designed to help teams reduce manual intervention while improving operational consistency for ongoing migrations and sync scenarios. This capability is positioned for scenarios such as off-hours movement, staged cutovers, and incremental syncs before final migration completion.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: site-to-site VPN connections with certificate authentication

Body.Content:
Azure Site-to-Site VPN with digital certificate authentication provides an alternative to the traditional pre-shared key (PSK) model by using a certificate-based asymmetric trust model. In this configuration, Azure and the on-premises VPN device authenticate each other by using separate inbound and outbound certificates. The outbound authentication certificate is stored in Azure Key Vault and is accessed by the VPN Gateway through a user-assigned managed identity with the required Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) permissions. Because X.509 certificates use asymmetric keys and a trusted certificate chain to validate identity, this approach helps reduce the risk of impersonation and Internet Key Exchange (IKE) negotiation tampering. 

Learn more.
