Title: Public Preview: Customer‑managed encryption keys now supported on Premium SSD v2 disks for Azure Database for PostgreSQL

Body.Content:
You can now enhance data security for your Azure Database for PostgreSQL workloads by using customer managed keys (CMKs) with Premium SSD v2 disks. Available in public preview, this update gives you greater control over how your data at rest is encrypted, allowing you to use your own keys stored in Azure Key Vault while continuing to take advantage of the high performance and scalability of Premium SSD v2 storage. CMKs are especially valuable if you operate in regulated industries or need to meet internal compliance requirements that specify customer‑controlled encryption and separation of duties. 

With this preview, you can manage key rotation and access policies according to your organization’s standards, while Azure continues to handle the underlying database operations and performance optimization. The result is a stronger security posture without compromising performance, availability, or ease of management for your PostgreSQL deployments on Azure.   

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL dashboards with Grafana

Body.Content:
You can now monitor your Azure Database for PostgreSQL with rich, built-in Grafana dashboards—right from the Azure portal. This native integration with Azure Monitor means you no longer need to set up or manage a separate Grafana instance to get deep visibility into your database performance. 

With just a few clicks, you can see prebuilt dashboards showing real-time metrics like CPU usage, storage, active connections, query throughput, and more. You can also correlate metrics with PostgreSQL logs, helping you troubleshoot slow queries and spikes instantly. Grafana Explore is available too, so you can dive deeper into your data when needed. 

These dashboards help you answer critical questions faster: Is my database healthy? What’s causing performance issues? Do I need to scale? You can customize dashboards, save them to your subscription, and share them across teams. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Query Profiler in MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code

Body.Content:
The MSSQL extension for Visual Studio Code now introduces Query Profiler in public preview, bringing real-time insight into your database activity directly inside Visual Studio Code. With Query Profiler, you can capture query and database activity as it happens, helping you quickly understand what your app and backend processes are doing, identify slow operations, and spot performance bottlenecks while you build. Powered by Extended Events, Query Profiler delivers low-overhead performance monitoring designed to minimize impact on your database. 

Query Profiler supports SQL Server (on-premises or in private or public cloud environments) and Azure SQL Database. You can monitor active sessions, review execution details, and better understand how your application interacts with your database during development and testing. Instead of switching between monitoring tools and your editor, you get a streamlined, developer-focused profiling experience integrated with your existing connections and query workflow. 

Whether you are debugging performance issues or validating changes before deployment, Query Profiler gives you clear, actionable insight into what your database is doing in real time. This public preview allows you to explore the experience early and share feedback. 
Learn more.

Title: Retirement: Azure Policy faster enforcement and retirement of login/logout workaround

Body.Content:
Over the years, we’ve made significant investments to improve the responsiveness of the Azure Policy service. As a result, policy assignment creation and updates for Resource Manager mode policies now get enforced within 5 minutes.

Title: Generally Available: Draft & Deploy on Azure Firewall

Body.Content:
The new Draft & Deploy feature for Azure Firewall Policy introduces a streamlined, two-phase approach to managing firewall policies, significantly reducing deployment time and disruption. Traditionally, any policy update would trigger a full deployment of both the policy and the attached firewall, taking 2–4 minutes per change.   

With Draft & Deploy, users can collaboratively make multiple changes in a draft version cloned from the current policy without affecting the live environment. Once finalized, all changes can be deployed at once, replacing the existing policy.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Databricks Lakebase

Body.Content:
Today we’re announcing the General Availability of Azure Databricks Lakebase, a managed PostgreSQL environment with next generation separation of storage and compute for OLTP, providing instant availability, instant clones, and scale-to-zero. Lakebase lets you build intelligent, transactional applications and AI agents on the same governed data foundation you already use for analytics, BI, and machine learning in Azure Databricks. 


With Lakebase, operational data is written directly to lakehouse storage instead of siloed OLTP systems and shadow databases. This eliminates brittle ETL pipelines, reduces data duplication, and enables real‑time insights and AI on fresh operational data without complex data movement. 


Developers can use familiar Postgres tools and libraries while Azure handles security, identity, networking, and compliance. Lakebase offers autoscaling, scale‑to‑zero, point‑in‑time recovery, and instant database branching so teams can move faster from prototype to production while maintaining enterprise‑grade reliability. 


Running on Azure Databricks, Lakebase unifies operational and analytical workloads on open data formats, making it easier to power AI‑driven customer experiences, real‑time operational analytics, and modern line‑of‑business applications—all with the global scale and enterprise trust of the Microsoft cloud. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Restrict usage of user delegation SAS to an Entra ID identity

Body.Content:
We’re excited to announce the addition of enhanced secure authentication in Azure Storage that combines the flexibility of user-delegation shared access signature (SAS) with the user-bound access of Entra ID. User-bound user delegation SAS is now in preview for all regions. 

 

User delegation SAS is an existing feature that allows users to create secure SAS tokens that are tied to the delegator, meaning the delegator must verify their identity with Entra to create the token. The resulting token can be traced to the delegator and can only be valid for up to 7 days. This feature is an extension of user delegation (UD) SAS, which is already generally available for Azure Blobs and in public preview for Azure Files, Azure Tables, and Azure Queues. User-bound user delegation SAS allows users to create a more secure SAS token than account SAS, service SAS, or normal user delegation SAS by restricting the usage of the SAS token to an end user identity. This will help enforce that the user delegated SAS can only be used by intended users. 

 

There is no additional cost to use user-bound user delegation SAS. Pricing is based on the standard read/write transaction costs for your storage account type. To learn more, please see Azure Storage Pricing. 

 

This preview is available in all public regions.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Secure ingestion and pod placement for Azure Monitor pipeline

Body.Content:
We are announcing several capabilities in public preview with Azure Monitor pipeline. 


  • Secure Ingress to Azure Monitor pipeline from external endpoints (TLS/mTLS) with Bring Your Own Certificates: BYOC empowers enterprises to maintain control and flexibility over certificate management, meeting regulatory and security requirements while integrating with existing PKI infrastructure. With this release, Azure Monitor pipeline supports both TLS and mutual TLS (mTLS) for TCP-based receivers, allowing customers to:  
    • Configure mTLS with their own certificates for client and server authentication  
    • Configure TLS with their own server certificates and client CA certificate 
  • Pod placement: Azure Monitor pipeline provides native controls for managing how Azure Monitor pipeline instances are scheduled across Kubernetes cluster nodes. The execution Placement configuration allows customers to:  
    • Target specific nodes based on their capabilities (e.g., high-resource nodes, specific zones)  
    • Control instance distribution to prevent resource contention  
    • Enforce isolation policies for high-scale deployments 

Learn more:  

  • Azure Monitor pipeline TLS configuration  
  • Azure Monitor pipeline pod placement

Title: Retirement: Windows Server Annual Channel (preview)

Body.Content:
Windows Server Annual Channel (Preview) on AKS will be retired on May 15, 2026, please transition to Long Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) by that date.  We encourage you to transition to Long Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) prior to the retirement date to experience the benefits of LTSC including longer support cycles and increased stability.  

From now to May 15, 2026 you can continue to use Windows Server Annual Channel (Preview) without disruption. On May 15, 2026, AKS will no longer produce new Windows Server Annual Channel node images or provide security patches. Required Action: Customers must migrate their Windows Server Annual Channel node pools to Long Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) by following the migration guide.

Migration guidance is available in the Azure Functions documentation.  

Learn more:

Title: Generally Available: Instant access support for incremental snapshots of Azure Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk

Body.Content:
Announcing the General Availability of instant access support for incremental snapshots of Premium SSD v2 (Pv2) and Ultra Disk. This new capability enables you to restore new disks immediately after creating snapshots of Pv2 and Ultra disks. Newly restored disks deliver high performance instantly, while data hydration continues rapidly in the background.  

Instant access snapshots accelerate backup and recovery workflows, enabling faster environment refreshes and rapid scaling. Common use cases include:  

  • Create instant backups before software updates and revert quickly if needed.  
  • Quickly scale stateful applications by creating multiple copies of primary data for new instances, such as adding read-only SQL Server replicas.  
  • Rapid nightly refresh of training or testing environments from the production. 

Instant access support for incremental snapshots of Pv2 and Ultra Disk is available in all public regions where Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk are supported. For pricing details, please visit Managed Disk Pricing. 

Learn more: 

  • Watch the demo 

  • Get started by creating instant access snapshots for your Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disk here.

Title: Private Preview: Vaulted Backups for Azure Disk

Body.Content:
Today, Azure Disk Backup protects data by taking regular, crash-consistent snapshots of Azure Disks. These snapshots are stored within your subscription and tenant in a resource group, referred to as the Operational Tier in Azure Backup. This enables fast, operational recovery for scenarios such as accidental deletion or data corruption and is commonly used alongside Azure VM Backup, which provides application-aware protection for virtual machines.  

Backup best practices recommend a 3-2-1 strategy, including storing a copy of backups offsite in an isolated location securing against a tenant-level compromise. 

With the introduction of Vault Tier backups, Azure Disk Backup now complements Azure VM Backup by extending disk-level protection with vault-based isolation, independent access controls, and immutability. This enables recovery of trusted data during ransomware attacks or tenant compromises, bringing disk backups in line with Azure VM Backup grade cyber-recovery security.  

As part of this Private Preview, Azure Disk Backup introduces two key capabilities: 

  • Vault Tier Backup: Protect disk backups in a vault (offsite) to meet cyber-recovery, ransomware resilience, and compliance requirements. 

  • Regional Disaster Recovery: Restore disk backups to a paired Azure region, enabling new disaster-recovery scenarios alongside Azure VM Backup and Azure Site Recovery. 

If you’re interested in participating, sign up for the Private Preview here.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Monitor pipeline transformations

Body.Content:
Azure Monitor pipeline transformations feature is now Public Preview! This feature enables users to shape telemetry before it’s ingested into Azure Monitor, helping them control ingestion costs, improve data quality, and simplify analytics at scale.

Built into the Azure Monitor pipeline for edge and multi-cloud environments, transformations allow data types such as Syslog and CEF to be filtered, aggregated, standardized, and reshaped prior to ingestion. Automatic schema standardization and built-in validation guardrails ensure continued compatibility with standard tables, allowing users to apply transformations confidently without disrupting dataflow.

Transformations also include prebuilt KQL templates for common scenarios, along with advanced filtering and aggregation to reduce noise, lower ingestion volume, and summarize high frequency data into meaningful time windows. By shaping data closer to the source, Azure Monitor pipeline transformations deliver cleaner data and faster insights for high volume and complex telemetry environments.

  • Azure Monitor pipeline transformations demo

Title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files Elastic zone-redundant service level

Body.Content:
Azure NetApp Files Elastic zone-redundant storage (ANF Elastic ZRS) is an advanced high-availability service level for Azure NetApp Files that provides continuous data access with zero data loss, even if an entire Azure Availability Zone goes offline. Built on Azure’s Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) architecture and compute infrastructure, ANF Elastic ZRS synchronously replicates file data across availability zones within one region. By eliminating single points of failure, it ensures mission-critical workloads remain online and protected without requiring special configuration or manual intervention. This makes it ideal for applications that demand uncompromising resilience and in-region data protection. 

Azure NetApp Files Elastic ZRS provides consistent performance for metadata-heavy workloads across VMs and containers, making it well suited for AI, analytics, and Kubernetes/OpenShift environments. Whether you’re running mission critical workloads, AKS and containerized apps, cloud‑native applications, or general file shares, Azure NetApp Files Elastic ZRS delivers continuity without compromise, cost‑effective scalability, and operational simplicity. You can create volumes as small as 1 GiB, giving you the flexibility to optimize storage for workloads of any size. 

This new service is in Preview in these regions and we will be rapidly expanding.

Learn more: 

  • Understand Elastic zone-redundant storage service level
  • Create a NetApp Elastic account in Azure NetApp Files

Title: Generally Available: Azure Container Storage v2.1.0 now with Elastic SAN integration and on demand installation

Body.Content:
Azure Container Storage v2.1.0 is now generally available. This release adds native Elastic SAN support and introduces a lightweight, on-demand installation model to simplify deployment and operations for Kubernetes workloads on Azure. 

Elastic SAN Storage Type Support

With full support for Elastic SAN as a native storage type, you can provision scalable volume groups and consolidate large number of Kubernetes volumes under a single SAN resource, enabling faster attach and detach operations, higher throughput, and reduced management overhead for stateful workloads. The release also includes streamlined setup, improved defaults, and enhanced automation for Elastic SAN creation and volume group configuration.

On demand, modular Installation

Azure Container Storage v2.1.0 now supports modular, on-demand installation, allowing you to deploy only the components required for your selected storage type. This reduces cluster footprint, accelerates deployment, and simplifies lifecycle management.


Node Selector Support for component placement

Additionally, node selectors support enables precise control over where Azure Container Storage components run, helping optimize performance and resource usage in clusters with dedicated storage node pools or mixed topologies.

Title: Public Preview: X-Forwarded-For (XFF) grouping for rate limiting on Application Gateway WAF v2

The capability integrates with existing Application Gateway WAF v2 custom rate‑limit rules and policies.

Title: Retirement: Azure Front Door and Azure CDN profiles will end support for DHE cipher suites on April 1, 2026

Body.Content:
As part of our ongoing commitment to security, Azure Front Door (Standard, Premium, Classic) and Azure CDN from Microsoft (Classic) services will no longer support  weak cipher suites TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 and TLS_DHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256 on April 1 2026 for both ‘client to service’ connections and ‘service to origin’ connections.

Required action

To ensure uninterrupted service and maintain strong encryption standards, take the following actions:

  1. Update your origins to disable DHE ciphers and use any of the recommended cipher suites. Follow our documentation to see how to update cipher suites for some of the common origin types used with Azure Front Door/Azure CDN.
  2. Inform your clients to only use the recommended ciphers while connecting to your domains hosted on Azure Front Door/Azure CDN. If you own any of the clients, update them to use the recommended ciphers.
  3. For Front Door Standard/Premium profiles, you can also use the Configure Azure Front Door TLS policy feature to disable the DHE ciphers in advance before 1 April 2026. For all Front Door (Standard, Premium, Classic) and Azure CDN from Microsoft (Classic) profiles, we will disable the DHE ciphers after April 1 2026.

Help and support

For more information and guidance regarding DHE cipher retire, refer to our documentation.

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and need technical help, please submit a support request .

Title: Generally Available: Default Ruleset 2.2 in WAF for Azure Application Gateway

Body.Content:
Announcing the general availability of Default Rule Set (DRS) 2.2 for Web Application Firewall on Azure Application Gateway.

The Azure-managed DRS provides active protection against common web vulnerabilities and exploits. It also includes Microsoft Threat Intelligence collection rules, authored in collaboration with our intelligence teams, to deliver broader coverage, targeted vulnerability mitigations, and continual improvements in false-positive reduction.

DRS 2.2 is based on OWASP Core Rule Set 3.3.4, bringing refinements to existing detections and new protections, including rules that detect content types declared outside the actual content-type header and enhanced remote code execution (RCE) detections. An additional eight Microsoft Threat Intelligence rules expand coverage across SQL injection, XSS, and application-security attack patterns.

To significantly reduce legitimate traffic being blocked, DRS 2.2 ships at Paranoia Level (PL) 1 by default. PL1 includes high-signal, lower-noise rules that rarely trigger false positives. PL2 rules are disabled by default because they are more aggressive and typically require fine-tuning. You can keep PL2 disabled or selectively enable individual PL2 rules where warranted. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Ubuntu 24.04 support in AKS

Body.Content:
Customers upgrading AKS clusters often need a clear and flexible path to adopt new OS versions without disrupting workloads. Ubuntu 24.04 is now generally available on AKS starting with Kubernetes version 1.32, with containerd 2.0 enabled by default.  

It can be enabled using the new Ubuntu2404 OS SKU in Kubernetes 1.32 and above, or by using the standard Ubuntu OS SKU in Kubernetes 1.35 and above, where Ubuntu 24.04 becomes the default.  

Existing clusters already using the Ubuntu OS SKU will automatically migrate to Ubuntu 24.04 when upgraded to Kubernetes 1.35 or later.  

For rollback or testing scenarios, AKS also now supports the Ubuntu2204 OS SKU across Kubernetes versions 1.25 through 1.36, allowing practitioners to switch OS versions without requiring a Kubernetes version change. These options provide more control over OS lifecycle management and simplify migration planning for cluster operators. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: User delegation SAS for Azure Tables, Azure Files, and Azure Queues

Body.Content:
User delegation SAS for Azure Tables, Azure Files, and Azure Queues is now available in public preview. User delegation (UDK) SAS is already generally available for blobs, and this release extends that support to tables, files, and queues.


User delegation SAS allows users to create a more secure SAS token than account or service SAS by tying the SAS token to the delegator. This extension of UDK SAS will allow users to set SAS tokens at the table, table entity, queue, queue entity, file container, and individual file level. Any SAS token set at the higher level will provide access to all table/queue/file entities within, and any SAS token set at the base level will only provide access to that individual entity.

 

There is no additional cost to use user delegation SAS. Pricing is based on the standard read/write transaction costs for your storage account type. To learn more, please see Azure Storage Pricing.

 

This preview is available in all public regions.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Geo-Replication for Azure Service Bus Premium

Body.Content:
The Geo-Replication feature for Azure Service Bus in the premium tier is now generally available. The Service Bus Geo-Replication feature is one of the options to insulate Azure Service Bus applications against outages and disasters, providing replication of both metadata (entities, configuration, properties) and data (message data and message property / state changes).  

The Geo-Replication feature ensures that the metadata and data of a namespace are continuously replicated from a primary region to one or more secondary regions. Moreover, it allows promoting any secondary region to primary, at any time.   

Promoting a secondary repoints the endpoint for the namespace to the selected secondary region and switches the roles between the primary and secondary region. The promotion is nearly instantaneous once initiated and doesn’t require any changes on the client side.  

More information on this feature can be found in the documentation.

Title: Retirement: Deprecation of Custom Resource Providers

Body.Content:
In 2026, Azure Resource Manager will be deprecating the Custom Resource Provider (CuRP) service.

We will retire the feature by October 31, 2026. We will be performing a scream test on October 27, 2025, as part of this deprecation. On July 31, 2026, creates, updates, patches, and actions to custom resources and resource providers will be blocked. You will only be able to read and delete your custom resources and resource providers.

We understand that this deprecation may be an inconvenience to you and your team. Here are some potential CuRP alternatives you can use to support your existing workflows.

If your CuRP scenario:

  • Only involves triggering an endpoint without the need for persistent resource management, consider Deployment Scripts.
  • Only involves triggering an endpoint without the need for persistent resource management, and you use Bicep, consider Bicep Extensions.
  • Involves triggering several different endpoints or services for your solution, consider Azure Functions.

If you have any questions, please ask your Microsoft account manager to email curpdeprecation@microsoft.com with your name, company name, email contact, and subscription ID.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Blob-to-Blob migration made simple with Azure Storage Mover

Body.Content:
Azure Storage Mover’s new Azure Blob container-to-container migration feature is now in Public Preview, empowering organizations to move data between two Blob containers within the same or different storage accounts, subscriptions or Azure regions securely, reliably, and at scale. With this release, customers can eliminate manual pipelines and tools, automate migrations in the Azure portal, and gain real-time visibility into every job. 

Key benefits: 

1. Fully Managed and Scalable 

Azure Storage Mover is a fully managed service, meaning Microsoft handles the infrastructure, scaling, and reliability. This reduces operational overhead and ensures consistent performance across large-scale transfers. 

2. No Agent Required 

Unlike on-premises migrations, cloud-to-cloud transfers do not require deploying an agent. This simplifies setup and reduces the need for additional compute resources. 

3. High-Speed, Parallel Transfers 

Storage Mover supports parallel file transfers, enabling faster migration of large datasets. This is particularly useful when moving data across regions or between storage accounts with high throughput requirements. 

Get started today and simplify your cloud data estate with Azure Storage Mover’s Blob-to-Blob migration. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection

Body.Content:
Azure NetApp Files advanced ransomware protection (ANF ARP) is now in Public Preview.  ANF ARP is designed to help organizations proactively detect, respond to, and recover from ransomware threats on cloud volumes. ANF ARP monitors Azure NetApp Files volumes for suspicious activity using file extension profiling, entropy, and IOPS patterns. When a threat is detected, the system creates a point-in-time snapshot, enabling rapid evaluation and recovery. Notifications are sent via Azure Activity log and attack reports are retained for 30 days. There is no specific additional charge for ANF ARP but see Considerations section when sizing your deployment to accommodate ANF ARP.

Title: Update: The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026.

Body.Content:
The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026. This change aligns with the broader Azure Virtual Network (VNet) update and replaces the previously communicated September 30, 2025 date. 

Starting March 31, 2026, newly created VNets will default to using private subnets. This means: 

  • Explicit outbound connectivity (e.g., via NAT Gateway, UDR, or other methods) must be configured to access public endpoints on the Internet or Microsoft services. 

  • Default outbound access will be disabled by default, but not removed. Customers who do not configure an outbound method will lose internet connectivity from their Batch nodes. 

  • Review your current Batch pool configurations, especially those using simplified node communication without public IPs.

  • Plan to implement an explicit outbound method before the March 2026 deadline. 

Learn more:

  • Read Default Internet outbound access for Simplified node communication Batch pools without public IP addresses will be retired on 30 September 2025.

  • Read How and when default outbound access is provided

  • Read Feature Update: Default behavior for newly created virtual networks will be private

The retirement date for default outbound access has been extended to March 31, 2026 . This change aligns with the broader Azure Virtual Network (VNet) update and replaces the previously communicated September 30, 2025 date.

Starting March 31, 2026 , newly created VNets will default to using private subnets . This means:

Explicit outbound connectivity (e.g., via NAT Gateway, UDR, or other methods) must be configured to access public endpoints on the Internet or Microsoft services.

Default outbound access will be disabled by default , but not removed. Customers who do not configure an outbound method will lose internet connectivity from their Batch nodes.

Review your current Batch pool configurations, especially those using simplified node communication without public IPs.

Plan to implement an explicit outbound method before the March 2026 deadline.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Blob Storage SFTP - Resumable Uploads

Body.Content:
Announcing the general availability of resumable uploads for Azure Storage Blob SFTP. In the event of a failed partial transfer, this new feature enables users to open the partial file and continue writing the remaining content. This capability optimizes time and conserves network bandwidth, especially in situations where network interruptions occur during file transfers, such as in remote areas with low connectivity or when transferring large files like multimedia or seismic data etc.  

Resume Upload  

The resumable upload feature for Azure Blob Storage SFTP is now generally available. This feature allows users to resume file uploads from the point of failure in the event of partial transfer failures, thereby saving time and reducing network bandwidth usage.  

Learn more. 

The SFTP transfer modes that Azure Blob Storage SFTP supports are below: 

  • Write: This mode lets the client continue an upload by adding data to an existing file from a specific point without creating a new file.  
  • Write + Create: This mode allows the client to resume an upload by either adding to an existing file or creating a new one if it doesn't exist, providing flexibility when the file may not be present initially.  
  • Append: This mode adds data to the end of an existing file without overwriting its current contents.  

Resumable upload enhances efficiency by saving time and bandwidth during interrupted file transfers. Please reach out to blobsftp@microsoft.com for feedback about SFTP for Azure Blob Storage.

Title: Retirement: Remove dependency on these Azure ML SDKs before June 30, 2026

Body.Content:
On June 30, 2026, AzureML SDK V1 will reach end of life. The following SDKs which work in tandem with the AzureML SDK V1 will also be retired.  

  • azureml-train-core  

  • azureml-pipeline  

  • azureml-pipeline-core  

  • azureml-pipeline-internal  

  • azureml-pipeline-steps  

After June 30, 2026, you can continue to use these SDKs, however they will not be supported and may stop working without notice.  

Recommended action  

To ensure that you are using a supported SDK for your workloads, it is recommended to migrate to AzureML SDK V1 before 30 Jun 2026.  

Detailed guidance is documented here.

Help and support  

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support case.  

Links provided herein may take you to a third-party website and are provided for convenience only. Third-party websites are subject to the third-party's terms and privacy statements.  

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

These features make it easier to secure, manage, and consume APIs in a way that supports advanced use cases like AI integrations, all while improving security and governance.

Title: Public Preview: Managed Identity support in Network Watcher VNET flow log, traffic analytics and packet capture

Traffic Analytics leverages VNET flow logs and aggregates, processes and enriches the flows to analyze traffic flow and offers insights into network activity, visualization, security, and performance. 

Network Watcher packet capture enables the capture of network packets directly from a virtual machine, helping users perform deep network analysis and diagnose issues. 

Managed identities provided by Microsoft Entra ID enables VNET flow logs and traffic analytics to securely access Azure Blob Storage and log analytics workspace respectively without the need to manage credentials. For more information, see What is managed identities for Azure resources. 

After you enable managed identity for Network Watcher VNET flow logs, traffic analytics, or packet capture by granting the managed identity necessary permissions will use the managed identity to obtain an access token from Microsoft Entra ID for accessing the specified resource.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure MCP Server for Azure Database for MySQL

Body.Content:
Announcing that Azure MCP Server now supports Azure Database for MySQL. With this update, you can empower AI agents and applications to interact with your MySQL data using natural language through the open Model Context Protocol (MCP). By integrating MySQL tools into the Azure MCP Server alongside other services such as Azure AI Search, Azure Cosmos DB, and Azure Storage, you gain a unified interface for building intelligent, context-aware workflows. This consistency reduces integration complexity, accelerates development, and enables you to create agentic solutions that span data exploration, analysis, and operational actions—all within the trusted Azure ecosystem. 

 

You benefit from faster insights, simplified schema discovery, and the ability to automate MySQL-driven business logic without leaving your development environment. 

 

Get started today by installing Azure MCP Server in Visual Studio Code, enabling GitHub Copilot, and setting up Microsoft Entra authentication for Azure Database for MySQL. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Custom handler support in Azure Functions Flex consumption

Body.Content:
Azure Functions now supports custom handlers in Flex consumption. Custom handlers are lightweight web servers that receive events from the Functions host. Any language that supports HTTP primitives can implement a custom handler. 

 

Custom handlers are best suited for situations where you want to: 

  • Implement a function app in a language that's not currently offered out-of-the box, such as Go or Rust. 
  • Implement a function app in a runtime that's not currently featured by default, such as Deno.  

With custom handlers, you can use triggers and input and output bindings via extension bundles. 

Learn more:

  • Get started with Azure Functions custom handlers with quickstarts in Go and Rust.
  • Review the documentation.

Title: Retirement: Migrate to dedicated VM for your compute clusters

Title: Public Preview: Container network metrics filtering in Advanced Container Networking Services for (ACNS) for AKS

Body.Content:
Container network metrics filtering in Azure Container Networking Services (ACNS) is now available in public preview.

 

In containerized environments, the ingestion of excessive network metrics can lead to inflated storage costs and cluttered dashboards, making it difficult to maintain observability efficiency. Azure Container Networking Services (ACNS) now offers container network metrics filtering, available in public preview, to address this challenge. 

This new capability enables users to define fine-grained filters at the Cilium level using a Custom Resource Definition (CRD), allowing metrics collection to be scoped by namespace or pod. By filtering metrics before they reach Prometheus, organizations can significantly reduce data volume, lower operational overhead, and improve the clarity of their observability tools.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: 20 MB/s/TiB Performance Tier for Azure Managed Lustre

Body.Content:
Azure Managed Lustre now offers a new 20 MB/s/TiB performance tier in public preview, designed to meet the demands of large-scale AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. This tier enables customers to provision file systems up to 25 PiB in a single namespace, delivering up to 512 GB/s of bandwidth and supporting up to 20 billion inodes for massive file counts.

The 20 MB/s/TiB tier uses Lustre’s DNE2 multi-MDS architecture, adding one MDS per 5 PiB to enable directory striping across multiple metadata targets. This boosts metadata operations, delivering over 5× higher IOPS in mdtest benchmarks as striping scales. Ideal for AI training and HPC workloads, it ensures high metadata throughput and efficient handling of massive datasets.

By offering a lower bandwidth density option, customers can optimize costs while scaling to larger namespaces, consolidating workloads into a single, high-performance file system and simplifying their architecture.

To request access to the public preview, please fill out this form.

Title: Generally Available: CSI Dynamic Provisioning for Azure Managed Lustre

Body.Content:
CSI Dynamic Provisioning for Azure Managed Lustre (AMLFS) is now generally available. With dynamic provisioning, Kubernetes applications can request AMLFS-backed persistent volumes on demand using standard StorageClass and PersistentVolumeClaim objects—no pre‑provisioning of volumes is required. This simplifies day-to-day operations for AI/ML training, simulation, and high‑throughput analytics that rely on POSIX file semantics and shared access at scale.

This GA supports Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters running Kubernetes 1.21 and later and uses the Azure Lustre CSI driver. Dynamic provisioning is supported in driver version v0.3.0 and later. Node pools must use the Ubuntu Linux OS SKU.

Administrators define a StorageClass that references an AMLFS file system; developers then bind PVCs to create AMLFS volumes automatically. The driver integrates with the AMLFS client (Lustre 2.15.x) and follows the Kubernetes CSI specification.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Auto-import for Azure Managed Lustre

Body.Content:
The Auto-import feature for Azure Managed Lustre (AMLFS) is now available in public preview. Auto-import enables seamless, policy-driven synchronization of data from Azure Blob Storage containers into AMLFS clusters, automatically reflecting new, changed, or deleted blobs in the Lustre namespace. This feature supports hybrid workflows where data is generated in Blob and consumed in AMLFS.

Customers can configure import policies per Blob container–AMLFS cluster pair, specifying which types of changes are imported and how conflicts are resolved. This flexibility supports a range of scenarios, including post-deployment ingestion, machine learning pipelines, and continuous data synchronization for analytics workloads. Auto-import helps unify object and file-based workflows, enabling near real-time data sharing and reducing operational overhead by eliminating the need for manual import scripts or intermediate file servers.

Operational efficiency is further enhanced by allowing customers to select conflict resolution policies and control whether deletions in Blob are reflected in AMLFS. These capabilities provide native integration with Azure Blob Storage and the Azure ecosystem.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: TLS and TCP termination on Azure Application Gateway

Body.Content:
Azure Application Gateway has introduced general availability support for TLS and TCP protocol termination. This enhancement enables you to load balance and securely process non-HTTP(S) traffic for applications that rely on TCP or TLS protocols. The gateway terminates the incoming connection at the proxy and establishes a new connection to the backend servers. The TLS certificate management is available for both HTTPS and TLS protocols on a resource, simplifying the certificate operations and providing a single endpoint for clients. 

With this release, the TLS/TCP proxy also brings support for Client IP preservation using the PROXY protocol header, as well as support for port 22 on listeners. 

This capability is available on Application Gateway Standard v2 and WAF v2 SKUs. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Managed Instance on Azure App Service

Body.Content:
Announcing Managed Instance on Azure App Service, now in Public Preview! This new capability makes it easy to move web apps to the cloud with minimal configuration—no code rewrites required. Whether your .NET apps run on-premises or in VMs, you can move to a fully managed PaaS environment, future-proof your infrastructure, and unlock cloud benefits.

Why Managed Instance?

Many organizations still rely on older .NET apps for critical tasks like billing, HR, compliance, and reporting. These apps often depend on Windows-specific features and custom tools, which makes rewriting them expensive and risky. With Managed Instance on Azure App Service, they can keep operating with critical dependencies on local Windows services, third-party vendor libraries, and custom runtimes without requiring any code changes. The result is faster app modernization with lower overhead, and access to cloud-native scalability, built-in security and Azure’s AI capabilities.

Key Benefits:

  • Full App Service experience with turnkey scaling, resiliency, and integrated services.
  • Greater control via RDP access through Bastion, custom configurations, and identity management.
  • Compatibility for complex workloads, including classic .NET Framework apps, without code changes.

As part of a holistic migration and modernization strategy, Managed Instance simplifies app modernization, reduces costs, and accelerates your journey to the cloud.

Title: Public Preview: Smart Tier account level tiering (Azure Blob Storage and ADLS)

Body.Content:
Introducing smart tier Public Preview for account level tiering 

Announcing the public preview of smart tier for Azure Blob Storage and Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS). Smart tier is a fully managed and automated data tiering solution, avoiding manual tier placement for object storage standard online tiers. 

Smart tier automatically moves your data between hot, cool, and cold access tiers based on usage patterns, optimizing your costs for these access tiers automatically. New data is stored in the hot tier. Any object that isn’t accessed for 30 days is moved to the cool tier; after 90 days of inactivity, it transitions to the cold tier. If objects are accessed, they are transitioning back to the hot tier and restart their tiering cycle. 

Key Capabilities 

  • Seamless Enablement: Activate smart tier at the storage account scope on new and existing general purpose v2 storage accounts with zonal redundancies today.  
  • Automated Lifecycle: Data movement between tiers is fully automated. Smart tier ensures optimal tier placement for both your active and inactive objects.
  • Simplified Billing Model: Your data uses the existing hot, cool and cold tier capacity prices. There are no charges for tier transitions inside smart tier, early deletion or data retrieval fees. A monitoring fee Is charged for objects stored in smart tier over 128 KiB in size. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Application Gateway mTLS passthrough support

Body.Content:
Announcing a new mTLS enhancement in Azure Application Gateway for backend applications that perform client certificate and authorization header validation at the backend while still requiring web traffic inspection through the Web Application Firewall (WAF). This update introduces greater flexibility by allowing such applications to accept and inspect traffic through the Application Gateway even when a client certificate is not presented, supporting mixed authentication scenarios with both mTLS and token-based access.

What Changed

Previously, Application Gateway listeners operated in Strict mode, blocking any connection without a valid client certificate. This meant traffic relying solely on authorization tokens could not reach the backend.

With this update, you can now enable Passthrough mode for mutual TLS (mTLS) connections, allowing:

  • Requests without client certificates to pass through WAF for inspection.
  • Backend applications to retain full control over certificate and token validation logic.

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: JWT Validation in Azure Application Gateway

Body.Content:
Announcing the preview of JSON Web Token (JWT) validation in Azure Application Gateway — enabling authentication and token validation right at the Application gateway before traffic reaches your backend applications or APIs.

Why It matters

  • Protect at the perimeter: Block requests with missing or invalid tokens (401/403) at the edge, ensuring only trusted traffic reaches your services.

  • Boost performance: Offload token validation from your microservices or web apps to improve scalability and response times.

  • Simplify operations: Apply consistent authentication policies centrally across multiple applications and routes.

What’s included in the preview

  • Issuer (iss) validation

  • Audience (aud) matching - supports Client ID and/or custom App ID URIs

  • Expiration (exp) enforcement

  • Signature verification using JWKS

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Rule-based routing in Azure Container Apps

Body.Content:
Azure Container Apps support for rule-based routing is now generally available. This feature provides greater flexibility and composability to your Azure Container Apps by simplifying your architecture for microservice applications, A/B testing, blue-green deployments, and more.  

Rule-based routing allows you to direct incoming HTTP traffic to different apps within your Container Apps environment based on the requested host name or path. This includes support for custom domains. Instead of having to configure a separate reverse proxy, such as NGINX, you can now provide routing rules for your environment and incoming traffic will automatically be routed to the specified target apps.

Title: Public Preview: Azure SQL change event streaming

Body.Content:
You can now stream data changes in near real time from Azure SQL Database directly into Azure Event Hubs. With the public preview of change event streaming (CES), you can streamline data integration and support enhanced analytics, event-driven architectures, and the modernization of monolithic applications. 

 

By streaming operational data from SQL databases to Azure Event Hubs, you can seamlessly integrate this data into real-time dashboards, microservices, and various downstream systems, reducing the delays and complexities associated with traditional batch-based pipelines. Data is transferred from SQL only once and can be accessed by multiple consumers, minimizing polling on operational databases. Additionally, when data is available on a common message bus, it becomes more accessible for new consumers, unlocking faster innovation such as AI solution development. 

 

CES offers near real-time latency, an “at least once” message delivery guarantee, and minimal impact on source workloads.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Elastic clusters on Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server

Body.Content:
Now you can use elastic clusters to horizontally scale Azure Database for PostgreSQL through row-based and schema-based sharding. Elastic clusters make it easy to build multitenant apps by offloading shard management and operations—such as tenant isolation, split, or online rebalancing of shards—to the service.  

 

Row-based sharding is ideal for multitenant software as a service (SaaS) deployments, as it splits tenants into rows within a cluster-distributed table, enhancing density and improving margins per tenant. Alternatively, schema-based sharding suits microservices and lift-and-shift migrations of existing applications, offering more customization of schemas for each tenant.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Oracle to PostgreSQL migration tooling in Visual Studio Code

Body.Content:
Migrating from Oracle to PostgreSQL is now simpler and faster with the new Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration tooling, available directly in the Azure Database for PostgreSQL extension for Visual Studio Code. 

 

This new tool helps you seamlessly convert your Oracle schemas and application code to PostgreSQL equivalents without leaving your development environment. You can extract Oracle schema files, validate conversions in a scratch PostgreSQL database, and review AI-assisted conversion recommendations—all through a step-by-step guided wizard inside Visual Studio Code. 

 

The tool automatically identifies Oracle-specific constructs and transforms them into PostgreSQL-compatible syntax while flagging any items that require developer review. In the background, integration with Azure OpenAI Service brings intelligent code conversion to both database and application layers, reducing manual rework and accelerating migration readiness. 

 

In addition to database schema conversion, the new Application Migration capability leverages GitHub Copilot Agent Mode together with specialized Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversion tools to modernize client application code. 

 

Whether you’re modernizing a single application or moving enterprise workloads, this tool helps you streamline end-to-end migration, ensure compatibility, and get to PostgreSQL faster. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure DocumentDB - an open-source, MongoDB-compatible document database service for hybrid and multicloud

Body.Content:
Microsoft is announcing the general availability of Azure DocumentDB, a fully managed document database service built on the open-source, MongoDB-compatible DocumentDB, now governed by the Linux Foundation. Formerly known as Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB (vCore), Azure DocumentDB gives you the power of open source with the performance, security, and scale of Azure. 

  

What you gain: 

  • Freedom and flexibility. Build once and deploy anywhere with a consistent open-source MongoDB-compatible database that runs across hybrid and multi-cloud environments. 

  • AI-ready innovation. Use built-in vector and hybrid search to power retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), copilots, and other intelligent applications. 

  • Elastic performance. Get instant autoscale and independent compute and storage scaling—so you pay only for what you use. 

  • Enterprise-grade reliability and security. Protect your data with Microsoft Entra ID authentication, customer-managed keys, and 35-day backups at no additional cost, backed by 99.999% uptime full-stack service-level agreements and around-the-clock Azure support. 

 

With Azure DocumentDB, you can modernize your MongoDB workloads, build AI-driven apps faster, and scale globally on an open, flexible, and enterprise-ready foundation. 

Learn more.

Freedom and flexibility . Build once and deploy anywhere with a consistent open-source MongoDB-compatible database that runs across hybrid and multi - cloud environments.

AI-ready innovation . Use built-in vector and hybrid search to power retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), copilots, and other intelligent applications.

Elastic performance . Get instant autoscale and independent compute and storage scaling—so you pay only for what you use.

Enterprise-grade reliability and security . Protect your data with Microsoft Entra ID authentication, c ustomer- m anaged k eys, and 35-day backups at no additional cost, backed by 99.999% uptime full-stack service-level agreements and around-the-clock Azure support.

With Azure DocumentDB , you can modernize your MongoDB workloads, build AI-driven apps faster, and scale globally on an open, flexible, and enterprise-ready foundation.

Learn more .

Title: Generally Available: Azure Cosmos DB fleet pools

Body.Content:
Now you can more easily operate your Azure Cosmos DB accounts at scale. Azure Cosmos DB fleet pools give you new capabilities when building multitenant software as a service (SaaS) applications. 

 

You can simplify capacity management by creating a pool of throughput (RU/s) that can be shared by accounts in the fleet. You get all the security and performance isolation benefits of creating one Azure Cosmos DB account to represent a tenant or end customer, while also efficiently sharing RU/s resources across tenants to avoid overprovisioning at the per-tenant level. Throughput pooling is now generally available. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Priority-based execution in Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
You can now enable priority-based execution in Azure Cosmos DB to ensure that high-priority requests are favored during periods of contention. The system will throttle low-priority requests first, allowing high-priority operations to proceed on a best-effort basis. 

 

Using the Azure Cosmos DB SDK, you can assign each request a priority level (high or low). Low priority requests are retried according to the configured retry policy, helping maintain responsiveness for critical workloads. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Cosmos DB in Microsoft Fabric

Now generally available, Cosmos DB in Fabric enables you to build operational and analytical workloads in Microsoft Fabric. You can use the AI-features in Azure Cosmos DB plus the innovations in Fabric to run SQL queries over JSON data and build real-time intelligence over transactional data. You can also use Azure Cosmos DB as a lightning fast serving layer for Microsoft Power BI, using Spark for reverse extract, transform, load (ETL)—all without having to stitch together separate services.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Float16 data type for vector indexes in Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
Azure Cosmos DB now supports float 16 data types for vector indexes. With this update, you can store and query vectors using half-precision floating-point numbers. Using float16 cuts storage usage in half compared to float32, while maintaining high retrieval accuracy for most AI workloads. 

 

Float16 can be especially useful for large-scale scenarios when you need to store many vector embeddings. By reducing vector size, you can lower indexing and storage costs, making it easier to scale semantic search and AI agent memory retrieval. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Confidential computing in Azure Container Apps

Body.Content:
Confidential computing support in Azure Container Apps is now in public preview. This release brings hardware-based Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to your containerized workloads. Azure already provides encryption of data at rest and in transit, and confidential computing provides an additional layer of protection for data in use by encrypting data in memory and processing it only after the cloud environment is verified. This helps customers prevent unauthorized access to data in use, even from the cloud operator, and is beneficial for organizations that require further protection for sensitive data and applications.  

Confidential computing is accessible through workload profiles in Azure Container Apps, and the public preview is limited to select regions. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Container Apps introduces flexible workload profile

Body.Content:
Flexible workload profile represents a new option that blends the simplicity of consumption with many of the performance and control characteristics of dedicated workload profiles. This offers the same easy-to-understand, pay-per-use serverless model as Consumption, while adding features like planned maintenance windows, dedicated networking support, and access to larger replica sizes for demanding applications. Running in a single-tenant compute pool, this flexible workload profile provides improved predictability and isolation without adding operational complexity. This new profile is designed for customers who want the convenience of serverless scaling with greater control over performance and environment stability. 

Learn more.

With this GA release, Azure Functions delivers: 

  • Unified observability – Standardize logs, traces, and metrics across your serverless workloads.

Start using OpenTelemetry in Azure Functions today and bring modern, standards-based observability to your apps. View the documentation for step-by-step guidance on enabling OpenTelemetry and configuring exporters for your preferred backend.

Title: Announcing: Resources for migrating to Azure Functions Flex Consumption

Body.Content:
Azure Functions Flex Consumption is now the recommended hosting plan for serverless workloads requiring advanced scaling, networking, and cost optimization. To support customers migrating from the Azure Functions Consumption plan or from AWS Lambda, Microsoft has published comprehensive migration guides and tooling:


  • Azure Functions Consumption to Flex Consumption: The new documentation provides step-by-step instructions for moving your Azure Functions apps from the Consumption plan to Flex Consumption. This includes guidance on updating your infrastructure as code (ARM/Bicep), configuration changes, and leveraging new AZ CLI commands to automate the migration process.

  • AWS Lambda to Azure Functions Flex Consumption: For customers migrating from AWS Lambda, this guide covers mapping Lambda concepts to Azure Functions, code porting strategies, and best practices for deploying to Azure Functions Flex Consumption. This includes instructions for using GitHub Copilot in VS Code for help with code refactoring, manual refactoring for specific changes, or other migration aids.


These resources are designed to minimize downtime and ensure a smooth transition, enabling customers to take advantage of Flex Consumption’s improved scaling, networking, and cost controls.

Learn more:

  • Migrate Consumption plan apps to the Flex Consumption plan 
  • Migrate AWS Lambda workloads to Azure Functions

A key feature of MCP is the ability to define tools that AI agents can leverage to accomplish whatever tasks they’ve been given. MCP servers can be run locally, but remote MCP servers are important for sharing tools that work at cloud scale.

Azure Functions lets you author focused, event-driven logic that scales automatically in response to demand. You just write code reflecting unique requirements of your tools, and Functions will take care of the rest. 


Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure DocumentDB high-performance storage

Body.Content:
Now you can run bigger, faster workloads on fewer nodes using high-performance storage for Azure DocumentDB. This update delivers up to 64 TiB capacity, 80,000 IOPS, and 1,200 MB/s throughput per physical shard (node). Storage IOPS and throughput on Azure DocumentDB clusters with high-performance storage are always optimized by default—configured using the maximum values permitted by the selected compute and storage combination.

 
This update provides the headroom required for I/O-intensive applications and very large datasets, helping you to consolidate data that previously needed many shards and to maintain low latency at peak traffic. Real-time analytics, personalization, and high-volume commerce scenarios benefit from predictable throughput and consistent performance as you scale.
 
To get started, you can create a cluster with high-performance storage in the Azure portal, then benchmark your workload to right-size shards and compute for your targets.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager address overlap prevention in mesh

Body.Content:
Azure Virtual Network Manager address space overlap prevention in mesh is now generally available, bringing enhanced reliability and governance to multi-virtual network environments. 

Unintended address overlap within mesh can lead to dropped traffic. This feature introduces a built-in validation mechanism to proactively detect and prevent such conflicts. 

With this capability: 

  • When adding a virtual network to a mesh, Azure Virtual Network Manager automatically verifies that the new virtual network’s address space does not overlap with existing members. 
  • When updating an existing virtual network’s address space or adding a new peering, Azure Virtual Network Manager ensures the operation will not introduce an overlap. 

Any address change triggers an update to Azure Virtual Network Manager, ensuring real-time validation and consistent routing integrity across large-scale environments. 

This GA release empowers customers to maintain end-to-end network reliability, prevent configuration-induced outages, and uphold governance standards across distributed Azure deployments. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Cross region pool association support for Azure Virtual Network Manager IP address management

Body.Content:
Managing IP address spaces across multiple regions can be complex and error-prone.  

With this new capability, you can now associate a single IPAM pool with virtual networks in multiple regions, simplifying governance and ensuring consistent CIDR allocation globally.  

Key benefits include: 

  • Simplified management: Consolidate address planning into one multi-region pool instead of per-region pools. 
  • Consistent governance: Enforce CIDR policies across regions with flexible region restrictions. 
  • Backward compatibility: Existing single-region pools continue to work seamlessly. 

This enhancement enables global-scale deployments while reducing operational overhead and maintaining precise control of address allocation across your Azure footprint.  

This preview feature is available in select regions. To get started, please refer to the documentation for guidance on enabling this preview feature.

Title: Public Preview: Add durability to AI agents in Azure Functions using Microsoft Agent Framework

Body.Content:
You can now build and host reliable production-grade AI agents using the durable extension for Microsoft Agent Framework. This integration combines the Microsoft Agent Framework with Azure Functions’ durable capabilities, delivering proven orchestration and resilience for serverless AI agent hosting. You gain automatic session management, built-in HTTP endpoints, and elastic scaling from zero to thousands of instances—all with pay-per-use pricing and automated infrastructure management. 

 

Key capabilities include: 

  • Stateful agent sessions: Maintain persistent conversation history across distributed instances with automatic failover for uninterrupted operation. 
  • Durable tool calls: Checkpoint progress during long-running tool invocations, extending beyond typical timeout limits. 
  • Deterministic multi-agent orchestration: Coordinate specialized agents through predictable, code-driven workflows that survive failures and restarts. 
  • Human-in-the-loop workflows: Pause orchestrations for days or weeks awaiting human approval at zero compute cost, then resume seamlessly. 
  • Built-in observability: Access deep insights via the durable task scheduler dashboard with execution replay, conversation history, and integrated performance metrics. 

The extension supports both C# and Python, enabling developers to deploy AI agents confidently on Azure Functions with enterprise-grade durability and scalability.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: AKS Automatic managed system node pools

Body.Content:
Provisioning and maintaining system node pools in AKS requires ongoing effort to ensure proper scaling, patching, and availability, tasks that can divert resources from application development and delivery.

Managed system node pools in AKS Automatic removes this operational burden by providing a fully managed infrastructure layer that handles system components without customer intervention. This means teams no longer need to maintain infrastructure for system workloads, allowing them to focus entirely on deploying and scaling applications. By isolating system workloads from customer applications, AKS Automatic improves reliability and ensures consistent performance backed by SLAs. The result is faster time to value, reduced infrastructure overhead, and a simplified path to Kubernetes adoption.

Title: Public Preview: Windows Server 2025 on AKS

Body.Content:
Organizations running Windows-based workloads on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) face increasing pressure to modernize as support timelines for older Windows Server versions approach retirement. To help customers prepare, AKS now offers preview support for Windows Server 2025, bringing significant improvements over Windows Server 2022.  

 

Windows Server 2025 provides many improvements as compared to Windows Server 2022:  

  • Stable ABI: Allows you to run Windows Server 2022 containers on Windows Server 2025 
  • New defaults: Generation 2 VM, containerd 2.0, FIPS enablement 
  • Improved Nano server flexibility and added functionality: For example, Nano server now contains support for 32-bit apps via a FoD 
  • Improved GPU support: CUDA workloads can now run in a container 

With upcoming retirements for Windows Server 2019 on March 1, 2026 and Windows Server 2022 on March 15, 2027, we recommend testing out the new Windows Server version to prepare for your migration. When migrating to Windows Server 2025, you’ll need to recreate your node pools with the new OS and migrate existing workloads. 
Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager for Arc-enabled clusters

To simplify this, Azure Kubernetes Fleet Manager now supports Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes, enabling organizations to seamlessly manage any CNCF-compliant Kubernetes distribution, regardless of where it’s running.

Fleet Manager also empowers cluster administrators and application teams with intelligent workload placement, making it easier to deploy configurations and applications consistently across environments. 

This enhancement helps reduce operational overhead, improves deployment agility, and ensures consistent governance across distributed Kubernetes infrastructure.

Title: Generally Available: Pod sandboxing on AKS

Body.Content:
Running containerized workloads in shared environments can raise concerns around security and workload isolation. To address this, AKS now supports pod sandboxing, enabling customers to run containers in per-workload pod VMs. Each pod VM is isolated from others and from the host, providing a strong compute isolation boundary. 

This feature enhances workload security by reducing the risk of cross-pod interference and host-level vulnerabilities, making it ideal for multi-tenant scenarios or sensitive applications.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Container Registry Repository Permissions with Attribute-based Access Control (ABAC)

Body.Content:
Organizations operating Azure Container Registries (ACR) require least-privilege permissions over which Microsoft Entra identities can publish or consume container images. With ACR repository permissions using attribute-based access control (ABAC), administrators can now grant granular repository and namespace-level permissions. This enables secure container registry operations by ensuring that CI/CD pipelines and Kubernetes workloads can only perform image push, pull, or delete operations on authorized repositories. 

 

ABAC is available for both new and existing ACR registries, across all SKUs, in all regions.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: ExpressRoute Scalable Gateway

Body.Content:
ExpressRoute Scalable Gateway (ErGwScale) is our next-generation offering that brings flexibility, performance, and operational simplicity to Virtual Network Gateway deployments. With this release, you can dynamically scale gateway infrastructure to meet real-time traffic demands. 

What’s new 

  • Dynamic scaling: Deploy ErGwScale to achieve up to 40 Gbps of connectivity for virtual machines and private endpoints within your virtual network. 
  • Auto scaling: Configure minimum and maximum scale units, and Azure automatically adjusts capacity based on bandwidth and flow demand—delivering efficiency and eliminating manual tuning. 
  • Fixed scale option: For predictable workloads, set a steady scale to maintain consistent bandwidth for stable traffic patterns. 
  • FastPath + gateway coexistence: ErGwScale complements FastPath for scenarios where FastPath isn’t supported—such as high-bandwidth or complex routing cases—ensuring seamless performance. 

This offering introduces elastic scaling, zero-downtime upgrades, and enterprise-grade reliability, making it ideal for hybrid connectivity and demanding workloads. 

 Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure VNet Flow Log - Filtering

Body.Content:
VNet Flow Log captures IP traffic flowing through VNets, Subnets, & NICs for monitoring, troubleshooting, network optimization, security, and compliance needs. 

This release introduces advanced filtering capabilities in VNet Flow Logs, empowering users with unprecedented granular control over network traffic logging. With support for nine distinct criteria including IP addresses, ports, protocols, encryption state, allowed/denied actions, flow states, and traffic directions.  

This empowers organization to surgically capture only the traffic that truly matters most to their operations. This flexibility enables selective recording of intra/inter-VNet traffic, CIDR-based flows, inbound/outbound traffic or traffic flowing through specific ports and much more all through intuitive logical operations of AND and OR.  By prioritizing critical flows and tailoring monitoring to user preferences, organizations gain faster, more actionable insights while maintaining robust network visibility 

This release aids significant operational efficiencies by dramatically reducing log volume and noise. By targeting only relevant traffic logs, organizations can streamline troubleshooting, minimize data processing overhead, and lower total cost of ownership (TCO) through reduced storage requirements. The simplified log management not only preserves essential visibility but also ensures compliance and security monitoring remain uncompromised. environments. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher Topology – AKS Visualization

Body.Content:
Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) visualization in Network Watcher Topology (Public Preview) delivers end-to-end visibility of AKS clusters directly within the Azure networking experience. Customers can now explore their Kubernetes environments, including the control plane, node pools, and connected Azure resources, through an intuitive, interactive topology view. 

With this release, organizations can visualize AKS clusters as part of their broader network topology, closing the gap between Kubernetes workloads and Azure infrastructure. Users can trace dependencies, understand traffic paths, and identify connectivity issues - all within a single unified map. 

This capability simplifies troubleshooting and performance analysis by visually mapping relationships between pods, services, load balancers, and underlying VNets or subnets. It enables teams to collaboratively diagnose issues and maintain consistent visibility across layers. 

Integrating AKS visualization into Network Watcher Topology improves operational efficiency by reducing investigation time, minimizing tool switching, and providing actionable insights at a glance. It bridges the visibility gap between infrastructure and containerized workloads, empowering teams to maintain reliable, secure, and optimized AKS deployments. 

With AKS visualization in Topology, customers gain a unified, Azure-native view of their network landscape, ensuring awareness from the network edge to the container.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Network Watcher – Agentless Connection Troubleshoot

Body.Content:
Agentless Connection Troubleshoot (public preview) introduces a faster, simpler, and fully agentless way to diagnose network connectivity issues across Azure resources. Previously, running connectivity checks required installing the Network Watcher Extension on virtual machines, adding setup overhead and potential deployment delays. With this release, customers can now perform end-to-end connectivity tests without deploying any agents or extensions, reducing friction and improving reliability. 

With Agentless Connection Troubleshoot, users can instantly validate reachability, latency, and packet loss between Azure resources directly from the Azure portal, CLI, or API, with no dependency on VM configuration. This enables faster diagnostics while maintaining the same level of accuracy and depth as extension-based checks. 

This enhancement simplifies network troubleshooting by removing manual setup steps and potential extension failures, ensuring consistent results across environments. It also strengthens security posture by reducing in-guest dependencies and operational overhead. 

By making Connection Troubleshoot completely agentless, Azure empowers users to detect, triage, and resolve connectivity issues faster while improving operational efficiency and scalability. Customers can now run comprehensive connectivity tests instantly, enabling frictionless, reliable, and secure network diagnostics across their Azure workloads. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Advanced sampling and richer data collection in Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro

Body.Content:
Azure continues to embrace open standards by adding new capabilities to the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro that powers Azure Monitor Application Insights. 

New Capabilities:

  • Rate-limited sampling and trace-based log sampling: New sampling options in the Distro provide an alternative to the existing fixed-rate (percentage-based) sampler. Rate-limited sampling helps you control data ingestion by capping the number of traces collected per second and trace-based log sampling drops any logs correlated with sampled out traces, providing predictable cost management while maintaining reliable observability. Learn More.
  • Performance Counters: Azure Monitor’s OpenTelemetry Distro now automatically collects system and process metrics, known as performance counters, that power key Application Insights experiences. These metrics provide deeper visibility into application performance and help you quickly diagnose and resolve performance issues. Learn More.
  • New Telemetry Attributes: We’ve worked with the OpenTelemetry community to add Synthetic Source, Device IP Address, and Device OS/Browser to the semantic model. By bringing these fields into the official OpenTelemetry data model and Azure Monitor Distro, you can now seamlessly filter by synthetic traffic indicators, enrich client-source context, and segment telemetry by platform—making monitoring smarter, investigations faster, and insights more actionable. Learn More.

Title: Public Preview: NCv6 Virtual Machines

Body.Content:
We are announcing the public preview of NCv6 RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition Virtual Machines, as the next enhancement of NC Series VMs available on Azure.

Nvidia RTX PRO 6000 BSE GPUs are designed to accelerate a wide array of workloads including video streaming, graphics rendering, product design, digital twins, and AI development. The NCv6 VM family will be available in three categories to best suit your workload needs:  

  • Compute optimized - NClds_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 - designed for AI and LLM inferencing workloads 
  • Memory optimized - NCmds_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 - tailored for visualization and graphics workloads 
  • General purpose - NCds_RTXPRO6000BSE_v6 - category ideal for VDI and general-purpose AI workloads. 

For workloads running NCv6, customer experience will be the same as other NC and NV Series VMs such as T4, A100, and H100, with all currently supported workloads from those SKUs also supported on NCv6. Additionally, NCv6 VM SKUs will come with integrated NVIDIA vGPU licenses and support Multi Instance GPU (MIG), enabling greater flexibility and efficiency for a variety of use cases. 

Sign up for the public preview. 

Learn more.

Title: Private Preview: Azure Boost remote storage throughput and network bandwidth enhancements

Body.Content:
Remote storage throughput and network bandwidth performance enhancements for the latest Azure Boost architecture are now in preview. 

Azure Boost is a Microsoft Azure system that offloads virtualization tasks—such as networking, storage, and host management—from the hypervisor and host OS to purpose-built hardware and software, freeing CPU resources for customer workloads while enhancing security through physical isolation and hardware root of trust. By reducing maintenance impact and improving scalability, Azure Boost enables faster, more secure, and highly efficient cloud operations for demanding workloads.  

Performance enhancements of this latest architecture include up to 20 GBps remote storage throughput, up to 1 M remote storage IOPS, and up to 400 Gbps network bandwidth. These enhancements will be available beginning with the D/E/Fsv7 Intel “Granite Rapids” VMs (in preview). Other new VMs will also begin using this architecture and will provide similar performance capabilities. 

You can learn more about these new Azure Boost performance enhancements by reading the blog. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Microsoft HTTP DDoS Ruleset 1.0 on Application Gateway WAF v2

Body.Content:
Announcing the public preview of the HTTP DDoS Ruleset for Application Gateway WAF v2. 

HTTP-layer DDoS attacks remain a leading cause of application downtime, and traditional static controls often fall short against evolving botnets. The new HTTP DDoS Ruleset for Azure WAF introduces automated, adaptive Layer 7 protection that learns, detects, and defends with minimal configuration. Once assigned, the ruleset continuously baselines normal traffic for each Application Gateway and, when attack surges are detected, selectively blocks offending clients with no emergency tuning required. 

The HTTP DDoS Ruleset features: 

  • Automated learning of traffic baselines at both the gateway and per-IP level. 
  • Dynamic thresholds and sensitivity settings to balance protection and user experience. 
  • Two core rules: one for high-rate client anomalies and one for suspected bots, leveraging Microsoft Threat Intelligence. 

Currently, portal access for this feature is via the preview portal.  

Learn more.

Title: Private Preview: Azure Boost confidential device

Body.Content:
The Azure Boost confidential device feature is now in preview. 

Azure Boost is a Microsoft Azure system that offloads virtualization tasks—such as networking, storage, and host management—from the hypervisor and host OS to purpose-built hardware and software, freeing CPU resources for customer workloads while enhancing security through physical isolation and hardware root of trust. By reducing maintenance impact and improving scalability, Azure Boost enables faster, more secure, and highly efficient cloud operations for demanding workloads. 

The Azure Boost confidential device feature is designed specifically for upcoming versions of Azure confidential VMs and will allow the confidential computing trust boundary of these VMs to be extended into the Azure Boost card using the PCIe TDISP standard. This standard supports hardware-based attestation of the Azure Boost card and hardware-based encryption of the PCIe data path. This feature will enhance confidential VM performance by eliminating the need for a “bounce buffer” when sensitive data within the trust boundary of the confidential VM is shared outside of that trust boundary. This feature will deliver faster data movement, reduce CPU overhead, and improve confidential VM performance without compromising security. 

Learn more.
