Title: Public Preview: Azure Copilot observability agent

Body.Content:
Cloud operations need more than reactive troubleshooting, they demand intelligent observability that scales across resources and delivers actionable insights when services aren’t performing as expected.

  • Resource health checks and diagnostics integration for quick remediation
  • Log-enriched anomaly detection for precise root cause identification

What’s New:
  • Extended regional availability – now supported in most Azure regions
  • Copilot support – interact naturally with alerts and dive into investigations with one click

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Online container copy in Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
You can now minimize downtime when you copy data across containers in Azure Cosmos DB accounts. You can use online container copy in Azure Cosmos DB to copy data from one container to another in real time. Your application using the source container remains online while the data is being copied to the destination container in real time. After your data is completely copied, you can switch over to the new container.  


Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Dynamic threshold for Log search alerts

Body.Content:
We’re bringing Azure Monitor’s dynamic threshold capabilities to Log search alerts!
Using dynamic thresholds means you don't have to know the right threshold for each Log alert rule - Dynamic thresholds calculate the most appropriate thresholds for you.

Key benefits
Dynamic thresholds apply advanced machine learning and use a set of algorithms and methods to:

  1. Learn the historical behavior of log query results.
  2. Analyze these results over time and identify hourly / daily / weekly seasonal patterns.
  3. Calculate the most appropriate thresholds for log alert rules.
  4. Adapt automatically to changes in data patterns and adjust the threshold accordingly.
  5. At-scale monitoring - in rule monitoring multiple dimensions - the Dynamic threshold is calculated individually, per dimension combination.
Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Copilot brings new intelligent agents to support end-to-end lifecycle management of workloads

Body.Content:
Azure Copilot introduces specialized agents (gated preview) to help migrate, operate, and modernize workloads anywhere. Copilot evolves chat into an immersive, full-screen command center (public preview) powered by GPT-5 reasoning, artifact generation, and ARM-driven scenarios. Customers get contextual, multi-modal, and personalized experiences, including chat history and inline actions. A compliance-first architecture and Bring Your Own Storage (public preview) let customers manage chat data securely and control data residency. The new agents (gated preview) are as follows:

  • Deployment Agent: Streamlines environment planning and guided infrastructure deployment.
  • Migration Agent: Automates cloud migration, generates AI recommendations, and modernizes apps.
  • Optimization Agent: Finds cost and carbon savings and enables direct action.
  • Observability Agent: Diagnoses full-stack app issues and suggests mitigation using Azure Monitor.
  • Resiliency Agent: Offers resiliency insights, auto-remediation, and ransomware protection.
  • Troubleshooting Agent: Pinpoints issues, suggests fixes, and guides AKS troubleshooting.

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Monitor unified onboarding experience for AKS and VMs

Body.Content:
Azure Monitor now offers a unified, single-click onboarding experience for both Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) clusters and virtual machines (VMs). This new experience simplifies setup by automatically deploying the latest Azure Monitor capabilities with optimized defaults.

For AKS, the experience combines managed Prometheus metrics, container logs with Kubernetes events, and our newly GAed Dashboards with Grafana. As a part of the new experience, we are also introducing a new application monitoring addon and preconfigured AKS recommended alerts for faster troubleshooting.

For VMs, the onboarding includes new OpenTelemetry-based metrics (now in public preview and free), legacy Log Analytics counters, and recommended VM alerts for comprehensive performance visibility.

This unified experience provides a consistent, streamlined approach to monitoring across your compute environments, helping you get started with Azure Monitor in minutes.

Title: Public Preview: Built-in CIS benchmarks for Azure endorsed Linux distros in Machine Config

Body.Content:
Microsoft Azure now offers built-in Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmarks in public preview for all Azure endorsed Linux distributions through Azure Machine Configuration’s new customizable security benchmarks capability, powered by azure-osconfig’s compliance engine. This capability allows organizations to easily customize and apply industry-standard security benchmarks which are in parity with the content published on CIS website. It supports both Level 1(L1) and Level 2(L2) server profiles, enables exception and parameter customization, operates in audit-only mode at no additional cost, and extends compliance management to hybrid scenarios via Azure Arc. Using this new capability, you can introduce a flexible, compliance as code driven approach to your organization to maintain security and compliance across your hybrid infrastructure. The solution is officially certified by CIS for CIS benchmark assessment for all the supported benchmarks.  

Learn more:

Title: Public Preview: Large volumes up to 7.2 PiB

Body.Content:
The Large Volumes up to 7.2 PiB with Cool Access feature allows you to create Azure NetApp Files volumes up to 7.2 PiB on dedicated capacity, designed for workloads where most data are rarely accessed. This enhancement extends cool-access support beyond the previous 2 PiB limit, giving customers a new scale option for large deployments. By combining petabyte-scale capacity, cool-tier economics, and enterprise-grade performance, organizations can store massive datasets cost-effectively without compromising efficiency. 

This capability helps reduce storage costs for infrequently accessed data while maintaining predictable performance for active workloads. It’s ideal for industries managing large archives, backups, and compliance-driven datasets where 80–90% of data can reside in the cool tier. Use cases include archives, media libraries, healthcare imaging, compliance data lakes, AI/ML datasets, EDA projects, and large file shares—delivering multi-petabyte consolidation, transparent tiering, and lower TCO without sacrificing enterprise-grade performance. 

This feature is supported in all regions that support large volumes. 

Learn more: 

  • What’s New in Azure NetApp Files 

  • Create an SMB volume for Azure NetApp Files 

  • Create an NFS volume for Azure NetApp Files 

  • Create a dual-protocol volume for Azure NetApp Files 

  • Resource limits for Azure NetApp Files

With this feature, you can:
  • Optimize costs by migrating from Log Analytics based metrics to OpenTelemetry metrics
  • Improve performance with faster metric query response times

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Agent mitigations and guardrail customization

Body.Content:
Introducing guardrails for agents in Microsoft Foundry Control Plane. Formerly called content filters, guardrails can now be applied at the agent level rather than only to model deployments. They include existing controls to help mitigate prompt injection attacks, harms and risks, and to support groundedness. Our newest risk that can be detected, task adherence, helps keep agents on task, detecting when an agent’s next proposed action starts to drift off task.

A new control model also gives you more flexibility in how to configure guardrails and steer agent behavior. Title: Public Preview: Foundry IQ by Azure AI Search

Body.Content: Foundry IQ, powered by Azure AI Search, is a knowledge system that delivers a smarter way to ground agents in enterprise data. Agents only need to connect to a single knowledge base to access multiple sources, removing the need to manage separate APIs and function calls. Knowledge bases perform knowledge retrieval over supported sources including Microsoft SharePoint, Fabric OneLake, and web. Unlike traditional RAG and vector databases, knowledge bases use an agentic retrieval engine holistically across sources and conversations. It also has broader access to data, because it can connect to data remotely or in a synced index. This enables better response quality out of the box, where single-shot retrieval can fall short. Foundry IQ is enterprise-ready, with Purview governance and Entra-based access control, so developers can build with trust and confidence. Create and manage knowledge bases from the Foundry portal, or directly in Azure AI Search.

Title: Generally Available: OpenShift Virtualization now available on Azure Red Hat OpenShift

Body.Content:
Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization is now generally available on Azure Red Hat OpenShift (ARO), enabling customers to manage virtual machines and containers from one cloud-native platform. This GA builds on feedback from the preview announced at Red Hat Summit and helps organizations modernize while preserving mission-critical workloads. It simplifies operations with integrated migration tools, Kubernetes-native automation, and cost optimization under consistent governance.

The release adds support for Red Hat Migration Toolkit for Virtualization (MTV), integration with Ansible Automation Platform, and licensing benefits such as included RHEL entitlements and Windows Server licensing through Azure Hybrid Benefit. Organizations can move legacy apps to Azure with minimal disruption, leveraging Azure’s security, compliance, and hybrid features through the OpenShift console. Unifying VMs and containers helps teams speed delivery, apply DevOps practices, and reduce overhead.

Learn more.

FAQ:
Q: Can I migrate existing virtual machines to ARO?
A: Yes, use Red Hat MTV to automate and minimize downtime.
Q: Can I run containers and VMs together?
A: Yes, in a single OpenShift cluster.
Q: What storage is recommended?
A: Use OpenShift Data Foundation; Azure NetApp Files is in preview.
Q: How are support and compliance handled?
A: All ARO clusters receive joint Red Hat–Microsoft support with unified security.

Title: Generally Available: Govern Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoints using Azure API Management

Body.Content:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) governance in Azure API Management (APIM) is now generally available.

This release extends Azure API Management’s proven governance, security, and observability model to a new generation of AI-driven workloads. Enterprises can now apply consistent policies, authentication, and monitoring across both traditional APIs and AI systems that connect through MCP. 

What’s New:

  • Expose APIs through MCP: Publish any managed API as an MCP-compliant endpoint so AI agents can securely discover and invoke enterprise capabilities using standard protocols. 
  • Proxy and govern external MCP services: Apply Azure API Management policies, authentication, and observability to third-party MCP servers—such as those hosted on Azure Functions, Container Apps etc. or externally hosted MCP servers. 
  • Unify access and governance: Use the same products, policies, and subscription model to manage both API and MCP traffic, ensuring consistent control and visibility across your organization. 
  • Discover and govern through API Center: Register MCP endpoints in Azure API Center to build a private catalog of enterprise MCP integrations, making them easy to discover, onboard, and reuse across teams while maintaining centralized governance and compliance. 

Available across Azure API Management classic and v2 tiers, including the Developer tier and the Self-hosted Gateway. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Automated Testing Framework for Logic Apps [Standard]

Body.Content:
We’re pleased to announce the general availability of automated testing for Azure Logic Apps (Standard) in the Visual Studio Code extension. This new capability empowers developers and integration specialists to build more reliable workflows by simplifying the unit testing experience directly within their local development environment. 

Starting with version 5.58.8 of the Azure Logic Apps (Standard) extension for Visual Studio Code, you can now: 

  • Generate unit tests from existing workflow runs or saved workflow definitions. 
  • Edit and customize tests directly within Visual Studio Code. 
  • Execute tests locally, enabling faster validation and iteration before deploying to production. 

The enhanced testing experience combines a visual designer interface and an SDK for test script implementation, both powered by the same Test Runner engine to ensure consistency and accuracy of results regardless of the testing approach used. 

You can also execute tests as part of a build or CI/CD pipeline, improving developer productivity and overall code quality through early detection of errors and regressions. 

To get started, update your Azure Logic Apps (Standard) extension in Visual Studio Code and explore the new “Test” features available.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: New Agent Loop capabilities in Azure Logic Apps

Body.Content:
Announcing a new set of capabilities for Agent Loop in Azure Logic Apps, now in public preview. These updates expand how organizations can build, secure, and deploy agentic workflows across their enterprise environments enabling more flexible AI orchestration, governance, and collaboration.

Learn more:

Title: Public Preview: Industry-leading storage performance Ebsv6 VM series

Body.Content:
Announcing the public preview of the new Azure Ebsv6 VM series, powered by 5th Generation Intel® Xeon® processors. The Ebsv6 and Ebdsv6 VMs deliver up to and industry leading 800,000 IOPS and 14 GBps of remote disk storage throughput, providing high-performance remote storage bandwidth for demanding workloads. This new generation provides up to 2x higher remote storage performance compared to the previous generation, enabling workload consolidation on fewer VMs.

Key new features and improved VM specs compared to Ebsv5/Ebdsv5 

  • Up to 192 vCPU and 1832 GiB memory 

  • 15-30% improvement in CPU performance  

  • 40% larger local SSD capacity with 3X read IOPS 

  • Azure Boost which enables up to: 

    • 800K IOPS and 14GB/s remote storage throughput with Premium v2 and Ultra Disk support 

    • 15% higher remote storage performance per vCPU with up to 6600 IOPS/vCPU 

    • 10% higher remote storage throughput per vCPU 

    • Up to 200 Gbps VM network bandwidth  

    • Enhanced security through Total Memory Encryption (TME) technology 

The Ebsv6 VM series is optimized for large database workloads such as online transaction processing systems, data warehousing applications, and AI/ML workloads that require sequential streaming.

These VMs will initially be available for Public Preview in the US East region. Please sign up for the public preview through this form.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Scheduled Actions

Body.Content:
Schedule Actions gives the ability to manage the lifecycle of VMs at high scale on a periodic basis. Subscription throttling and retries due to transient errors are handled automatically to ensure that your operations succeed without additional overhead.

What is Scheduled Actions?

Scheduled Actions is a separate resource provider named compute.schedule that sits above our REST API and makes calls on your subscription’s behalf at the time that you specify.

Scheduled Actions supports the following VM operations:

  • Stop
  • Start
  • Hibernate
Why use Scheduled Actions?

  • To schedule power operations on VM resources at scale at up to 5000 concurrent operations.
  • When a higher scale is needed and spreading out call volume is too cumbersome or it's not an option
  • To not have to deal with the complexity of handling throttling issues from the compute stack
  • To offload complexity of determining if the error is transient in nature and needs to be retried. Scheduled Actions handles retries on transient errors.

Learn more:

  • Read the blog.

  • Get started.

Title: Public preview: Support for large volume breakthrough mode

Body.Content:
Breakthrough mode in Azure NetApp Files enables extreme performance and scalability for demanding HPC and EDA workloads. It supports large volumes up to 2PiB, delivering throughput up to 50GiBps, depending on workload characteristics. Breakthrough mode uses six storage endpoints for each large volume ensuring consistent performance. Storage systems hosting breakthrough mode volumes are reserved for each customer to provide peak performance and not compete with other workloads. 

Key benefits include: 

  • High-capacity scaling for large-scale, latency-sensitive workloads 

  • Simplified network management with multiple storage endpoints per volume 

  • Dedicated capacity stamps to eliminate noisy neighbor interference and maintain predictable performance 

Supported in all regions where large volumes are supported.

 

How to create a volume with large volume breakthrough mode enabled.  

  • Create an NFS volume 

  • Create an SMB volume 

  • Create a dual protocol volume

Title: Public Preview: Query-based metric alerts in Azure Monitor

This feature empowers teams to proactively manage performance and reliability at scale, without sacrificing flexibility or security.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager UseExisting Mode for UDR management

Body.Content:
Azure Virtual Network Manager UDR management now offers UseExisting mode, providing customers with greater flexibility and compliance control over user-defined routes (UDRs). 

With the UseExisting mode, Azure Virtual Network Manager detects and appends required routes to an existing route table associated with a subnet, preserving the original route table’s name, group, and tags. If no route table exists, Azure Virtual Network Manager automatically creates one as before. Customers seeking Azure Virtual Network Manager-managed route tables can continue using the existing Managed Only mode (the default). 

This general availability release empowers customers to: 

  • Maintain governance compliance by retaining ownership of route table configurations 
  • Simplify operations with seamless integration of AVNM automation into existing environments 
  • Enhance flexibility by choosing how AVNM interacts with routing resources  

The UseExisting mode makes it easier than ever to adopt Azure Virtual Network Manager UDR management at scale—combining centralized automation with customer-driven governance and control. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager peering compliance

Body.Content:
Azure Virtual Network Manager peering compliance is now generally available, providing a secure and compliant mechanism to protect network connectivity managed by Azure Virtual Network Manager. 

In large-scale environments, it’s essential to prevent unintentional changes to critical connectivity configurations. With peering compliance, any virtual network peering created and managed through Azure Virtual Network Manager topology is safeguarded from accidental modification or deletion by virtual network owners outside of Azure Virtual Network Manager. 

This release allows users to enforce compliance by restricting direct edits to key peering properties and preventing deletion of peerings. Changes can only be made through Azure Virtual Network Manager connectivity configurations, ensuring consistency and governance across your environment.  

With this general availability release, customers gain stronger governance controls, reduced configuration drift, and higher confidence that network topologies remain secure and compliant across teams and subscriptions. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Virtual Network Manager IP Address Management Pool Association Recommendation

Body.Content:
Azure Virtual Network Manager IP Address Management (IPAM) – Pool Association Recommendation is now generally available, bringing intelligent, large-scale automation to IP address management in Azure. 

As organizations expand their network footprint across regions and management groups, identifying and associating virtual networks with the right IPAM pools can become increasingly complex. Unassociated virtual networks may consume overlapping address spaces, raising the risk of conflicts during provisioning. 

With Pool Association Recommendation, customers can now automatically identify all virtual networks within their Network Manager scope that are not yet associated with an IPAM pool. The feature intelligently recommends the most suitable pool for each virtual network by applying longest-prefix matching within the pool hierarchy, ensuring optimal fit and capacity alignment. 

Administrators can bulk select and associate virtual networks in a single action directly from the Azure portal—streamlining operations, reducing manual effort, and ensuring full coverage at scale. 

This general availability release empowers customers to manage address spaces more efficiently, minimize configuration drift, and maintain consistent governance across large, distributed Azure environments. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Agentic CLI for AKS

Body.Content:
Diagnosing and resolving issues in Kubernetes clusters can be complex and time-consuming, especially when navigating logs, telemetry, and diagnostics manually. To simplify this experience, Azure Kubernetes Service is introducing a new agentic AI-powered CLI experience through the “az aks agent” command. 

This new capability brings agentic reasoning directly into the Azure CLI, allowing developers and operators to interact with their clusters using natural language. By describing an issue or query, users can trigger an intelligent agentic loop that gathers signals from multiple sources, analyzes diagnostics, identifies health issues and root causes, and provides actionable recommendations. The CLI agent also integrates with the AKS MCP server and can seamlessly create and manage an Azure OpenAI instance, though it supports any LLM provider. 

Powered by HolmesGPT - an open-source project co-maintained by the AKS team and accepted as a CNCF sandbox project- this feature is now available in public preview. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: LocalDNS for AKS

Body.Content:
LocalDNS for AKS is now generally available.  

 

Large-scale Kubernetes clusters often face DNS resolution delays and reliability issues, especially during upstream outages or high query volumes. To address this, Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) now offers LocalDNS, a feature that is generally available. 

LocalDNS deploys a DNS proxy on each node, enabling faster and more reliable DNS resolution by handling queries locally. This eliminates bottlenecks, reduces latency, and ensures continued resolution even during upstream DNS outages through configurable serve-stale settings. 

With no application-level changes required, LocalDNS delivers immediate performance improvements and supports advanced DNS customization for both internal and external domains. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Vaulted Backup for Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS)

Body.Content:
Azure Backup vaulted protection for ADLS Gen2 delivers secure, off‑site backups to help organizations meet resilience and compliance goals. Vaulted backups maintain an independent copy of your data, isolated from the source account - providing protection against accidental deletion, malicious activity, and ransomware. 

 

Capabilities at a Glance: 

  • Off‑site protection: Recover data safely by restoring to alternate storage accounts to support clean recovery workflows. 
  • Automated & flexible scheduling: Configure daily or weekly backup policies and trigger on‑demand backups when needed. 
  • Long‑term retention: Store backups for up to 10 years to meet compliance and archival requirements. 
  • Security‑first design: Soft‑delete, immutability, encryption, and multi‑user authorization protect backup data in the vault. 

Scope and availability at GA: 
Vaulted backups can be configured for block blobs in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 accounts. General availability will start with a subset of the regions from Public Preview list. We will continue expanding to additional regions over the coming months.

Body.Content:
Maintaining consistent and secure node configurations in Kubernetes environments can be challenging due to issues like configuration drift, manual changes, and complex upgrade paths. These challenges often lead to unpredictable behavior and increased operational overhead. 

Azure Kubernetes Service now supports Flatcar Container Linux in public preview. Flatcar is built on an immutable filesystem, which helps ensure predictable node behavior by preventing unauthorized changes and simplifying recovery from security incidents. As a Cloud Native Compute Foundation (CNCF) project, Flatcar also supports cross-cloud deployment, making it a strong choice for organizations seeking enhanced security and operational efficiency across diverse environments. 

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Linux OS Guard for AKS

Body.Content:
Cloud-native workloads face increasingly sophisticated threats—from rootkits and container escapes to unauthorized code execution—that demand stronger security guarantees. To address these challenges, Microsoft has introduced Azure Linux with OS Guard, now available in public preview. 

Built on the FedRAMP-certified Azure Linux 3.0 base, OS Guard is a next-generation immutable container host that enforces immutability, code integrity, and mandatory access control. It leverages advanced technologies like dm-verity, SELinux, and Integrity Policy Enforcement (IPE)—recently upstreamed in Linux kernel 6.12—to ensure only trusted binaries from signed sources can run, while locking down user space against tampering. With Trusted Launch enabled by default, OS Guard also secures boot components using measured integrity backed by vTPM keys. 

Azure Linux is the trusted OS powering Microsoft’s own fleet, and OS Guard builds on that foundation to deliver enhanced protection for cloud-native environments. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: DNS flow trace logs for Azure Firewall

Body.Content:
Azure Firewall now supports DNS flow trace logs — a new logging capability that gives you deep, end-to-end visibility into DNS traffic and name resolution paths. This enhancement provides richer telemetry to help you troubleshoot, validate, and secure DNS flows across your network. 

DNS flow trace logs build on existing DNS Proxy functionality by logging critical metadata including query types, response codes, queried domains, upstream DNS servers, and the source and destination IPs of each request. These insights enable faster diagnosis of application connectivity issues, improved auditing, and better security investigations. 

Key highlights                                                                  

  • End-to-end DNS visibility — see each step of DNS resolution across your environment 
  • Faster troubleshooting — pinpoint DNS failures and validate forwarding and custom DNS configuration 
  • Cache insights  -- determine whether the Azure Firewall cache was used for DNS resolution 
Learn more:
  • Read the monitoring data reference documentation.
  • Learn about Azure Firewall Prescaling.

Title: Generally Available: Geo Priority Replication for Azure Blob

Body.Content:
Geo priority replication enhances the replication process for GRS and GZRS storage accounts by enabling accelerated data replication between the primary and secondary regions. This feature is backed by a Service Level Agreement (SLA), ensuring the Last Sync Time for Block Blob data remains at 15 minutes or less, 99.0% of the billing month. With this guaranteed sync time, users can feel more confident about their data’s durability and availability, especially if an unexpected outage occurs in their primary region and a failover is required. 


Geo Priority Replication applies to Block Blob.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Application Gateway for Containers with Web Application Firewall (WAF)

Body.Content:
Announcing Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) support for Azure Application Gateway for Containers is now generally available. Application Gateway for Containers is the next evolution of Application Gateway + Application Gateway Ingress Controller. With the addition of Azure WAF support, Application Gateway for Containers workloads can now protect workloads from web-based attacks like SQL injections, cross-site scripting, protocol anomalies, and more.  

When using WAF to protect your Application Gateway for Containers resources you get access to the Azure-managed Default Rulesets (DRS), providing protection not only from threats identified by the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP), but also additional protections provided by Microsoft’s Threat Intelligence Center (MSTIC). Application Gateway for Containers WAF users also have access to bot protection via bot manager rulesets and protection against DDoS attacks using rate limiting custom rules.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: labels() function in KQL graph semantics

Body.Content:
The labels() function in KQL graph semantics is now generally available. This function enables you to retrieve, filter, and project label information for nodes and edges in your graph queries, making it easier to work with categorized graph data.

The labels() function works with graph models in both Fabric Eventhouse and Azure Data Explorer, allowing you to:
  • Filter graph elements by their labels to focus on specific node or edge types
  • Project label information in query results for better data understanding
  • Use labels with collection functions like any(), all(), and map() for advanced pattern matching
  • Access labels of intermediate nodes in variable-length paths using inner_nodes()

Labels can be either static (fixed labels assigned to node or edge types) or dynamic (labels derived from data properties during graph construction), giving you flexibility in how you organize and query your graph data.
Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Object Replication Metrics

Body.Content:
Blob storage Object Replication metrics for pending operations and pending bytes are now generally available in all regions. These replication metrics will empower you to optimize the performance, troubleshoot replication delays, and maintain high availability across your Object Replication policies. 

The two metrics that will provide deeper visibility and insights into your object replication progress are: 

  • Pending Operations: Tracks the total number of operations pending replication from the source to the destination storage account of your OR policy 

  • Pending Bytes: Tracks the total volume of data pending replication from the source to the destination storage account of your OR policy 

Both metrics are emitted in time buckets (e.g. <5min, 5-10 min, 10-15 min, etc.) which show how long your operations have been pending replication to the destination account.  This assists with quickly identifying delays in the replication pipeline and makes it easier to monitor replication performance.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL read replicas with Premium SSD v2

Body.Content:
You can now configure read replicas (in-region and geo-replicas) with Premium SSD v2 storage tier in Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. Read replicas enable you to scale out read-heavy workloads and improve performance by offloading read operations to replica servers, while write operations continue on the primary. In addition, geo-replicas can serve as read-write failover servers in the event of a disaster, enhancing your business continuity strategy. 

 

Replication is performed asynchronously using the native physical replication technology in PostgreSQL, enabling you to replicate from a primary server to up to five replicas. 

 

With Premium SSD v2, each managed disk delivers up to 80,000 IOPS. When combined with five read replicas, you can achieve up to 480,000 IOPS, helping you meet the demands of your most performance-intensive workloads. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Planned Failover for Azure Storage

Body.Content:
Planned Failover is a customer-managed failover that provides the ability to failover your geo-redundant storage account while keeping geo-redundancy and data durability. You can seamlessly swap the primary and secondary storage endpoints of your geo-redundant account. After the Planned Failover is completed, all new write operations will be directed to the original secondary region, which will serve as the new primary region. Planned Failover can be utilized in a variety of scenarios including disaster recovery drills, partial outages where storage remains healthy or proactive disaster preparation. It is now generally available for GPv2 storage accounts and is compatible with Blob, ADLS Gen2, Table, File, and Queue data.  

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE in Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL Geospatial Queries

Body.Content:
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL now supports ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE for geospatial queries, now generally available. 


With this feature, you can sort query results by their distance from a given point or GeoJSON object directly within Azure Cosmos DB. You no longer need to calculate distances in application code or perform client-side sorting. This function makes it easier to deliver real-time, location-aware experiences for logistics, retail, mapping, and smart-city scenarios with less code and better performance, such as “find the nearest store,” “list drivers by proximity,” or “rank properties by distance.” 


By handling sorting within the database engine, queries become simpler, faster, and more efficient, reducing latency and round-trip overhead. ORDER BY ST_DISTANCE works seamlessly with existing spatial data types and indexing in Azure Cosmos DB, providing consistent performance and accuracy at global scale. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Query Advisor in Azure Cosmos DB

Body.Content:
Azure Cosmos DB for NoSQL includes Query Advisor, now generally available in the .NET SDK. 


Query Advisor helps you write faster, more efficient queries by analyzing your query structure and providing clear, actionable recommendations. It identifies ways that can potentially reduce Request Unit (RU) cost and improve performance. 


As your applications grow, even small changes in query design can have a big impact on scalability and cost. Query Advisor reviews your queries, detects patterns that may cause excessive scans or processing, and suggests improvements, such as optimized filters, more efficient array operations, or simplified subqueries. Each recommendation includes a brief explanation and an example rewrite so you can learn and decide what to apply. 

 

This feature helps developers and database engineers understand how to fine-tune queries for their workloads, achieve better performance, and control RU consumption. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: ExpressRoute resiliency insights

Body.Content:
Resiliency insights is an assessment capability designed to measure your network's reliability for ExpressRoute workloads. At the core of this capability is the resiliency index, a percentage score calculated based on factors such as route resilience, zone-redundant gateway usage, advisory recommendations, and resiliency validation tests. This index evaluates the control plane resiliency of the ExpressRoute connectivity between your Virtual Network Gateway and on-premises network(s). By analysing and improving this index, you can enhance the robustness and reliability of your connectivity to Azure workloads through ExpressRoute.
Learn more.

By proactively testing your network, you can ensure continuous connectivity to Azure workloads and ensure the robustness of your connections. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure HBv5-series VMs

Body.Content:
Azure HBv5-series VM is now generally availalbe in the Azure South Central US region. HBv5 VMs are optimized for memory bandwidth-intensive HPC applications, such as computational fluid dynamics, automotive and aerospace simulations, weather modeling, energy research, molecular dynamics, computer aided engineering, and more. HBv5 VMs feature 6.7 TB/s of memory bandwidth across 450 GB (438 GiB) of memory (HBM) capacity. Also included are 368 4th Generation EPYC™ processor cores with a 3.5 GHz base frequency, 4 GHz boost frequency, and no simultaneous multithreading. HBv5-series VMs also provide 800 Gb/s of InfiniBand from NVIDIA Networking to enable supercomputer-scale MPI workloads, and 15 TiB of local NVMe SSD storage with up to 50 GB/s (reads) and 30 GB/s (writes) of block device performance.

Learn more.

Also included are 368 4th Generation EPYC™ processor cores with a 3.5 GHz base frequency, 4 GHz boost frequency, and no simultaneous multithreading. HBv5-series VMs also provide 800 Gb/s of InfiniBand from NVIDIA Networking to enable supercomputer-scale MPI workloads, and 15 TiB of local NVMe SSD storage with up to 50 GB/s (reads) and 30 GB/s (writes) of block device performance.

Learn more .

Title: Public Preview: Azure Functions zero-downtime deployments with rolling updates in Flex Consumption

Body.Content:
Azure Functions now supports rolling updates in the Flex Consumption plan, delivering zero-downtime deployments with a simple configuration change.  


Instead of forcefully restarting all instances during code or configuration updates, the platform gracefully replaces live instances by draining batches every few seconds while dynamically scaling out the latest version to meet demand. This approach ensures uninterrupted execution and resilient throughput across HTTP, non-HTTP, and Durable workloads—even during intensive scale-out scenarios.  


How to enable: 

  1. Update your ARM/Bicep template with `”properties.functionAppConfig.siteUpdateStrategy.type”` set to `“RollingUpdate”` 

  2. For Durable Functions, configure an orchestration match strategy (see guidance). 

Known limitations: 

  • Scale-out issues may occur with low HTTP concurrency; recommended value is 16. 

  • Real-time rollout monitoring is not supported; allow up to two minutes for completion. 

  • No automatic rollback; intervene by redeploying the last healthy version. 

  • Internal details such as batch size and drain intervals are not configurable and are subject to change. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: High Scale Private Endpoints

Body.Content:
You can now increase Azure Private Endpoint’s virtual network (VNet) limits by upgrading to High Scale Private Endpoints (HSPE). Today local VNet limits are restricted to 1,000 private endpoints per Virtual Network. Any attempts to create additional endpoints will result in an PrivateEndpointsPerVnetLimitReached error that can only be resolved by either deleting existing private endpoints or raising a support request to increase present limits. However, by activating HSPE you will automatically be able to deploy 5,000 PEs in a singular VNet.  

It is also recommended that you only deploy up to 4,000 Private Endpoints in total across your peered virtual networks. Surpassing this recommendation may result in connectivity issues with your private endpoint traffic. If you would like higher limits without the risk of connectivity issues, it is recommended to upgrade to HSPE. This will raise private endpoint cross peering limit to 20,000 endpoints.

Additionally, Azure Virtual Network Manager’s High Scale Private Endpoints support for mesh (connected groups) is now generally available, offering greater scalability for complex Azure network topologies. HSPE for mesh enables you to scale private connectivity across large, interconnected environments with ease.

Regions of Availability:

This feature is available in all public regions.

Learn more:

  • About High Scale Private Endpoints.
  • What is Azure Virtual Network Manager’s Mesh topology?

Title: Retirement: Support for Node.js 20 ends on April 30, 2026 – upgrade your apps to Node.js 22

Body.Content:
In alignment with the end of community support, on April 30, 2026, support for Node.js 20 in Azure Functions will end. Your apps that are hosted on Functions will continue to run, but security updates and performance optimizations will no longer be available and we'll no longer provide customer support for Node.js 20.  

Required action   

To avoid potential security vulnerabilities and take advantage of the latest features, follow the steps to upgrade your Functions apps to Node.js 22 by April 30, 2026 

 

More information 

If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.  

Learn more.

Title: Public Preview: Instant Access Snapshots for Azure Premium SSD v2 and Ultra Disks Storage

Body.Content:
Announcing the Public Preview of Instant Access Snapshots for Premium SSD v2 (Pv2) and Ultra Disks. This new capability enables you to restored new disks immediately after creating snapshots of Pv2 and Ultra disks. Restored disks deliver high performance instantly, while data hydration continues rapidly in the background.  

Common Scenarios 

Instant Access Snapshots accelerate backup and recovery workflows, enabling faster environment refreshes and rapid scaling. Common use cases include:  

  • Create instant backups before software updates and revert quickly if needed.  
  • Quickly scale stateful applications by creating multiple copies of primary data for new instances, such as adding read-only SQL Server replicas. 
  • Rapid nightly refresh of training or testing environments from the production.  

Pricing  

  • Public Preview: No additional charges apply when using Instant Access snapshots. Standard billing for disks and snapshots remains unchanged.  

  • Post General Availability (GA): Two charges will apply:   

      • Storage Charge: Billed only for the additional storage space consumed by Instant Access Snapshots, based on data changes on the source disk after the snapshot is created.   

      • Restore Charge: A one-time fee applies for each disk restored from an Instant Access Snapshot, calculated based on the disk’s provisioned size at the time of restore. 

Get started by creating Instant Access Snapshots for your Premium SSD v2 and Ultra disks here.

Title: Retirement: Remove dependency on these preview features before March 31, 2026

Body.Content:
On March 31, 2026, the following preview features will be retired:  

  • Group multiple steps as a whole to better organize complex pipelines  

  • Compare pipeline jobs to debug failures or unexpected issues  

  • Import data into a data labelling project  

  • Use v2 data asset (uri_folder and mltable) in a data labelling project  

  • Monitor data drift between training and inference  

  • Add linked services  

  • Monitor compute resource  

After March 31, 2026, these preview features will no longer be available.  

To ensure that you do not run into an issue, it is recommended to remove dependency on these features before May 31, 2026.  

Detailed guidance is documented here.

Help and support  

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support case.  

Links provided herein may take you to a third-party website and are provided for convenience only. Third-party websites are subject to the third-party's terms and privacy statements.  

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

Title: Generally Available: Azure WAF CAPTCHA Challenge for Azure Front Door

Body.Content:
Announcing the General Availability of CAPTCHA for Azure Web Application Firewall (WAF) with Azure Front Door.

Modern web applications face evolving threats, including bots, web scrapers, and brute-force attacks, many of which can bypass traditional security controls like IP blocking and rate limiting. CAPTCHA provides an adaptive layer of protection, ensuring legitimate users can access applications while blocking harmful automated traffic. 

This new security feature enhances bot mitigation strategies by introducing an interactive challenge that verifies human users in real time, helping organizations protect their applications from automated attacks. 

Learn more.

Title: Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 25.10 is now available for evaluation

Body.Content:
Azure Sphere OS version 25.10 is now available for evaluation in the Retail Eval feed. The retail evaluation period for this release provides 14 days (about 2 weeks) of testing. During this time, please verify that your applications and devices operate properly with this release before it is deployed broadly to devices in the Retail feed. 

The 25.10 OS Retail Eval release includes quality and underlying build system updates.

Learn more:

  • For more information on Azure Sphere OS feeds and setting up an evaluation device group, see Azure Sphere OS feeds and Set up devices for OS evaluation.
  • For self-help inquiries or technical support, review the Azure Sphere support options.
